least 99% of executed statements must answer inside the deadline, the counts go into the artefact, and zero
statements fails — `0/0` as a share would pass every run that never reached judging. Judging now prints every
200 plans, so the phase that caused this is no longer the only silent one.

**Green.** `pnpm check` — 1,995 tests, 104 files, coverage 99.98 / 99.60 / 100 / 99.98, `sql-exec.ts` at 100
on all four dimensions, `sql-guard.ts` at 100 / 97.87 / 100 / 100. Eleven tests for the guard, four for the
gate. `prereg/R24-dev-split.md` carries Amendment 1: nothing was read, the design is unchanged, and the run
it describes has still never been executed.

**Re-dispatched** as `41245819288` on `5ceee75`, the same inputs, with the judging phase now printing and the
statement deadline in place.

### 133 — 17.60 was never an inflation, and the pack was null in both directions

**The dispatch published thirteen gates and five contrasts in thirty-two minutes.** `41245819288` ran the
registered R24 design on `dev` — 1,534 questions, 5 folds, 6,571 calls, 0 call failures, 16 of 10,160
statements hitting the 20 s deadline (0.16%), 130 results truncated at the row cap (1.28%). The four cells:

| cell | accuracy | n |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | **57.43%** | 881/1534 |
| `none-noevidence` | 39.83% | 611/1534 |
| `full` | 56.84% | 872/1534 |
| `full-noevidence` | 40.55% | 622/1534 |

| contrast | pp | 95% CI | discordant | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| evidence, no pack | **+17.60** | [+15.38, +19.82] | 315/45 | <1e-4 |
| evidence, with pack | **+16.30** | [+14.14, +18.58] | 300/50 | <1e-4 |
| pack, with evidence | +0.59 | [−0.91, +2.09] | 73/64 | 0.4944 |
| pack, no evidence | −0.72 | [−2.15, +0.72] | 60/71 | 0.3824 |
| interaction | −1.30 | [−3.06, +0.46] | 86 up / 105 down / 1343 flat | — |

**Two of six predictions held, and the two that failed are worth more than the ones that passed.** The main
effect cleared its 8pp bar at 17.60 with an interval 2.14pp wide, half of what minidev could produce. But the
interval **[+15.38, +19.82] excludes 24.86** — and so does the registered explanation for that exclusion,
because the registration said an exclusion would mean minidev inflates the effect by dropping the simple
third. **Restricted to the mixture minidev actually keeps — moderate and challenging, n = 609 — the same
dispatch gives +22.99pp [+19.21, +26.77], which contains 24.86.** The gap between 24.86 and 17.60 is
**composition, not inflation**: 60% of dev is `simple`, where the sentence is worth 14.05pp, and minidev
contains none of it. Both numbers are now correct and they answer different questions — 22.99 for
moderate-and-challenging questions, **17.60 for the whole split and for any cross-system comparison**.

**The pack is null in both conditions, and that retires a mechanism.** Prediction 3 asked for
`full-noevidence − none-noevidence ≥ 2pp` and measured **−0.72pp [−2.15, +0.72]**: the +1.14pp cell that
reversed this record's conclusion in R23 does not replicate on 4.4× the sample. With the hint it is +0.59pp.
Neither interval excludes zero and neither reaches the 2.14pp the design can detect. Twenty-three iterations
have now varied the pack along eight axes; this is the first that measured it with an instrument able to
resolve 2pp **and** with the competitor both present and removed. **The honest statement is that the pack is
zero, not that it pays.**

**The interaction that motivated R25 did not replicate, and its own clause fired.** −1.30pp [−3.06, +0.46]
against R23's −6.00pp [−10.57, −1.71], on the split the competitors used, same four cells. The registered
refutation clause reads: *"an interaction whose interval contains zero demotes the competition reading from a
mechanism to a single-run observation."* It fired. **The reason to ask whether a value index could substitute
for the hint was that the pack was losing a competition, and on the larger panel it is not in one** — so the
line goes to selection work, not to the database.

**The difficulty story held, and it is the first time its shape was testable.** `simple` n=925 **+14.05pp**
[+11.24, +16.86], `moderate` n=464 **+22.63pp** [+18.32, +27.16], `challenging` n=145 **+24.14pp**
[+15.86, +32.41]. Monotone, and both ends inside their registered bands (5–15, 18–30). The simple-to-moderate
step is **+8.58pp ± 5.24**, resolved; moderate-to-challenging is **+1.51pp ± 9.38**, not resolved, so the
gradient's top end stays open. Prediction 6 held at 57.43% for `none`: the environment did not move.

**Store variance, for the ninth time.** The evidence effect per fold runs **14.98 to 21.50pp** and the pack's
runs **−2.28 to +3.26pp** across five stores rebuilt from the same corrections — the ±1.7pp band AUDIT 17.6
recorded, and the reason every claim here is within-dispatch. Cross-dispatch comparisons on this lane carry
one to two points of store variance, which is why R23's −6.00 and R24's −1.30 cannot be reconciled by
subtracting them.

**The instrument is what made the run exist.** `V48-statements-answered` read 16 of 10,160 (0.16%). Without
the deadline there is no R24: the previous dispatch spent 118 minutes inside one fold's judging phase and
published nothing. The gate is the difference between "the lane is slow" and "the lane is describing its own
timeout" being a number in the artefact.

**A second defect, found by the gate that re-derives instead of quoting.** The dispatch wrote the dev artefact's
canonical path, because the lane named its file after the *split* and there used to be one design per split. R24
is the second design on `dev`: the file at that address is R8.3b's, the run `eval:protocol` recomputes the
`reproduced` cell from, and copying R24's artefact in replaced it. Nothing failed at the write — the new file is
a valid artefact of the same lane over the same 1,534 questions, with a rebuilt store and `none` at 57.43%
instead of 57.63% — and `pnpm check` said so in one line: *the recorded comparison differs from the arithmetic
(indicative at 0.19pp, reproduced at 3.91pp)*. R8.3b's artefact is restored, R24's is committed under its own
name, and the lane now names a file after the design as well as the split (`artefactWriteIdOf`, five tests, the
same rule spelled once at workflow level so a dispatch's write path and its upload path cannot disagree).

**Green.** `pnpm check` — 2,000 tests, 105 files, four dimensions 99.98 / 99.60 / 100 / 99.98, `artefacts.ts`
at 100 in all four after the naming rule. The artefact is
committed at `eval/results/poc-sota-bird-dev-R24-dev-split.json`; `prereg/R24-dev-split.md` carries the Outcome
section with all five contrasts, the six prediction verdicts, the composition decomposition and the per-fold
spread.

### 134 — The dose was selection, and the instrument ran out before the pack did

**The dispatch published fourteen gates and eight contrasts in thirty-three minutes.** `41256898122` ran
R25 on `dev` — 1,534 questions, 5 folds, 9,096 calls, 0 call failures, 18 of 12,774 statements hitting the
20 s deadline (0.14%), 172 truncated at the row cap (1.35%). R24 left one live mechanism and this run was
built to kill or confirm it, so it needed a control the record had never had: an arm that gets **one item**
from the store's own order, so that the admission decision can be separated from the truncation it implies.
Four arms, where every previous design had two:

| arm | what it is | accuracy | n | rules/question |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `none` | no injection | 57.17% | 877/1534 | — |
| `full` | the store's own order, budget 4 | 57.11% | 876/1534 | 1.74 |
| `full-one` | the same order, truncated to its first item | 56.78% | 871/1534 | 1.00 |
| `full-accepted` | one item, and only on questions that admit it | **57.63%** | 884/1534 | 0.67 |

| contrast | pp | 95% CI | discordant | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `full-one` − `full` | **−0.33** | [−1.56, +0.85] | 42/47 | 0.6718 |
| `full-one` − `none` | −0.39 | [−1.76, +0.91] | 52/58 | 0.6338 |
| `full` − `none` | −0.07 | [−1.50, +1.30] | 60/61 | 1.0000 |
| `full-accepted` − `full-one` | **+0.85** | [−0.13, +1.83] | 35/22 | 0.1112 |
| `full-accepted` − `none` | +0.46 | [−0.78, +1.69] | 52/45 | 0.5426 |
| `full-accepted` − `full` | +0.52 | [−0.85, +1.83] | 58/50 | 0.5008 |

**The dose gap was selection, and truncating every question costs nothing.** `full-one − full` is
**−0.33pp [−1.56, +0.85]**. The store had been reporting a dose effect since R24 — questions that received
two items scored 4.13pp above questions that received one in R24's store, and 3.12pp in this one (dose-1
n=401 **+2.24pp**, dose-2 n=1,133 **−0.88pp**) — and it does not survive being made causal. **The store gave
its second item to the questions it had more to say about, and those were the questions where a note of
either length was worth more.** Two of the six registered predictions were staked on the opposite and both
are refuted: one note on its own is −0.39pp against nothing, not the +2pp the dose table implied.

**Per-question admission is the only arm in twenty-five iterations to point up, and it does not get there.**
`full-accepted − full-one` is **+0.85pp [−0.13, +1.83], 35 gained against 22 lost, p = 0.1112**. That is the
largest positive point estimate any pack arm has produced and the tightest interval against harm — the lower
bound excludes any loss larger than 0.13pp — and it still contains zero, which is what the registration said
would happen. The decision it encodes is not decorative: 1,027 of 1,534 questions were admitted (66.9%),
population 0.67 rules per question against `full`'s 1.74, and the gate that checks it (`V50`) read
`fitted` on all five folds with floors between 0.111 and 0.200, keeping 51–84% of each fold's
decisive-bearing learning rows.

**The run contained its own test–retest, for free.** Of the 507 questions refused the note, 507 received a
**byte-identical prompt** to `none` — and they moved **4 gained and 3 lost against `none`**. That is the
endpoint's own noise floor measured inside the dispatch, at **1.4% of 507**, matching the 1.4–2.6% band the
`none-replica` arms established in R17. Any effect below that is not visible on this lane, whatever its
p-value, and the admission arm's +0.85pp is only 3.4pp of gross movement against a floor that produces 1.4%
of the population for nothing.

**The registered refutation clause fired.** It reads: *"If `full-one − full` and `full-one − none` both have
intervals containing zero, the pack line is closed at every budget … the honest record is that the mechanism
is inert rather than mis-sized."* Both intervals contain zero, the first by 0.85pp of headroom and the second
by 0.91pp. **The pack line is closed.** The product decision that follows is not a smaller pack — it is no
pack before the question, which is what iteration 90 already shipped on weaker evidence and what this run
now puts a dev-scale interval around.

**Why nothing further can be measured here, in two numbers.** `V5-resolution` reads a minimum detectable
effect of **2.01pp** on this split. Two oracles computed on R24's artefact with the answer key in hand price
the entire remaining pack upside at **+2.35pp** (drop every net-harmful item) and **+4.17pp** (keep the pack
exactly where it helped). Every arm in this run lands inside **±1pp**. **An effect a perfect oracle prices at
2.35pp cannot be resolved by an instrument that needs 2.01pp to see anything**, and the split has no more
questions to buy resolution with. That is a statement about the instrument, not about the mechanism, and it
is the reason the next design cannot be another pack arm on BIRD dev.

**What held.** `full − none` at −0.07pp [−1.50, +1.30] reproduces R24's −0.59pp inside one interval, so the
anchor is stable across two stores built from different learning passes. `V49-dose-truncated` and
`V50-admission-engaged` both passed on their first run: 1,133 of 1,534 prompts (73.9%) differ from `full` and
**0 exceeded one item**, which is the check that makes `full-one` a dose control rather than a second copy of
`full`. Per fold, `full-accepted − full-one` ran **−0.33, +3.26, −1.30, +0.98, +1.63** and `full-one − full`
ran **0.00, −1.30, +1.30, −1.63, 0.00** — the second is a coin, which is what a refuted mechanism looks like
fold by fold. The admission effect is concentrated where the note is on the question: `moderate` **+2.16pp**
(13/3), `simple` **+0.65pp**, `challenging` **−2.07pp** (0/3 aggregate, three discordant questions). At 145
challenging questions that is a shape, not a result.

**Two defects in the new tools, both caught by their own first real use.** `admissionFloor` computed its
minimum population as `Math.ceil(Math.max(1, policy.minKept) * total)` — the share clamped to 1 instead of
1% — so every fold returned the lowest threshold that kept at least everybody, and `full-accepted` would
have silently degenerated into `full-one`. **The function's own tests failed on their first run with
`expected 0.5 / 0.9 to be …`**, which is the entire argument for writing them before the dispatch. Separately,
`parseContrastArgs` accepted `--left a --right b` by failing on the second flag: the single-value parser had
only ever been called once per arm, and the first call that passed two flags threw `unknown flag`. The
off-by-one in the arithmetic would have cost a 33-minute dispatch; the parser would have cost one command.

**Green.** `pnpm check` — 2,044 tests, 107 files, 99.98 / 99.61 / 100 / 99.98, with `dose.ts`,
`arm-contrast.ts`, `artefacts.ts` and `sota.ts` at 100 on all four dimensions. Committed:
`eval/results/poc-sota-bird-dev-R25-dose-and-admission.json`, `eval/results/poc-arm-contrast.json` (the
registered contrasts, re-derivable from the repository by `pnpm eval:arm-contrast`), and
`prereg/R25-dose-and-admission.md` with the Outcome section and all six prediction verdicts.

### 135 — Pruning the schema costs nine points, and the value index is closed on its largest sample

**Two arms that change what the model knows, measured on 1,534 questions for the first time.** `41264432646`,
28 minutes, 6,504 calls, 0 call failures, 13 gates pass, 14 of 10,135 statements at the 20 s deadline (0.14%),
126 truncated (1.24%), `V5` minimum detectable **2.07pp**. Four arms: the control, the pack as the anchor, and
the two channels this record had only ever measured on 350 questions with 12/11 and 7/33 discordant pairs.

| arm | accuracy | n | delta vs `none` | 95% CI | discordant | p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `none` | 57.43% | 881/1534 | — | — | — | — |
| `full` | 57.76% | 886/1534 | +0.33 | [−1.11, +1.76] | 67/62 | 0.7249 |
| `values` | **58.60%** | 899/1534 | **+1.17** | [−0.13, +2.48] | 64/46 | 0.1046 |
| `linked` | **48.17%** | 739/1534 | **−9.26** | [−10.95, −7.63] | 24/166 | <1e-4 |

**The pruner is not a missing feature, it is an active harm.** −9.26pp [−10.95, −7.63] is 4.5 times the
split's floor and the largest single-arm effect this record has measured in either direction. R21's −7.43pp
was real; it also *understated*: at 4.4× the sample the harm grew. Restricting the DDL to the tables the
question names deletes the table the evidence points at, and the decomposition says so: `simple` −10.2pp
(61.8% → 51.6%), `moderate` −8.4pp (50.9% → 42.5%), `challenging` −5.5pp (50.3% → 44.8%) — the harm shrinks as
the questions get harder, which is what deleting schema the question needs looks like on easy questions. **The baseline
this lane has been running since iteration 1, the whole DDL, was the right prompt**, and the competitor
ablations that price schema linking at 12.71pp are measuring a system that *starts* from a pruned schema and
therefore has something to lose by pruning it further. We start where they end.

**The value index is closed at the largest sample this benchmark offers, and it goes out positive.** +1.17pp,
64 gained against 46 lost, p = 0.10 — the largest positive prompt-side estimate in twenty-six iterations — and
the registered clause fires anyway, because it was written on the interval: *"an interval containing zero with a
half-width of at most 1.6pp closes the value channel as a prompt annotation."* The interval is [−0.13, +2.48]:
it contains zero and its half-width is 1.31pp. **The clause fires and the channel closes.** What that settles
is the record's last local explanation for its own 24.86pp gap: the difference to XiYan and CHASE is not the
column values in the prompt, because adding them is indistinguishable from zero here, and it is not the
pruning, because pruning is nine points *down*.

**The anchor held for the third store, and the pack's number moved for the ninth time.** `full − none` is
+0.33pp [−1.11, +1.76] where R24 and R25 read −0.07 and −0.07 — all three inside one interval of each other,
which is what an anchor is for. The pilot on 350 questions read `full` at **−4.00pp**, and at 1,534 the same
store reads +0.33: the ninth instance of a minidev pack reading that does not survive the split, and the reason
every claim in this record is within-dispatch.

**The gate this iteration added was proven before the registered run, not after it.** `V51-channel-applied`
exists because a channel arm that rewrote nothing is the control wearing the channel's name, and this record
has published a channel result without checking which of the two it had. The pilot read `values` 100.0% /
`linked` 34.9% and the dev run 100.0% / 36.4% — inside the registered 1–40% band, and 100% for the annotator
because annotation is unconditional. **Had the pruner fired on nothing, its −9.26pp would have been `full`'s
+0.33pp** and the record would have published "pruning is inert" as a finding.

**Green.** `pnpm check` — 2,050 tests, 107 files, 99.98 / 99.61 / 100 / 99.98, `sota.ts` at 100 on all four
dimensions after six new gate tests. Both artefacts are committed (`poc-sota-bird-dev-R26-channels.json` and the pilot
`poc-sota-bird-R26-channels.json`), and `pnpm eval:protocol` re-derives both against `prereg/R26-channels.md`
and its thirteen declared gates.

### 136 — The competitor was a control, and the "general" protocol has one user

**This entry is an architecture audit, not a run.** No dispatch, no model call, no new number: it re-reads the
repository against the claim the repository makes about itself, because the claim and the code had drifted and
the drift had been shaping which experiments got designed.

**The category error, fixed first because everything else followed from it.** Twenty-six iterations have been
designed against systems listed in `COMPETITIVE.md`, and that file never said what "competitor" meant. It now
does (§0): a **product competitor** builds the artefact we would ship and is comparable only on EX; a
**same-unit control** published one manipulation we also performed and is comparable only on Δpp; a
**methodology peer** is comparable only on whether a claim is admissible. **RSL-SQL sits in the second row and
had been read as the first.** Its 12.71pp schema-linking ablation is the same quantity as our 17.60pp evidence
ablation on the same 1,534 questions; its leaderboard row is not comparable to our EX at all, because the two
differ in the generator's training, the candidate pool and the schema form simultaneously. The correction is
not cosmetic: a competitor's number says where to spend engineering on the product, a control's number says
which of *our own* components is mispriced, and three of this file's past misreadings came from running the
second kind of comparison through the first kind of question.

**The product consequence is larger than the table.** None of the first-row systems is an alternative to this
project, because this project ships no text-to-SQL system: it ships a library that turns a host's corrections
into scoped knowledge, and text-to-SQL is one host — `nl2charts` is the one in the README, τ²-bench is the one
with a second harness. The XiYan/CHASE row is therefore a **host that could embed us**, and the honest
competitive question about it is not "do we beat 71.58 EX" but "would its pipeline improve if our pack were
injected", which R26 answered for the two prompt-side channels and which is not a leaderboard position.

**What the coupling audit found, in lines.** The claim under test was that the library had been absorbed into
one application scenario. It has not been, at the level that matters:

| layer | lines | scenario words in production code | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `core` | 7,074 | **0** — every hit is in `__tests__` (`task: 'sql.generate'` is a free-form scope string) | clean |
| `eval` measurement protocol / statistics | 19,125 (60.4%) | none | general in name |
| `eval` `sota-bird.ts` lane | 6,635 (21.0%) | all text-to-SQL | scenario |
| `eval` `sota.ts` | 3,090 (9.8%) | 31 gates + `PROMPT_VERSION='sql-prompt/3'` + `extractSql` + `SqlArm` | **mixed, not separated** |
| `eval` eight SQL modules | 2,039 (6.4%) | all text-to-SQL | scenario |
| `eval` τ²/l4 second scenario | 754 (2.4%) | tool calling | scenario |

**11,764 lines, 37.2%, are text-to-SQL, and none of them are in `core`.** The library is genuinely
scenario-agnostic: its subpath exports let a host take `core/apply` and `core/memory` without the distiller, and
two hosts already embed it (`node` 1,312 lines, `browser` 301).

**The coupling is in the reuse table, not the line count.** The measurement layer only looks general because
it has one customer:

| check | reading |
|---|---|
| call sites of `buildValidityGates` (31 gates) | **`sota-bird.ts` only** |
| gates the τ²-bench lane uses | **3, written beside it**: `l4-paired` (delta ≥ 0), `l4-resolution` (half-width ≤ 5pp), `l4-same-split` |
| that lane's `l4-resolution` verdict | **failed — 14.98pp half-width against a 5pp bar, at n = 68** |

**So the second scenario never used the protocol; it wrote a weaker one and one of its three gates failed.** The
31 gates were invented by, tuned by and validated against a single benchmark, and the only evidence that they
are a protocol rather than a habit is that a second lane would have reused them. It did not. The failure was
recorded as a note in `poc-l4-pair.json` rather than as a verdict, which is the second half of the defect: a
non-blocking gate that fails and is narrated is a gate that does not exist.

**The sub-package answer, and why the obvious split is wrong.** Isolating SQL into `microglia-sql` would
produce a repository whose *product* is general and whose *measurements* are scenario-specific — which is
exactly the shape that makes the generality untestable. The split that buys something is between **protocol and
adapter**, cut on one rule: *does the function signature mention a scenario type?* Gates, paired statistics,
artefact validation, pre-registration and the arm contract do not; `sql-exec`, `schema-link`, `m-schema`,
`value-samples`, `bird-data` and the SQL half of `sota.ts` do. The target graph is `core ← protocol ←
eval-sql / eval-tau2`, with the adapter contract (`LaneAdapter`: load / prompt / parse / score / strata) as the
seam, and §17.64 carries the design.

**"A general flywheel" is not too ambitious; "general" was being asserted at the wrong level.** Three claims
have to be separated and only the first is currently true: **architecture-general** (yes — 7,074 lines, zero
scenario words, two hosts embedded), **mechanism-general** (no — scenario 1 is 26 iterations with one +1.17pp
point that its own clause closed, scenario 2 is n = 68 with a 15pp half-width), **commercially-general** (not
touched — no scenario has produced a deliverable effect). And the sharpest version of the objection comes from
our own data: **SQL generation is the most favourable terrain this theory has** — a correction is executable, a
rule is testable, transfer is measurable, the schema is stable — and here it produced 1.17pp. A weaker
scenario should be expected to produce less, not more. That is an argument for demoting the claim from
assertion to hypothesis and for making the **next experiment a test of generality** rather than another SQL
ablation, which is what R27 is.

**What this entry changes about the queue.** The previous plan put R27 on the candidate pool because CHASE's
13.95pp pool headroom is the largest unpriced gap in the file. That stands, but it is now second: the first
question worth buying is whether the protocol layer is a protocol, and it can be answered by running the second
scenario through the first scenario's gates — no new dataset, no new model, one dispatch. **An architecture that
cannot be shown to be general from the outside is not general; it is a single application with good module
hygiene.**

### 137 — The protocol is a package, and the estimate that produced its scope was wrong by fifteen gates

**R27 stage 1 is closed.** `packages/protocol` exists, holds all 39 validity gates, the 39-id publication order
as data, the `LaneAdapter` contract and the transfer reconciliation, and has **no runtime dependency**: it
cannot name a scenario even if someone wanted it to. `sota.ts` keeps `buildValidityGates` as its named entry
point and delegates; the lane is otherwise unchanged.

| what moved | lines | where it lives now |
|---|---|---|
| `FrameDelivery`, `EvidenceDelivery`, `ValidityGate` | 31 | `protocol/src/gates.ts` |
| `ProtocolGateInput` (the required fields) + `ScenarioGateInput` (2 optional) | 300 | `protocol/src/gates.ts` |
| the 31 gates, the transfer helper and its 8 ids | 510 | `protocol/src/gates.ts` |
| `GATE_ORDER` + `inGateOrder` | 55 | `protocol/src/gates.ts` |
| `LaneAdapter`, `mergeGates`, `blockingFailure` | 145 | `protocol/src/adapter.ts` |
| `SUBSTRATE_FLOOR`, `NET_PUBLISHED_STEP` | 8 | `protocol/src/gates.ts` (re-exported by `probe-pair`) |

**The scoping estimate in §136 was 22 gates on the protocol side and 9 on the adapter's, and it was wrong by
fifteen.** The first pass read gate *names*: `parse-rate` sounded like a parser's gate, `pool-complete` like a
candidate pool's, `channel` like a schema channel's. Re-deriving the split from the `input.*` fields each gate
actually reads gave **29 of 31**, and counting the eight transfer ids — passed *into* `transferGates` as
arguments rather than written beside an object literal, so a scan for `id:` misses them entirely — gave **39
gates, 37 of which depend on nothing scenario-specific**. The two that do (`V4`, `V10`) read an *optional* field
and are **absent** rather than green when a lane cannot supply it.

**The wrong number stays in the record on purpose.** A name-based cut would have parked nine gates in the adapter
that had no scenario in them, which is the fork this design exists to prevent; the estimate was produced by
intuition and the correction by measurement, and the second is the only part worth reusing.

**Two real defects were found while moving, and neither was the one being looked for.**

1. **`V51` passed a channel that never fired, if its floor was zero.** The gate read `share >= floor`, and a
   floor of `0` makes `0/100` pass — so a lane could declare "I do not care how often this happens" and buy a
   green tick for a manipulation that never occurred, which is the exact failure the gate was built to catch.
   `applied > 0` is now an invariant of the gate rather than a consequence of a floor: the floor answers *how
   often must this happen*, and zero is not an answer to that question. No published artefact changed.
2. **`typecheck:lanes` was not running under `--strict`.** The library compiles under the full `tsconfig.base`
   (`exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`); the six CLI lanes were checked by a command line
   with neither. Turning `--strict` on surfaced **four real defects** in code that had passed every run since it
   was written: `relevanceFor` and `reconcile` accepted the `none` arm and indexed a `Partial<Record<…>>` that
   has no such key, and `scale.ts` wrote `intent: string | undefined` into a `KnowledgeScope` whose optional
   field does not admit an explicit `undefined`. All four fixed by narrowing the parameter to
   `Exclude<ArmName, 'none'>` and by conditional spreads; the gate is now as strict as the library.

**The regression is the point, and it is unusually strong for a move this size.** `pnpm eval:protocol` re-derives
every one of the **31 committed artefacts** — thirteen pre-registrations, their declared gate lists in both
directions, and the cell comparisons — and it passed on the first run after the extraction. Byte identity was
preserved through two structural changes that could have broken it: `V4` moved out of the array literal into a
conditional push (the publication order is now explicit data, which is what keeps it in fourth position), and
`V51`'s floors moved out of the gate into the entries (each entry carries its own `floor` and `expects`, so the
gate never learns a channel's name and the published sentence still reads *"values at least 95% of prompts,
linked at least 1%"*).

**Green.** `pnpm check` — typecheck, `typecheck:lanes` under `--strict`, 2,090 tests over 109 files, four
coverage dimensions at **99.98 / 99.61 / 100 / 99.98**, with `protocol/src` and `sota.ts` both at **100 on all
four**; `audit:repo`, six offline lanes, `eval:protocol` and `bench` (blocking gates PASS) all green.

### 138 — Four gates fire, two of them vacuously, and the protocol has never said no

**R27 stage 2 is closed, and it refuted its own registration.** The stage was specified as "make the τ² lane
implement `LaneAdapter` and replace its three bespoke gates with the thirty-nine", with four predictions written
down in advance. The predictions were the point: a stage that could not fail would have been a refactor. What
happened is that three of the four held in a way that closes one question, and the first one fell by a margin
large enough to close a different one.

| # | registered prediction | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | at least **15** of the 39 gates are evaluable on τ² without a signature change | **refuted: 4 fired, 2 of them vacuous, 9 is the lane's ceiling** |
| 2 | `l4-resolution` becomes blocking and the run fails it | **held**, through `V5-resolution` rather than through a τ² copy of it |
| 3 | no gate changes its threshold | **held** — 6pp stayed 6pp; the τ² lane's own 5pp bar was replaced by it, a disclosed 1pp loosening that both fail at 15pp |
| 4 | the τ² effect does not move by more than 1pp | **held at 0.00pp**: 1.4706pp before, 1.4706pp after, same interval, same p |

**The measurement, as three buckets rather than one number.** The stage produced an **arm index**
(`packages/eval/src/tau2-gates.ts`) that accounts for all 39 ids in both directions — a test holds
`supplyable ∪ armIndexed = GATE_ORDER` exactly — because a single count would have hidden the finding inside the
number:

| bucket | count | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **supplyable** | **9** | the lane's record type can carry the enabling field |
| ↳ informative on the committed record | **2** | `V3-parse-rate` (100%), `V5-resolution` (fails at 21.41pp) |
| ↳ vacuous | **2** | `V6`, `V7` — they fire, pass, and certify nothing |
| ↳ unrecorded | **5** | `V1`, `V2`, `V8`, `V32`, `V44`: the driver never wrote the field down |
| **arm-indexed** | **30** | the field exists, but only an arm τ² never ran produces it |

**Why prediction 1 mattered more than a count.** Stage 1 counted portability by asking each gate's signature one
question — *does it mention a scenario type?* — and got 37 of 39, from which the claim "a second scenario is
measured without editing a gate" was written. Stage 2 shows the question was about the wrong noun. A signature
being scenario-free does not make a gate **evaluable**: `V45-clearance-dose-matched` names no scenario type at
all and is unreachable for a lane that ran no clearance arm. **Portability is indexical — a gate is as portable as
the arm behind it —** and the honest statement is narrower and more useful than the one it replaces: the
*apparatus* is scenario-agnostic (τ² is scored by the same function, the same publication order and the same
artefact schema with zero edits to a gate), while the *gate set* is a catalogue of validity conditions of which
each lane instantiates the subset its arms support. The thirty absences are not a failure list; they are the
conformance checklist the second scenario was worth buying, and every entry names the experiment that would make
its gate fire.

**The defect the stage did find is a type, and it cost the lane its entire report.** `ProtocolGateInput` made
eight fields mandatory. Two of them — `meanPackIds` and the call tally — are knowable only to a lane whose model
runs in this process; τ²'s agent is a Python program on the other side of a facade, and the calls are its. A lane
that could not state those two **could not call `buildProtocolGates` at all**, so the four gates it *could* prove
were never evaluated. The instrument was all-or-nothing: one unstated fact and the whole report is withheld, which
is the opposite of the rule this package already applied to its scenario half — *a gate that cannot fire is
absent rather than green*. All eight fields are optional now, and the second scenario fires four gates where it
fired none.

**Two gates had never certified anything, and the record shows it.** `V6-controls-inject` evaluates `every` over
the list of pack-based control arms; with that list empty the predicate is vacuously true. Across the seventeen
published BIRD artefacts it carries the sentence *"no pack-based controls configured"* **seventeen times**, and
`V7-channel` carries *"no channel control was run"* sixteen times (the seventeenth is the oracle control at
29.71pp). They are kept rather than deleted — the sentence is a true statement about the run, and removing it
would rewrite seventeen committed files — but every count in this entry separates them from the gates that read a
measurement, because a report that said "four gates" where two do work would be the same overstatement the stage
was called to correct.

**The number that is larger than all of the above: the protocol has never said no.** Across the seventeen
committed BIRD artefacts, **34 distinct gate ids**, every gate that is carried **passes**, without exception. The
valued range of `V5-resolution` over that record is 1.96pp to 4.87pp against a 6pp bar, so the one flag that
could have stopped a run was never in a position to. The first red verdicts in the entire published record are
the two this stage produced — `V5-resolution` and `l4-paired`, both blocking — and they arrived the moment a
second scenario was measured rather than a second iteration of the first. **A validity suite whose published
output has only ever been green is not a gate; it is a form**, and the way to tell the difference is to point it
at a run that should fail. That is what the τ² re-scoring is.

**`V5-resolution` is blocking because it was measured, not because it was decided.** Seventeen artefacts pass it;
the run that fails it can resolve a 21.41pp difference at 80% power against a 6pp bar, and it published a 1.47pp
delta anyway. The flag was carried from a period when a run could not estimate its own minimum detectable
difference, and it had never been exercised since — a gate whose only failure case is the case it exists for is a
gate that is recorded rather than enforced. The stage also put the two statistics side by side, because they are
not the same number and the record has been quoting one of them: the **95% half-width** is `1.96·SE` = 14.98pp,
the **minimum detectable difference** is `2.802·SE` = 21.41pp, and the ratio is 1.43. Both are in the artefact;
the gate reads the one its own criterion names.

**A third finding, about the contract rather than about the gates.** `LaneAdapter` reads as though a lane sees
the model's raw reply. τ²'s does not: the agent runs in another process and the evaluator hands back a verdict
with a decomposition. So `parse` parses **the receipt** and `score` reads the verdict out of it. That is not a
workaround — no gate inspects a candidate's shape, only its outcome — but it does narrow what the contract's
prose claimed, and the narrowing is recorded in `lanes/tau2.ts` beside the three functions it applies to. The
consequence for the roadmap is concrete: `V46-raw-is-verbatim` and `V47-evidence-ablated` need a transcript-level
manipulation, which means the τ² driver would have to receive the events rather than a verdict, and that is a
driver change rather than a gate.

**Refutation applied.** The registered consequence of falling below fifteen was that the generality claim is
**withdrawn from the positioning text rather than qualified**. It is withdrawn: `COMPETITIVE.md` §0 and the
README paragraph now say what was measured — apparatus agnostic, gate set arm-indexed — and neither says "a
second scenario is measured by the same gates" any more. The stronger, chequeable version replaces it, and it is
the version the code can be read against.

**Green.** `pnpm check` — typecheck, `typecheck:lanes` under `--strict`, **2,142 tests over 110 files**, four
coverage dimensions at **99.98 / 99.62 / 100 / 99.98** with `tau2.ts`, `tau2-gates.ts` and `protocol/src` all at
**100 on all four**; `audit:repo`, six offline lanes, `eval:protocol` (13 pre-registrations, 10 gate-list
agreements, 2 cell recomputations), `bench` (blocking gates PASS) and `bundle:size` all green. No published
artefact changed except `poc-l4-pair.json`, which is the measurement.

**The lane is red on purpose, and CI asserts that it is red for the right reason.** The τ² conformance step reads
the committed arms, reproduces `1.4706pp`, fires `V5-resolution` at 21.41pp against a 6pp bar, and requires the
process to exit non-zero — then checks the audit's shape: four fired, two vacuous, thirty-five absent, nine
supplyable, thirty arm-indexed. A green step here would mean the protocol had been tuned to pass, which is the
failure the registration was written to catch.

### 139 — Every published delta put beside the difference its own sample could resolve

**This round ran two measurements and neither of them is a new model call.** The first is R28, the stratification
that was registered last round. The second is an audit the project has never run on itself: for each of the
seventeen artefacts that carries a paired per-question comparison, its delta beside the smallest difference that
artefact's own sample could have detected. The second was not planned. It was computed because the first could not
be read without it.

**R28 is refuted, in sign, and the refutation is not a near miss.**

| bucket | questions | helped / harmed | delta | 95% half-width | minimum detectable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[0, 0.2)` | 725 | 27 / 27 | **+0.00pp** | ±1.99 | 2.84 |
| `[0.2, 0.4)` | 670 | 28 / 30 | **−0.30pp** | ±2.23 | 3.18 |
| `[0.4, 0.6)` | 121 | 11 / 2 | **+7.44pp** | ±5.84 | 8.35 |
| `[0.6, 1]` | 18 | 1 / 3 | **−11.11pp** | ±21.78 | 31.13 |

MEMTRIM (arXiv 2610.07311) predicts that harm concentrates at *intermediate* overlap and is small at both ends.
The minimum here is at the **top** bucket, the maximum is in the middle, and the whole shape is worth 18.55pp
against a minimum detectable difference of **32.23pp**. `S1` fails (the minimum is at an end bucket), `S3` fails
(two buckets are thin — the top one holds 18 questions and 4 discordant pairs), the difficulty control `S2` fails
because the `moderate` band puts its minimum at the bottom, and `S4` fails because the ordering moves when the
tokeniser does: `3 < 1 < 0 < 2` under words, `0 < 1 < 3 < 2` under character 4-grams.

**The registered criteria were missing a power floor, and running them is what showed it.** As written, `S2` lets
a three-question cell decide whether a difficulty band keeps its minimum in the middle — a coin flip wearing the
costume of a control. And nothing in the four criteria asked whether the minimum is far enough below its
neighbours to *be* a minimum. `S5` is that check, added as a disclosed amendment rather than slipped in: **a gap
is only a gap if it exceeds its own resolution**, and this one does not. The same amendment applies a floor of ten
discordant pairs to `S2`, which turns `challenging` into an honest *undecided* rather than an accidental
agreement. Neither amendment changes a number; both change what the number is allowed to be called.

**The stratification's real yield is what it eliminates.** For 90.9% of the corpus — the 1,395 questions whose
best rule shares under 40% of their content terms — the overlap explains nothing: +0.00pp and −0.30pp, on buckets
that carry ±2pp intervals. The remaining 9% is where any signal would have to be, and it holds 139 questions
between them. **Relevance, measured lexically at the question level, is not the axis on which this memory helps or
hurts.** That is now the second such measurement: the embedding probe of §62 found that hurt rules and helped rules are
*not* separated by cosine similarity either (0.254 against 0.226, p = 0.12), and in the opposite direction from
the lexical bucket reading here. **Two covariates, two different signs, neither resolvable** — which is a stronger
statement than either alone: whatever makes a rule help or hurt, it is not how similar the rule is to the question.

**Then the audit, which is the reason this round matters more than its own null.**

| the record, sorted by resolution | n | helped / harmed | delta | 95% half-width | minimum detectable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `poc-sota-bird-dev.json` | 1,534 | 47 / 68 | −1.37pp | ±1.37 | **1.96** |
| `poc-sota-bird-dev-R25-dose-and-admission.json` | 1,534 | 60 / 61 | −0.07pp | ±1.41 | 2.01 |
| `poc-sota-bird-dev-R26-channels.json` | 1,534 | 67 / 62 | +0.33pp | ±1.45 | 2.07 |
| `poc-sota-bird-dev-R24-dev-split.json` | 1,534 | 64 / 73 | −0.59pp | ±1.50 | 2.14 |
| `poc-sota-bird-anchor.json` | 350 | 10 / 12 | −0.57pp | ±2.63 | 3.76 |
| …eight more at n = 350… | 350 | — | −2.00 to −4.29pp | ±2.80 to ±3.17 | 4.00 to 4.53 |
| `poc-sota-bird-transfer.json` | 350 | 8 / 24 | **−4.57pp** | ±3.17 | 4.53 — **the only resolvable row** |

**One of seventeen published deltas exceeds its own minimum detectable difference. Five exceed their own 95%
half-width, and all five are negative.** The record has measured harm and never measured help. Six iterations of
prompt-side channel work — framing, evidence, dose, probe, raw, square — produced point estimates between −2.57
and −4.86pp, and not one of them is distinguishable from zero at the bar the project's own `V5-resolution` gate
applies to a single comparison. Those were not nulls either; they were *unreadable*, and the difference matters
because a null licenses "the channel does not help" while unreadable licenses only "we do not know".

**The number that reorganises the rest: the mechanism's best positive reading is smaller than the sharpest design
the project has ever run.** The `values` channel returns **+1.17pp** on 1,534 questions, 64 helped against 46
harmed, 95% interval `[−0.13, +2.48]`, p = 0.1046. That comparison's own minimum detectable difference is
**1.91pp**. The effect is 61% of what its design could resolve — and that design is the best in the record. To
resolve a 1.17pp effect at the observed 7.2% discordance takes **4,100 paired questions**; to resolve a round 1pp
at the dev split's 8.4% takes **6,603**. BIRD's dev split is 1,534. Its train split is 9,428. **The corpus that
would settle this question exists and the project has never run on it.**

**What this says about the standing hypothesis, stated carefully.** The hypothesis entering this round was that
the negative effects come from what is stored and how it is used. That is still the best hypothesis available and
nothing here refutes it — but the audit changes what "we do not know" means: six iterations of the record compared
effects of 1–5pp on samples that could see 3.8–4.9pp, so the *evidence that the storage is wrong* has never been
separated from the evidence that the **instrument** was too coarse to see either answer. Relevance is now excluded
as the axis by two independent covariates. What remains is a family the record has never tested, and every member
of it is a property of what a rule **does to the query** rather than of how near it is to the question: whether it
supplies an identifier the question does not contain, whether it repeats a decision the model already made
correctly, whether it names a table the schema already ruled out. Those are readable from `predictedSql` against
`baselineSql` in the committed artefacts — the same offline, zero-call substrate this round used — and they are
the subject of R30's first stage rather than a reading list.

**Three defects, none of them on the round's list, and the third is the one that matters commercially.**

The first is the registration's missing power floor, and it is the third time in four rounds that a criterion was
found to be decidable by cells too small to decide anything (§138's `V5-resolution` is the second). The second
belongs to the audit itself: it covers whole-artefact deltas, so an arm inside an artefact is not a row — the
record's one positive reading, the `values` channel at +1.17pp, is not in the table above and had to be looked up by
hand. **The audit undercounts positives rather than overcounting them**, which is the direction that matters, and
the gap is in the artefact's `notes` rather than left for a reader to find.

**The third was found while checking the arithmetic of the claim this project has been making about itself.**
`COMPETITIVE.md` §1 carried one row for this project, annotated `1 (+ memory pack)`, quoting **57.63** on BIRD dev.
That number is the **no-memory** cell. `compareCell` reads `metrics.accuracy_without_memory` by construction, because
the published cell it is compared against is a no-memory cell — so the row that says "+4.11 over the reproduced
baseline" has always been a row about the harness. The memory arm of that same run is **56.26**, which means that on
BIRD dev **the pack costs 1.37pp of execution accuracy** (paired, 1,534 questions, 47 helped against 68 harmed,
resolution 1.96pp). The row is now split in two, and the numbers are what they are: the harness beats the published
baseline by 4.11pp and the product feature subtracts from it. The loss is inside its own resolution, so the correct
statement is not "memory hurts" — it is that **nothing on BIRD dev attributes any of our advantage to memory**, and
the one number in this record that was read as a product win was reading the wrong arm.

**The arithmetic that produced the correction, because it is the same arithmetic as everywhere else in this round.**
57.63 against a published 53.52 is two *independent* samples — they cannot be paired, so the width is
`sqrt(p₁(1−p₁)/n + p₂(1−p₂)/n) = 1.79pp`. The difference of 4.11pp is 2.30 standard errors: it clears the 95% bar
(3.51pp) and **not** the 80%-power bar (5.02pp). The project had been quoting the point estimate without either.

**Green.** `pnpm check` — typecheck, `typecheck:lanes` under `--strict`, **2,191 tests over 112 files**, four
coverage dimensions at **99.98 / 99.63 / 100 / 99.98** with `strata.ts` and `power.ts` at **100 on all four**;
`audit:repo`, six offline lanes, `eval:protocol` (13 pre-registrations, 10 gate-list agreements, 2 cell
recomputations), two new workflow steps that recompute `poc-harm-strata.json` and `poc-power-audit.json` byte for
byte, `bench` (blocking gates PASS) and `bundle:size` all green. No published artefact changed except the two this
round added.

### 140 — The harm is a name the question never mentioned, and it was in the record the whole time

**Three rounds of covariates came back flat, and the fourth axis needed no new calls.** R26 varied the channels a
rule travels through and bounded the annotator at +1.17pp. R28 stratified 1,534 committed questions by query–rule
overlap and got a shape worth 18.55pp against a resolution of 32.23pp — not a shape. R30 stage 1 asked the
question those two could not: not *how near the rule is* but *what the rule made the query do*. That quantity was
already sitting in every committed case, in two fields nobody had read side by side: `predictedSql` and
`baselineSql`, the same question answered by the same model with and without the pack.

**What was built.** `packages/eval/src/sql-diff.ts` (a tokeniser, a shape extractor, and a diff), `query-diff.ts`
(the join to the outcome, four tests and a counterfactual), and one bin that writes
`eval/results/poc-query-diff.json` from one committed file. 1,307 lines with their comments, 69 tests, and **100
on all four coverage dimensions for both modules**. The workflow recomputes the artefact and compares it byte for
byte, then asserts the nineteen facts below, so a classifier change that flipped a verdict arrives as a named
failure rather than as a diff nobody reads.

**The taxonomy, and the first split that is not a similarity.**

| label | n | share | helped / harmed | delta | 95% half-width | MDE | baseline acc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `unchanged` | 692 | 45.1% | 0 / 0 | **+0.00pp** | ±0.00 | ∞ | 65.3% |
| `reworded` | 73 | 4.8% | 1 / 0 | +1.37 | ±2.68 | 3.84 | 64.4% |
| `imported-name` | 155 | 10.1% | 10 / 25 | **−9.68pp** | ±7.48 | 10.69 | 45.2% |
| `narrowed` | 103 | 6.7% | 16 / 9 | +6.80 | ±9.51 | 13.60 | 40.8% |
| `widened` | 108 | 7.0% | 18 / 13 | +4.63 | ±10.10 | 14.45 | 43.5% |
| `reshaped` | 58 | 3.8% | 11 / 4 | +12.07 | ±13.09 | 18.71 | 25.9% |
| `rewritten` | 345 | 22.5% | 11 / 11 | +0.00 | ±2.66 | 3.81 | 60.3% |

**The label is assigned by one rule with a stated precedence**: an ungrounded name outranks a direction, because a
query can both narrow and import and the imported name is the part a filter could act on. `narrowed` means more
conjunctions, more tables, more aggregates or a shorter select list; `widened` is its mirror; `reshaped` is both at
once, which is what a rewrite rather than an adjustment looks like. Six of the seven labels sit at or above zero.
**One sits eight points below it, and it is the one that names something the question never did.**

| code | what it splits on | n | delta present | delta absent | gap | 95% | clustered 95% | Fisher |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** | memory query introduces a name neither the baseline nor the question contains | 155 | **−9.68pp** | +1.45pp | **−11.13** | ±7.61 | [−19.60, −2.63] | 0.0015 |
| F2 | the same, morphological grounding | 114 | −9.65 | +1.13 | −10.78 | ±8.37 | [−21.78, −1.59] | 0.0102 |
| F3 | introduces a name the question *does* contain | 24 | +12.50 | +0.13 | +12.37 | ±21.65 | [−4.29, +31.82] | 0.4426 |
| F4 | adds a table the baseline did not read | 77 | −10.39 | +0.89 | −11.28 | ±11.47 | [−24.50, +1.87] | 0.0499 |
| F5 | adds at least one conjunction | 40 | −7.50 | +0.54 | −8.04 | ±13.04 | [−21.18, +6.97] | 0.2599 |
| F6 | changed the query at all | 842 | +0.59 | +0.00 | +0.59 | ±2.64 | [−1.15, +2.40] | 1.0000 |

**F1 is the first covariate this record has measured that clears its own resolution.** The gap is 11.13pp against
a 95% half-width of 7.61pp, the database-clustered interval excludes zero by 2.63pp, and the exact test gives
p = 0.0015 on 155 against 1,379. F6 is the control that makes it a mechanism rather than a denominator: *changing
the query at all* is worth +0.59pp ±2.64, so the effect is not "the pack moved something". F3 is the comparison
half, and it points the other way: the 24 questions where the pack imported a name the question **did** contain
gained 12.50pp, on a sample too small to resolve — the same direction the mechanism predicts, from the other side.

**F2 is the robustness check, and the design of it matters.** The strict grounding rule is exact token membership,
and it has a known false positive: `raceId` against "qualifying race No.903" is not a token of the question, though
BIRD's own gold query filters on it. Under a looser rule — a question word of three letters is a prefix of the name
— 41 of the 155 leave the group and the gap moves from −11.13pp to −10.78pp, still beyond its own ±8.37pp width.
**The finding survives the rule that was chosen to break it**, which is what separates a tokeniser artefact from a
measurement.

**Six features were tested, and the multiplicity is reported rather than absorbed.** F1 and F2 are one hypothesis
under two grounding rules, so the family is five distinct questions, and Bonferroni puts the threshold at
`0.05 / 5 = 0.01`. **F1 survives it at p = 0.0015. F2 does not: p = 0.0102 misses 0.01 by two ten-thousandths**,
and that is written here rather than rounded away, because the robustness check is exactly the place where a
reader is entitled to know that the second rule's exact test lands just outside the corrected bar while its
interval test clears. The registered criterion `Q1` keeps the 0.05 the registration named — a bar lowered after the
result is not a bar — and the adjusted threshold travels beside it in the artefact.

**The mechanism is damage, not missed repair, and stratifying on the baseline outcome is what shows it.**

| | already-correct queries destroyed | already-wrong queries repaired |
|---|---|---|
| group that imports an ungrounded name (n=155) | **35.71%** | 11.76% |
| everything else (n=1,379) | **4.56%** | 10.04% |

The repair rate is flat — 11.76 against 10.04, one point apart on 155 questions. **The damage rate differs by a
factor of 7.8.** That comparison is stratified on `withoutMemoryCorrect`, which is fixed before the treatment
exists, so it is not the difficulty story: both cells are questions the model *already answered right* without
memory, and in one of them the pack then broke seven times as many. The importing group is also the harder one
(45.2% baseline accuracy against the corpus's 57.4%), and a harder question has *more* room to gain — so the
difficulty confound points against the finding rather than for it. Both arguments are now in the artefact as `Q4`,
and the rate is reported rather than the argument.

**The registered predictions.** All five criteria pass; the refutation clause does not fire.

| code | criterion | actual | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Q1` | the identifier covariate separates help from harm, beyond its own width and at p < 0.05 | gap −11.13pp ±7.61, p = 0.0015 | pass |
| `Q2` | most discordant cases have no identifiable cause in the query diff | **94 of 129 (72.9%)** unexplained, the largest bucket | pass |
| `Q3` | the separation survives the looser grounding rule | gap −10.78pp ±8.37 over 114 | pass |
| `Q4` | it is not a difficulty artefact | 35.71% vs 4.56% destroyed | pass |
| `Q5` | a gate that discards every importing query would raise the delta | +0.33pp → **+1.30pp** | pass |

**Q2 is the one that bounds the round.** The covariate describes 35 of the 129 discordant questions and no more.
The other 94 flips — 72.9% — have no imported name in them, which is the registered prediction written down
before the run ("a category called *unexplained* is expected to be the largest single bucket, and its size is the
honest ceiling on what a per-question analysis can ever attribute"). It is also the answer to what a filter can
buy: at most the 35.

**The counterfactual, and the two reasons not to ship it.** For every question the gate would discard, the record
already holds the no-pack query and its outcome, so the gated arm is read rather than predicted:

| gate | discarded | measured | gated | 95% | MDE | McNemar p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| strict grounding | 155 (10.1%) | +0.33pp | **+1.30pp** | ±1.24 | 1.77 | 0.0495 |
| morphological | 114 (7.4%) | +0.33pp | +1.04pp | ±1.32 | 1.88 | 0.1448 |

The gate almost quadruples the point estimate and, for the first time in this record, produces a pack arm whose
95% interval excludes zero. **It is not shipped, for two reasons that the numbers themselves state.** It clears
the 95% bar by 0.06pp and misses its own 80%-power bar by 0.47pp, so it is a detection at the edge of what the
sample can see; and it was chosen by looking at these same 1,534 questions, so the improvement is in-sample by
construction and an out-of-sample run would regress it toward zero by an amount nobody has measured. R30 stage 2
is the sample that can confirm it. Until then the gate is a registered prediction with an estimate attached, not
a behaviour.

**The shippable form of the gate was measured too, and it fails, which is the round's second result.** `F1`
reads the query, so it is post-treatment: it can describe what happened and it cannot be applied before a query
exists. The version that *could* ship — an admission filter that refuses a rule whose text names something the
question does not — is a different hypothesis, and it was measured on the same corpus with a detector that reads
backticked identifiers and snake-case names:

| | n | helped / harmed | delta | baseline acc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| at least one injected rule names an ungrounded identifier | 385 (25.1%) | 19 / 8 | **+2.86pp** | 56.9% |
| no rule does | 1,149 | 48 / 54 | −0.52pp | 57.6% |

**It has the wrong sign.** And it is not finding what `F1` finds: of the 155 questions `F1` flags, the rule-level
flag catches **50** (recall 32.3%) while flagging 335 that `F1` does not (precision 13.0%). The agreement table is
`both 50 / query-only 105 / rule-only 335 / neither 1,044`. Two readings fit, and the artefact states both: the
detector sees an identifier in only **138 of the 1,066 committed rules (13.0%)**, because the rest say "a numeric
code column" rather than naming one — so either the rule text genuinely does not determine what the model writes,
or the representation loses the names. Either way the conclusion for the product is the same and it is
uncomfortable: **the version of this gate that could be applied before generation is not the version that works,
and the version that works needs a query to have been written first.** R31 registers the field that would tell the
two readings apart.

**Two things the record cannot answer, reported as absent rather than approximated.** The registration's third
category is *a table or column the rule named that the schema had pruned*, and the committed `per_case` stores the
schema candidate as `schemaTables: { kept, total, pruned }` — three numbers, no names. The category is therefore
**unmeasured**, and it is in the artefact under `unmeasured` with its reason, its nearest substitute (`F4`) and
the difference between them. F4 says *a table was added*; the registration asked whether *the pruning removed the
name the pack used*. Substituting one for the other would be a second question answered under the first one's
name, which is the defect §138 spent a round removing. The fix is one field in stage 2's `per_case`.

**The second absence is a number that reads as missing and is not.** The 692 untouched questions have a minimum
detectable difference of **infinity** — nothing can be detected from a comparison in which nothing changed — and
JSON writes infinity as `null`. `helped + harmed === 0` is what tells that apart from an empty group, and the
artefact says so in its notes rather than leaving a reader to infer it from a zero.

**One structural fact that changes how every rate in this record should be read.** 45.1% of the corpus is
untouched by the pack, and those questions carry 65.3% baseline accuracy against 45.2% for the questions where it
imports a name. **The pack moves the query exactly where the model was least sure**, which is why every
intent-to-treat number this project has published is diluted by a stratum where the treatment cannot act and is
selected on the model's own uncertainty. The 129 discordant cases therefore all live in the 50.1% that moved, and
every rate above is quoted over the whole corpus rather than over that subset — conditioning on "the query moved"
is conditioning on a post-treatment variable that correlates with difficulty by 20 points, and the honest
denominator is the one the treatment was assigned to.

**Green.** `pnpm check` — typecheck, `typecheck:lanes` under `--strict`, **2,260 tests over 114 files**, four
coverage dimensions at **99.98 / 99.65 / 100 / 99.98** with `sql-diff.ts` and `query-diff.ts` at **100 on all
four**; `audit:repo`, six offline lanes, `eval:protocol`, `eval:harm`, `eval:power` and the new `eval:query-diff`
all green, plus a workflow step that recomputes `poc-query-diff.json` byte for byte and asserts nineteen facts.
No published artefact changed except the one this round adds.

**What this changes.** Three covariates are now eliminated and one is not. Relevance, embedding similarity and
channel are dead as explanations; **what a rule makes the query name is alive**, with a gap that clears its own
resolution for the first time in twenty-eight rounds, a stratified damage rate that differs by a factor of 7.8,
and a pre-registered estimate of what removing it would buy. The product statement it licenses is narrow and
testable: *a rule may not put a name into the query that the question does not contain* — and the thing that
decides whether that is a result is whether it reproduces at n ≈ 6,600, which is R30 stage 2 and the only
remaining item on the critical path.

## 141. The pack does not put the name there, and the gate does not depend on one database

**The question this round answers was not on the list, and it retires an item that was.** R31 registered a store
rebuild — a `names` field on `LearnedItem` — on the premise that the representation loses the identifiers 928 of
1,066 rules never spell out. That premise is answerable from the record that already exists, because the lane
stores the rendered text of every rule that reached the prompt: if the pack's text does not contain the name, a
field that names it more precisely cannot change anything.

**The attribution, in three buckets that are exhaustive by construction.** Every one of the 155 questions §140
flags is placed in exactly one: the pack names the identifier; it does not and the query executed, which is what
licenses calling the name real — a statement that ran cannot have named a column its table does not have; or it
does not and the query never ran, which is *unverifiable* rather than *invented*, because a failed statement may
have named a real column and failed on a date format.

| bucket | questions | Δ vs no memory | already-correct queries destroyed | baseline accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the pack names the identifier | 60 (38.7%) | −8.33pp | 36.36% | 36.7% |
| the pack does not, and the query ran | 94 (60.6%) | −9.57pp | 34.04% | 50.0% |
| the pack does not, and the query never ran | 1 (0.6%) | — | — | 100.0% |

**The two buckets are damaged by the same amount.** The gap is **1.24pp against its own 14.74pp half-width**, and
the point estimate runs *opposite* to the hypothesis: the questions a rule named a column for are the *less*
damaged ones. Per name the picture is the same and slightly worse: 79 of 285 imported names are spelled out by a
rule (27.7%), and forgiving every spelling difference reaches 101 (35.4%).

**What that does to §140's product statement.** It is withdrawn. *A rule may not put a name into the query that
the question does not contain* describes a cause the pack has in 38.7% of the flagged questions and does not have
in 60.6%, and the 38.7% is not the damaged part. The mechanism that survives is the one the data states plainly:
**the pack changes what the model writes, and the imported name is the symptom of that change.** What replaces the
statement is narrower, still actionable, and no longer about how a rule is worded: *a generated query that names
something neither the question nor the pack mentions should not be executed as written.*

**The number that makes the withdrawal quantitative rather than rhetorical.** The read-time gate's +0.98pp
decomposes exactly across the buckets, because the fallback query is a column rather than a prediction:

| bucket | contribution to the gate |
|---|---|
| questions the pack named | **+0.33pp** |
| questions it never named | **+0.59pp** |
| statements that never ran | +0.07pp |

A third of what the filter recovers comes from the bucket an admission filter could reach and 60% from the bucket
it could never see. R31's cost — one dispatch and a contract change across distillation — buys a better-resolved
view of the third.

**The gate itself, taken apart three ways.** The estimate that motivated stage 2 is not a property of one database,
of the discard *size*, or of one half of the corpus:

| reading | result |
|---|---|
| leave-one-database-out | +0.77pp to +1.25pp over 11 databases; the weakest is `financial`, and it is still positive |
| permutation, 5,000 draws without replacement | observed +0.98pp against a null of −0.04pp [−0.46, 0.39]; **p = 0.0002** |
| split by database, balanced on count | A +0.76pp (n=794, 77 discarded), B +1.22pp (n=740, 78 discarded) |

The permutation null is not centred on zero and should not be: a random 10% of this corpus still discards damaged
questions in proportion, so it is worth something on its own. What the test says is that the gate's *placement*
beats random placement by four null standard deviations, which is the claim a filter has to make.

**What the split-half cannot say, written into the artefact rather than left to a reader.** Both halves were in
the corpus the hypothesis was formed on, so a split of it is a stability check and never an out-of-sample test.
The shrinkage an unseen sample would show is unmeasured, and R30 stage 2 is the only reading that can measure it.

**The first run of this round passed, and the criterion was tightened anyway.** `M3` was first written as a point
comparison — 36.36% greater than 34.04% — and it passed. The same run printed the interval around that difference,
which is twelve times its size, so the criterion was rewritten to require that the gap clear its own half-width
*before its verdict was accepted*, and it then failed. Both facts are recorded: the tightening changed the answer,
and a criterion that is adjusted after a result is only defensible if the adjustment and its direction are written
down. The direction here was towards the stricter bar; the round would have looked better without it.

**Two zero-cost readings, one dispatch avoided, and one claim withdrawn.** `pnpm eval:mediation` and
`pnpm eval:stability` both run in `pnpm check`; the workflow recomputes both artefacts byte for byte and asserts
34 facts about them, including the withdrawal itself. `schema-link.ts` now records the names the pruner removed
(R30 stage 1b), so the registration's third category becomes readable on the next dispatch.

**Green.** `pnpm check` — typecheck, `typecheck:lanes` under `--strict`, **2,320 tests over 117 files**, four
coverage dimensions at **99.98 / 99.65 / 100 / 99.98** with all four new modules (`corpus.ts`,
`pack-mediation.ts`, `gate-stability.ts`, and the refactored `query-diff.ts`) at **100 on all four**;
`audit:repo`, six offline lanes, `eval:protocol`, `eval:harm`, `eval:power`, `eval:query-diff`, `eval:mediation`
and `eval:stability` all green. `poc-query-diff.json` changed in exactly two places — one float in the last bit
from the closed form that replaces a difference of two bootstraps, and the `unmeasured` note for `pruned-name`.

## 142. The out-of-sample split exists, and finding out cost five defects and no model calls

**This round did not measure the mechanism. It made the measurement possible, and it found out that
the measurement would have failed five times.** R30 stage 2 is the only reading left that can test
§140's gate out of sample, and its own registered prediction 4 said the dispatch is the one most
likely to fail. So the round was a precheck: load the split exactly as the lane will, stop before the
first model call, and report what would have stopped a run.

**The two cheaper exits are closed, and one of them closed this round.** Mini-Dev cannot serve as a
second sample, because **496 of its 500 questions are dev questions**. The record already used that
fact correctly without naming it — R24's decomposition `925/1534 × 14.05 + 609/1534 × 22.99 = 17.60`
treats Mini-Dev as a slice of dev, not as an independent corpus — so nothing is withdrawn here. What
is new is that the alternative to a second sample is now a measured statement rather than an
assumption: a fresh split of dev is in-sample by construction, and Mini-Dev is a subset of dev. BIRD
train is the only remaining source: 9,428 questions over 69 databases that neither split touches.

**The precheck, on the real archive.**

| reading | train | dev (control) | mini-dev (control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| questions in the file | 9,428 | 1,534 | 500 |
| after the split's pool rule | 9,428 | 1,534 | **350** |
| after the manifest's selection | **7,829** | 1,534 | 350 |
| databases used | 58 | 11 | 11 |
| databases empty or unreadable | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| two copies of the gold disagree | **0 of 9,428** | — | — |
| verdict | **ready** | ready | ready |

The mini-dev column reading **350** is the check on the checker. 350 is the number every transfer
experiment in this repository calls that slice — it is in `ROADMAP.md` and in nine readings — and the
precheck was not told it. It fell out of applying the same pool rule to the same file, which is the
only reason to believe the train column is a reading rather than a coincidence.

**Five defects, none of which a dev run could have found.** Each would have consumed a dispatch, and
four of the five fail *after* the 8.9 GB download:

1. **`poolOf` read a field train does not have.** `row.difficulty.toLowerCase()` is a `TypeError` on
   9,428 rows that carry `SQL`, `db_id`, `question` and `evidence` and nothing else. The lane would
   die at startup, after the download and the unpack.
2. **The download buffered the archive.** `arrayBuffer()` puts the whole file in one allocation —
   346 MB for dev, which worked, and 8.9 GB for train, which is most of a runner's memory before the
   databases exist. It is now a stream to a `.part` file and a rename, which is also the reason an
   interrupted transfer cannot leave a truncated file under the name the size check trusts.
3. **The extractor looked for `dev_databases.zip`.** Train ships `train_databases.zip`, so the nested
   archive would not be found and every question would fail with "No database file" — the same
   failure mode as the second dev dispatch, one archive later. The nested pair is now a manifest
   field, read as a pair or not at all.
4. **`resolveDatabase` knew three database roots and not `train_databases`.** It now takes the root
   the caller's manifest declares, so a new archive layout is a manifest field rather than a fourth
   guess in a shared function.
5. **`SOTA_ARTEFACT` would have overwritten Mini-Dev.** The expression was
   `split == 'dev' && A || B`, which answers B for train — and B is `poc-sota-bird.json`. This is
   precisely the loss that variable was introduced to prevent, reappearing as a two-way choice that
   grew a third arm.

**The selection is a bytes-per-question decision, and it is nearly free.** The archive unpacks its
databases to **32.4 GB**, four of them over 4 GB each — but the questions are spread over the small
ones: `works_cycles` carries 474 questions in 115 MB, `retail_world` 373 in 0.1 MB, while `donor`
carries 160 in 4.5 GB.

| | databases | questions | unpacked |
|---|---|---|---|
| whole archive | 69 | 9,428 | 32.4 GB |
| the manifest's selection | **58** | **7,829** | **2.4 GB** |

Eleven databases cost 30.0 GB and 1,599 questions, so the selection keeps **83.0% of the questions
for 7.4% of the bytes**. The lane prints the number and carries it in the artefact, so a smaller `n`
is explained rather than discovered.

**`limit=7000`, and the reason is a measured wall clock rather than a preference.** Dev at 1,534
questions over four arms is 6,504 calls in 130 minutes. Seven thousand questions over two arms is
about 15,000 calls, 2.3× that, against a six-hour job limit and a 340-minute step timeout: a 15%
margin. The cost in resolution is 6% — dev resolves 2.01pp at 1,534, so 7,000 resolves 0.94pp and
7,829 would resolve 0.89pp — and both can see the +0.98pp effect the dispatch exists to test.

**The analysis path was also broken for a second corpus, and now is not.** The three readings that
produced §140 and §141 each read one hard-coded artefact and wrote one hard-coded name, so a train
run would have had no analysis or would have overwritten the dev evidence CI compares byte for byte.
`POC_RESULT_SUFFIX` writes `poc-query-diff-train.json` beside its dev sibling; the dev artefacts are
byte-unchanged this round, which is how the mechanism was checked.

**Green.** `pnpm check` — typecheck, `typecheck:lanes` under `--strict`, **2,353 tests over 118
files**, four coverage dimensions at **99.98 / 99.66 / 100 / 99.98** with `bird-rows.ts` at **100 on
all four**; `audit:repo`, six offline lanes, `eval:protocol`, `eval:harm`, `eval:power`,
`eval:query-diff`, `eval:mediation` and `eval:stability` all green, and all three dev artefacts
byte-identical. `prereg/R30-stage2.md` is written with its five predictions and its five refutations
before the dispatch, which is the only thing that makes the eventual number a test.

**What is still not measured.** Everything §142 enabled and did not do: the gate has no out-of-sample
number, the imported-name covariate has no second corpus, and the train accuracy is not comparable to
any leaderboard row — BIRD publishes no test cell for it. One dispatch is the whole remaining
distance, and it is the next item on the list.

## 143. The second-closest feature was the first one counted twice

**R32 registered three candidate explanations for damage that is not lexical. The first one is
gone, and it cost nothing to remove.** The registration named the table-set feature as its second
axis on the strength of a number: F4 — the memory query reads a table the baseline did not — reads
−10.39pp at p = 0.0499, the next-closest feature to resolving after F1's −11.13pp. That is exactly
what a shadow of F1 looks like, so §R32 prediction 2 fixed the test before the numbers were read:
`both / left < 0.5`, and then the reading the bar cannot give — *is F4 still harmful on the questions
F1 does not cover*.

**The contingency table, on the same 1,534 questions.**

| | F4 present | F4 absent |
|---|---|---|
| **F1 present** | 70 | 85 |
| **F1 absent** | 7 | 1,372 |

The overlap is **45.2%**, inside the registered bar of 50%. On the reading that matters, F4 is not a
second cause: on the **7 questions that add a table without importing a name, the net effect is
exactly 0.00pp**. The −10.39pp the registration quoted is carried entirely by the 70 questions where
both features are present, which means the two labels describe one event — a query that reached for
something the question did not supply, sometimes a column and sometimes a whole table.

**The same reading applied to the narrowing direction.** F5 — at least one added conjunction, the
direction whose *kind* average is +6.80pp — overlaps F1 by only **7.7%** (12 shared of 155), so the
two are genuinely different populations. But outside the overlap F5 is worth **−3.57pp on 28
questions**, against a half-width it does not clear. It is `inert` for the same reason F4 is: a label
that names a consequence of the mechanism without adding anything to it.

| pair | both | left only | right only | overlap | right outside left |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 / F4 (table added) | 70 | 85 | 7 | 45.2% | **0.00pp** (n=7) |
| F1 / F5 (conjunction added) | 12 | 143 | 28 | 7.7% | −3.57pp (n=28) |

**Why the criterion needed two questions and not one.** The registered bar —
`both / left < 0.5` — is satisfied by *both* pairs, and taken alone it would have said F4 and F5 are
distinct findings. They are distinct as *sets* and empty as *causes*, and the vocabulary this round
added says so: `shadow` (overlap ≥ 50%, the same finding twice), `independent` (small overlap and
still harmful outside it), `inert` (small overlap, nothing outside). The bar measures description;
the outside reading measures mechanism. A registration that fixed only the first would have licensed
a claim the second refutes.

**What this leaves of R32.** Axis 2 is closed. Axis 1 — procedural versus declarative rules — has a
problem the registration did not anticipate: the 1,066 rules are almost all written in the same
conditional–action form (*"A query that X returns Y rather than Z"*), so the two classes the axis
names may not exist in this corpus as syntactic objects. Axis 3 — schema ambiguity resolved in the
wrong direction — is untouched and is now the only one of the three that could explain the mechanism.
Both are recorded as open rather than done; a round that closed one axis and found a second
unmeasurable has not finished R32.

**Green.** `pnpm eval:feature-overlap` is recomputed from the same committed artefact as §140 and
§141, writes `poc-feature-overlap.json` beside them, and runs in `pnpm check`. The two new modules —
`feature-overlap.ts` and `diff-corpus.ts` — are at **100 on all four coverage dimensions**, and
`diff-corpus.ts` exists because the fourth reading of one artefact was about to acquire its own copy
of the same four-line construction.

## 144 — The rule's id was reused across folds, and the per-rule result was a different corpus

Three things happened in this round and only one of them was planned. The dispatch stopped on a
parameter I set, the first R32 axis turned out to be unmeasurable for a reason stronger than the one
§143 guessed, and — found while building the classifier for that axis — **a rule id is not a rule**.

### The dispatch stopped after one fold, and the number was mine

Run `41294945557` finished fold 1 of 5 and refused to go on:

```
[sota] fold 1/5: eval=1400 learn=280 edited=95 unanswered=0 distillFailed=0 active=184 calls=3175
[sota] budget forecast after fold 1/5: the run needs about 17145 calls, the cap is 16000 (short by 1145)
```

`prereg/R30-stage2.md` had registered "about 15,000 model calls", and 15,000 was 7,000 × 2 arms plus
a guess at learning. The guess was made in questions and the meter counts calls: a fold of 1,400
questions over two arms is 2,800 generations before any learning, its 280-question learning pass is
another 280 prompts, and the 95 edited queries were re-asked rather than dropped. That is 3,175
against a 3,000 estimate — 5.8% per fold, 14% over five.

**Amendment 1** raises the cap to 20,000 and changes nothing else: same `limit`, same arms, same
folds, same deadline, same five predictions and five refutations. A cap is a safety valve, not a
parameter of the design. Fold 1's numbers are **discarded** rather than reported — a run that
stopped because of a parameter I set is a truncated run, and the fold it finished is the first fold,
so quoting it would be reading the one fold that happened to fit. The re-dispatch (`41296776252`) is
the run this record will report.

### Axis 1 was not unmeasurable for the reason §143 gave

§143 closed axis 2 and left axis 1 with an impression: *the 1,066 rules are almost all written in
the same conditional–action form, so the two classes may not exist here as syntactic objects*. That
impression is wrong, and testing it produced a stronger reason.

**There are not 1,066 rules.** There are 1,066 *rows*, and they are **271 sentences over 229 id
slots**, of which 220 slots are cited by at least one question. Every count this record has quoted
about "the 1,066 committed rules" was a count of rows across five folds. A single run carries about
**210 rules**, not 1,066.

**The two forms do not separate, and they fail by 8 points rather than by inspection.** Classifying
each distinct sentence by whether it carries a declarative marker (asserts a state or consequence)
