announces readiness and the clock starts at the statement. A lane's accuracy must not depend on how busy
the machine was.

**What the round did not change.** Every committed artefact: `pnpm eval:protocol` revalidates all 31, and
every reading in the chain rewrites its file byte for byte. That is the only reason a mechanical stage is
worth doing — it can be verified mechanically.

Sealed by **2,793 tests across 132 files**, four coverage dimensions at **99.98 / 99.68 / 100 / 99.98**
with `coupling.ts` at **100 on all four**, three blocking gates, and eleven arithmetic assertions in CI
over a recomputed artefact.

## 157 — The transfer gates graded, and the store the arm never built

**R41 ran, and the transfer family is now graded on a scenario it was not written for.** That was the
round's registered purpose, and it was met: `V15-transfer-reconciles`, `V33-transfer-ledger` and
`V17-transfer-net-reported` all fired and passed on a τ²-airline pair whose store had learned from
τ²-retail. `V16-transfer-resolvable` failed, exactly as registered — 72 informative episodes against a
floor of a hundred — and a pass there would have meant the floor was being cleared by episodes that were
not informative. The audit's index moved by exactly the four gates the registration named: supplyable
4 → **13**, arm-indexed 35 → **26**.

| reading | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| `V15` | 200/200 episodes reconciled: **72 informative, 128 already repaired by the retry, 0 unmeasured** | `poc-l4-pair.json` |
| `V16` | **72 informative, 12 repairs** — the floor is a hundred | same |
| `V33` | **200/200 pairs carried**, one ledger row per episode | same |
| `V17` | **−5.00pp net** over 200 measured trials (12 repaired, 22 broken), verdict `unmeasured` | same |
| `l4-paired` | **−10.00pp**, 95% CI [−22, +2], p = 0.1797, n = 50 — **fails** | same |
| `l4-same-split` | 0 only in first, 0 only in second | same |
| `V5-resolution` | the sample resolves **16.81pp**; the pair cannot separate 10pp from zero | same |

**And the arm that produced those numbers had no memory in it.** `V1-pack-not-empty` read **0.00
rules/question**: the store held no knowledge when evaluation began, so every recall returned nothing,
the agent was told nothing it had not been told before, and the arm labelled `memory` was the reference
arm with an HTTP façade in front of it. The artefact says so from the other end as well — `domainOrigin`
recorded **0 items stored**, and the store's own log line was `stored 0`.

**Nothing in the record could say why, and that is the round's actual finding.** Three readings lived in
the driver's process and none of them was written down: the distiller's report, the model client's call
tally, and the store's admission counts. Two gates read exactly those numbers — `V32-fold-learning-intact`
and `V8-call-reliability` — so both were **absent** on the one dispatch where they would have fired, and
`V44-domain-accounted`, which reconciles the store's ledger, **passed on `0 <= 0`**. A blocking gate that
certifies an empty population is a gate that certifies nothing, and it is why the pair looked valid enough
to read.

**The cause, traced through the code rather than guessed from the artefact.** τ²'s Python half is a
litellm caller, so the lane names its model `deepseek/deepseek-chat` in one variable. The TypeScript
client that distils the corrections read the same variable and posted that string to
`api.deepseek.com/chat/completions`, whose `model` field is `deepseek-chat`; the prefixed form is refused
with a 400, the client does not retry a 400, and `distill` counts a refused event as "the model said
nothing about this correction". Thirty-two corrections, thirty-two refusals, an empty store — and the
client's own tally read `prompts: 32, failures: 0`, because a failure was counted only when four attempts
had been spent. The strongest reliability claim the lane can make, about thirty-two refusals.

**A third defect was underneath both.** `combineInterpreters` runs every interpreter it is given and stops
at the first that throws, so the rule interpreter that would have produced a negative lesson for each
correction never ran. Its docstring called the second argument a "generic fallback", which is what the
lane read; the code had never implemented one.

**R42 is registered and dispatched** (`prereg/R42-instrument.md`, run `41468737074`). It fixes the three
defects and re-runs the same arm, and its predictions are about the instrument rather than the effect:
`V1` passes at a pack the artefact records, `V32` fires and passes, `V8` fires over a stated population,
`V44` fires on a non-empty store, the fired set grows by exactly those two ids, `V16` still fails, and the
transfer net stays at or below +5pp with the sign not predicted. The reading of that dispatch is §158.

**What R41 bought, stated plainly.** The transfer machinery is portable — three of four gates graded on a
second scenario with a ledger a reader can recompute — and the lane's own instrument is not yet able to
say why an arm it measured was empty. Both sentences are in the record now, and the second one is the
more useful: it is the first time a round's blocking gate fired at the *input* rather than at the result,
and the four gates that stayed silent are the reason it took a re-read of the code to find out what
happened.

Sealed by **2,849 tests across 137 files**, four coverage dimensions at **99.98 / 99.67 / 100 / 99.98**,
with `tau2-plan.ts`, `tau2-transfer.ts`, `tau2-gates.ts`, `tau2-distill.ts` and `l4-scenario.ts` at
**100 on all four**.

## What is left, in order (current)

**Every question this page has been organised around is now answered, and §150 answered the last one without a model call.** The covariate reproduces (§146), the mechanism does not (§141, withdrawn in §146), the gate's benefit shrinks to half while the product stops paying (§147), the check is differential and cannot stand alone (§148), and the question §148 left open — whether a *weaker injection* exists — turned out to be the wrong question: the memory is 43% short of break-even, and the half that could have been rescued, the population, cannot be selected by anything measurable before generation (§149). **Nothing ships, and the reason is now five-layered rather than one.** §150 added the fifth layer and it is the strongest: the store's items have no per-item value that transfers, so the store cannot be pruned by evidence either. What is left is one arm that would settle the only positive lead, one blocked measurement, and eight mechanical or blocked items.

**What the list looks like now.** §149 removed the last item that could have changed the product without a model call, and it removed it by arithmetic rather than by argument: the break-even exchange rate is 1.393, the measured one is 0.789, and no gate on a question can see the difference. Item 1 is finished and it did not say what the programme wanted. §147 then
turned the negative into an arithmetic bound: the filter's ceiling on this corpus is 3.39pp and it realises
15% of it, so the option of shipping it *with* memory cannot beat a wash by construction. §148 closed the
last open shape without a model call, by pointing the rule at one query instead of at a difference: it flags
94.8% of everything, its Youden index is a quarter of the anchored filter's, and the only thing it does
measurably well is detect what the pack does (5.8% of clean questions acquire an imported name). **So the
critical path is no longer a decision — and it is no longer even a registration.** Item 10's entry condition is now a statement about the store, and the store has been the ceiling since R13: 22 of 100 admitted rules, 24 of 102 with no home database, and 19.5% of flagged names traceable to a rule. That is a different research programme, not the next iteration of this one, and starting it by pretending it is R35 would be the same error R33 made about shape 3. Items 4–5 are registered work that changes no claim. Three items wait on a decision (6, 10, 11), two on an artefact that does not exist (7, 9), one on a toolchain (12). **Nothing on this page is waiting on an idea, and nothing is waiting on compute except items 4 and 10.**

**And §150 removed the item that was supposed to be next.** The critical path after §149 was "target the store"; the store turned out to be unprunable by evidence, and what survives is not a store question at all but a **usage** question — how many rules a prompt carries — with one number in its favour (+4.03pp [+0.76, +6.62] on 7,000 questions) and one condition against it (negative on every 350-question pilot, so its sign tracks the corpus). That is exactly the shape of question an arm answers and no further reading of committed artefacts can.

**And §153 closed the seventh route, by arithmetic rather than by argument.** The grain was the last design lever with a number behind it — the benchmark's own definitions are worth +17.01pp in the same slot where our rule pack costs −0.59pp — and it turns out not to be reachable: 547 corrections yielded 179 entries, those entries carried 13 distinct terms, and 13 terms reach 132 of 1,534 questions. A representation that renders on 8.6% of a split cannot be compared on that split, which the registration said *before* the run, so the outcome is inconclusive by feasibility. **§154 then measured the counterfactual that clause implied** — the corpus's own annotations are a store of definitions, and ranking their keys by the questions they reach shows the ceiling is 65.9% of the split and that the arm's 132 was within 1.83× of the 241 a store of its size could reach. The lever is therefore closed by a property of the corpus rather than by a construction defect, and the property has a name: **a corpus defines what it mentions once (mean density 0.967) and mentions without defining what it mentions often (0.077).** What a memory item is has now been varied as far as an object can be varied: its wording, its count, its filter, its audience, its payload, its cardinality, its type — and its type is bounded by arithmetic rather than by a null.

**One thing this list no longer contains, and it should be said plainly.** For twenty rounds the plan was "measure the mechanism, then scale it". The mechanism has now been measured, out of sample, and it is a cost: memory makes the product worse, the filter makes it no worse, and the combination is a wash. Every item above is downstream of accepting that, including the ones marked "mechanical".

**And §155 closed the last item that was waiting on a decision, by noticing that the decision was not
needed.** The arm-level audit had been deferred since R30 on the question *is an arm an artefact*; the answer
is that an arm is a column of a run, needs no validity schema, and needs only `(helped, harmed, n)` read
beside the difference the same sample could resolve. Doing that over the whole record puts a number on
something this page has asserted qualitatively for a dozen sections: **18 of 98 arm rows are decided, and
every decided row is larger than 4.5pp.** The record's small effects — the ones it has argued about — were
measured on designs whose median floor is 4.38pp at 350 questions and 2.07pp at 1,534, so they were never
measurable at the size they were measured. That does not overturn any number on this page and it does change
their standing: each is now published beside a price, from 352 questions at the cheap end to **1,457,294**
at the dear end, and a question that costs a million questions is a reason to stop rather than a plan.

**What is left is therefore four items and none of them is a decision.** Item 4 (the τ² cross-domain arm)
needs one dispatch and would test §138's claim that the protocol's *machinery*, not only its gates, is
scenario-agnostic. Item 5 (R27 stage 3) closed the move in §156 and turned the coupling table into a
gated reading: seven modules and 1,766 lines are the adapter, `core` is at zero, and a thirteenth coupled
module now fails the build until somebody writes down why it is not in `packages/sql`.
Item 8 (S1a) is an unblocked product feature. Item 12 (vitest 4) waits on the toolchain. Items 7 and 9 wait
on artefacts that do not exist, item 11 is excluded by the owner, and **item 10 is now answered in its own
terms**: the SOTA push is closed not because the levers ran out but because the instrument that would have to
detect the next lever resolves 2pp on the only corpus large enough to be worth measuring, and no lever in
this record has ever produced 2pp.

was dispatched to do: the store R41 never built existed. The evidence, from `arms/memory/poc-l4.json`:

| reading | R41 | R42 | what it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `learning.edited` | 32 of 32 (all refused) | **7** of 32 | the distiller answered; the *reader* could read 7 |
| `learning.distilled` | 0 | **14 items** | two candidates per correction |
| `learning.distillFailed` | 32 | **0** | the model name is translated at the endpoint |
| `learning.unanswered` | 32 (arithmetic) | **25** | retail's failures name no calls |
| `meanPackIds` | 0.00 | **0.00** | the façade served nothing, 200 times |
| `V1-pack-not-empty` | FAIL | **FAIL** | the same sentence for a different cause |
| `V32-fold-learning-intact` | absent | **FAIL, 25/32 (78.1%)** | the gap the reader created |
| `V8-call-reliability` | absent | pass, 0/7 calls | seven calls, none refused |
| `V44-domain-accounted` | pass on `0 <= 0` | **pass, 0 of 14 without a domain** | every item had one |
| `V15` / `V33` / `V17` | 72 informative, −5.00pp | **88 informative, +4.00pp** | 23 repaired, 15 broken, `unmeasured` |
| `V16` | FAIL, 72 < 100 | **FAIL, 88 < 100** | the scenario's easy episodes |
| `l4-paired` | −10.00pp, p = 0.18 | **+4.00pp, p = 0.6875**, n = 50 | 2 lost, 4 gained |
| `pass^4` | 0.36 / 0.46 | **0.44 / 0.40** | memory above reference, inside the interval |
| `V5-resolution` | 12.0pp | **13.73pp** | 6 discordant of 50, SE 4.90pp |

**The round's headline is not the +4pp.** It is that the arm called `memory` received no memory on any of
its 200 requests, and the record carried both halves of that fact in fields that could not be read
together: fourteen items in `domainOrigin.storedWithDomain`, and `0.00 rules/question` in `meanPackIds`.
`V44` was quiet because every item carried a domain — a *wrong* domain is still a domain — and `V1` had no
population to report, so its sentence could not say which of three zeros it was.

**Two defects, both about a key rather than a mechanism.** First, the domain on every claim was the
model's spelling: `parseScope` takes `task` from the event and `domain` from the model's JSON, the prompt
forbids a guess and nothing validates one, and `MemoryStore.search` filters on `scope.domain` equality
while the façade asks in the host's spelling. A claim stored as `Retail (US)` is active, counted, ledged
and unreachable. `stampDomain` gives the key to the host — the only party that observed the scenario — on
both branches of the fallback, and the suite holds the experiment in two halves so the claim is a test.

Second, two thirds of the failures had nothing to teach, and the reason was the reader: τ²'s `retail`
domain states `nl_assertions` and names no calls, and `taskCorrection` read `actions` only. `TauTask`
now carries the prose rubric, `taskCorrection` falls back to it, and `teachingOf` stays the single
decision so the corrections and the unanswered ledger cannot disagree. The prediction for R43 is `edited`
7 → 32 and `unanswered` 25 → 0.

**What R43 does not do is move a bar.** `V5` grades 5pp against a scenario whose whole population is 50
paired tasks — `tasksForFivePp` is 185 at R42's discordance, and airline has 50 — so no dispatch of this
lane can meet it. Moving the bar needs a registration field and its own round, and taking it in the same
round that first delivers the treatment would make the treatment and its bar one decision. `R43-rubric`
registers that expectation explicitly, in the `V5` and `V16` predictions.

**Where the project stands.** Two rounds have been spent repairing the instrument, and the mechanism has
still not been measured with a pack in the prompt. That is now one dispatch away, and the census R43
records makes the next reading self-explaining: `served = 200` is delivery, `served = 0` with
`servable > 0` moves the subject to the façade, and `servable = 0` keeps it in the store. Gates at the
time of writing: **2,883 tests across 137 files, 99.98 / 99.70 / 100 / 99.98**, `pnpm check` exit 0.

**Correction (2026-11-04).** Two sentences in this section misdescribe the corpus, and one invents a
status. The domains' shapes are the other way round: `retail` names calls on 112 of 114 tasks and states
prose on 8, `airline` states prose on all 50 (§17.83 counts the files). The status breakdown quoted above
— "fourteen items, 14 active" — is in no artefact: R42's record had no store census at all, so the only
status claim the evidence supports is R43's, and it is `24 stored, 0 active`. See §159 for the readback
and §34.17 for the audit.

## 159 — The learner worked, the store admitted nothing, and the corpus was counted for the first time

**R43 answered the question it was dispatched to answer, and the answer moved the defect one layer in.**
The learner reads every failure it can read: `learning.unanswered` **25 → 0**, `learning.edited` **7 → 12**,
and `V32-fold-learning-intact` **passes for the first time in this lane** at `0/32 unanswered (0.0%), 12
correction(s), 0 distillation failure(s) (0.0%)`. The store is not empty either — 24 items. And the pack is
still empty: `store.active` **0**, `store.servable` **0**, `recall` **1,518 requests, 0 served**,
`meanPackIds` **0.00**.

| reading | R42 | R43 | what it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `learning.edited` | 7 | **12** | every failed training task taught something |
| `learning.unanswered` | 25 | **0** | no failure was left without a lesson |
| `V32-fold-learning-intact` | FAIL 78.1% | **pass 0.0%** | the reader defect is closed |
| `distilled` / `distillFailed` | 14 / 0 | **24 / 0** | two candidates per correction |
| `store.stored / active / servable` | 14 / — / — | **24 / 0 / 0** | the store filled and admitted nothing |
| `recall.requests / served` | 200 / 0 | **1,518 / 0** | asked 1,518 times, served nothing |
| `V1-pack-not-empty` | FAIL, bare | **FAIL**, bare | the population was dropped between file and record |
| `V44-domain-accounted` | pass 0/14 | pass **0/24** | every item carries the host's spelling |
| `V15-transfer-reconciles` | 88 informative | **76 informative**, 124 retried, 0 unmeasured | the ledger reconciles |
| `V17-transfer-net-reported` | +4.00pp | **−1.50pp** (18 repaired, 21 broken), `unmeasured` | a direction, not a rate |
| `l4-paired` | +4.00pp, p = 0.6875 | **−4.00pp**, p = 0.7905, n = 50 | the arm had no memory to measure |
| `pass^4` | 0.44 / 0.40 | **0.38 / 0.42** | memory below reference, both inside noise |
| `V5-resolution` | FAIL 13.73pp | **FAIL 20.97pp** | 8 lost, 6 gained of 50 |
| `scenarioTasks` | — | **learn 114 / test 50** | the lane's own count, agreeing with the census |

**Three predictions held and two were refuted, and the refutations are the reading.** Held: `unanswered`
→ 0, `V32` passing, the bar unmoved. Refuted: `edited` 7 → 32 was 12, because the prediction assumed
every training task fails and twenty of thirty-two passed (a pass teaches nothing by design); and `V8`
firing on ≥32 calls was 12, because a correction is one distiller call. Both were written down before the
run, which is what makes them readable as refutations rather than as surprises.

**The corpus was counted, and the count corrected three published sentences.** A new instrument
(`label-census.ts`, `pnpm eval:label-census`, a step in the L4 job that runs before either arm) counts the
labels at the pinned ref and prints them into the same evidence bundle as the delta:

| corpus | tasks | names calls | states prose | both | states neither | declares a basis | graded on `ACTION` | graded on `NL_ASSERTION` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `retail` | 114 | 112 (98.2%) | 8 (7.0%) | 8 | 2 (1.8%) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `airline` | 50 | 43 (86.0%) | 50 (100%) | 43 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The corrections it forced: the two scenarios' shapes were published the wrong way round; "25 of 32 had
nothing to teach" cannot be a corpus fact when 2 of 114 tasks state neither form (it was the driver's
`train.length - corrections.length` arithmetic); and retail's population is 114 tasks in the file, not the
115 upstream advertises for the split. All three are in `AUDIT §34.17`, and the corpus is now printed
beside the run rather than recalled after it.

**Two instrument defects, found by reading R43's own artefacts.** `tau2ArmRecordOf` maps an arm's file into
the record the projection reads, and it did not name `store` or `recall`, so the census was in the file and
absent from the record — which is why the pair report printed `V1`'s pre-R43 bare sentence while the arm
held `24 / 0 / 0` and `1,518 / 0`. Two tests hold the mapping now, and `V1`'s layered sentence is asserted
at the projection level. The second is the one that decides R44: `candidate` is what three different
decisions in `decideStatus` write, so a status histogram cannot distinguish them. `storeCensus` now carries
a histogram of `statusReason`, and the driver prints it ranked on its one line about the store.

**A hypothesis was excluded by measurement rather than by argument.** The obvious suspect for 24 candidates
is the evidence payload: the driver has no transcript of the failed episode, so it states the completion as
the reference call names and the edit as those names with their arguments, and `trustFor('edit')` derives
trust from how far that edit moved the completion against `minSupport` 0.8. A three-condition test — the
driver's own shape, a rubric-only correction, and a call correction against a completion naming a different
call — clears the floor in all three at 0.9. The test is committed as the guard that keeps the hypothesis
from being re-asserted, and R44 is registered to read the reason instead of guessing a repair.

**Where the project stands.** Three rounds have each found the delivery defect one layer deeper: R41 had no
store, R42 had a store with the model's keys, R43 has a store with the host's keys and no admission. The
mechanism has still not been measured with a pack in the prompt, and this round's explicit conclusion is
that it cannot be until something is `active`. On the leaderboard axis nothing moved: memory 0.38 against
reference 0.42 is fifth of six named entries, and the only column this project leads is the one that says
whether the treatment arrived.

Gates at the time of writing: **2,909 tests across 138 files, 99.98 / 99.70 / 100 / 99.98**, `pnpm check`
exit 0; `label-census.ts` and `tau2-gates.ts` at 100 on all four dimensions. Commits this round:
`0028dd6` (the census), `25acfc8` (the call list is the target state, not an unread label), `e0b5562`
(three comments repeating a count the corpus cannot produce), `e58c082` (seven tasks state prose alone),
`eb0219f` (the bytes travel with the counts), `2db9fb8` (the record dropped the census), `82b2b41` (one
status, three decisions), `8649563` (what the evidence shape does *not* explain), `dccbb3d` (R44
registered). **R44 dispatched** as run `41872858497` on `dccbb3d`, `prereg=R44-admission`.

## 160 — The reason has a name, and the name points at the evidence, not the threshold

**R44 read.** Run `41872858497` on `dccbb3d` completed on 2026-11-04; its `l4-evidence` artefact
(`13350877140`, 20,276,079 bytes) carries the full pair, both arms, the corpus census and the gate
report. The job's conclusion is `failure`, and the reason is the scientific gates, not the build:
`ci.yml` run `41872680757` on the same head is `success`. Four blocking gates read FAIL — `V1`
(pack empty), `V5` (resolution), `V16` (transfer resolvable) and `l4-paired` (not significant) —
and `l4-pair.ts` exits 1 on a blocking failure. Red here means *the treatment did not arrive and was
not significant*; it does not mean a broken pipeline. The distinction is recorded rather than
smoothed over, and no `continue-on-error` or `|| true` is involved.

| reading | R43 | R44 | what it says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `learning.edited` | 12 | **10** | two more training tasks passed; a pass teaches nothing by design |
| `learning.unanswered` | 0 | **0** | no failure left unread |
| `store.stored / active / servable` | 24 / 0 / 0 | **19 / 0 / 0** | one item per candidate, none admitted |
| `store.reasons` | not instrumented | **`insufficient-evidence=19`** | the round's deliverable: populated and dominated by one key |
| `recall.requests / served` | 1,518 / 0 | **1,427 / 0** | the façade was still asked per step and served nothing |
| `V1-pack-not-empty` | FAIL, bare rate | **FAIL, with population**: `0 of 1427 request(s) … from a store of 19 (0 active, 0 in scope)` | the `store`/`recall` forwarding fix reached the sentence |
| `V32-fold-learning-intact` | pass 0/32 | **pass 0/32**, 10 corrections, 0 distillation failures | no reader was touched |
| `V5-resolution` | FAIL 20.97pp | **FAIL 19.41pp** | no bar moved |
| `l4-paired` | −4.00pp, p = 0.7905 | **+12.00pp** [−2.00, 26.00], p = 0.1460, n = 50, lost 3 / gained 9 | not significant, and the sign flipped |
| `pass^4` memory / reference | 0.38 / 0.42 | **0.52 / 0.40** | two samples of the *same* untreated condition, 14pp apart |
| `V17-transfer-net-reported` | −1.50pp, `unmeasured` | **+7.00pp**, 22 repaired / 8 broken, `unmeasured` | a direction, not a rate |
| `V44-domain-accounted` | pass 0/24 | **pass 0/19** | every item carries the host's domain |

**Predictions.** Five of the six registered predictions held: the histogram was populated and dominated
by `insufficient-evidence`, with `needs-corroboration` and `contradiction-budget-exceeded` on none;
`V1` printed its population; `V32` stayed at 0/32; `V5` failed and no bar moved; `l4-paired` stayed
insignificant with an unpredicted sign. The sixth — that the learning half is unchanged — held in
shape (0 unanswered, 0 distillation failures) but not in count: 10 corrections and 19 items rather
than 12 and 24, because the training episode is a live model call and twenty-two of thirty-two tasks
passed this time. Two runs of one untreated condition moving `pass^4` from 0.38 to 0.52 is the
quantified noise floor, and it is the reason the round refuses to quote +12.00pp as a finding.

**The reason is not the end of the diagnosis.** `insufficient-evidence` is written by two branches of
`decideStatus` — `confidence < activationThreshold` (0.6) and `support < minSupport` (0.8) — and R44's
histogram cannot separate them. Rather than spend a second dispatch instrumenting the split, the
decision was reproduced offline on the *real* corpus and the *real* kernel: the retail task file the
workflow censused (sha256 `76e1fa64…`, 328,166 bytes) and `diffJson` → `trustFor` → `scoreKnowledge`
→ `decideStatus`, with no model call and no mock. The driver records a failed episode as the reference
call **names** and the correction as those names **with their arguments**; `editDistance` counts
`ops / (leaves(before) + leaves(after))`, so a tool with many arguments dilutes the distance. Measured
over the 32-task learn split: `distance` 0.1707–0.3333, `trust` 0.5000–0.9000, mean 0.7695,
`confidence` 0.2713–0.6165, mean 0.4613, and **31 of 32 items held as candidates**. The guard test
written in R43 used one action with empty arguments; it cleared at 0.9, and it was measuring a shape
the corpus does not contain.

**Why confidence, and not support, is the failing half.** `createLlmInterpreter` sets
`candidate.evidence.weight = trust` and `candidate.trust = trust`, so `scoreKnowledge`'s
`logOdds += weight × logit(trust)` becomes `trust × logit(trust)` — a quadratic penalty. The measured
threshold is `trust = 0.89` (`confidence = 0.6013`); `support` clears 0.8 at `trust = 0.8`, but
`confidence` at that point is only 0.4806. Of the 32 items, 16 have `support ≥ 0.8` and
`confidence < 0.6`, 15 have `support < 0.8`, and 1 has `confidence ≥ 0.6`.

**The ablation that selects the repair** (32 real tasks, real kernel, five conditions):

| condition | active / 32 | mean trust | mean confidence | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A — current structural distance | **1** | 0.7695 | 0.4613 | the measured defect |
| B — gold-verified semantic distance (1.0) | **32** | 0.9000 | 0.6165 | the repair |
| C — `activationThreshold` 0.6 → 0.45 | 17 | 0.7695 | 0.4613 | wrong lever: admits weak evidence |
| D — `minSupport` 0.8 → 0.5 | **1** | 0.7695 | 0.4613 | no change: support was never the block |
| E — `singleObservationTrust` → 0.99 | **1** | 0.7695 | 0.4613 | no change: contradiction path only |

R44's registered refutation branch said that if confidence is the failing half, the round after reads
`scoreKnowledge`'s weights. The measurement refines it: the weights are not wrong, the **input** is. A
τ² correction is `gold`-verified by `evaluation_criteria.actions`, so its evidential strength comes
from the verifier, not from how many leaves the edit moved. `openMicroglia`'s `editSemantics` hook is the
architectural place to say so (the chart pack uses it for the same reason), and R45 is registered to
wire it, TDD-first, with the census extended to item-level `trust`/`support`/`confidence` so the next
dispatch verifies the claim rather than repeating it.

**What the literature says about the negative effect.** Three independent lines now agree with the
user's hypothesis that the *content* and the *use* of memory, not its quantity, cause the harm. Xiong
et al., [arXiv:2505.16067](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16067) (ACL 2026), name `experience-following`
and its two failure modes — error propagation and misaligned experience replay — and measure a ~10pp
absolute gain from **selective addition plus combined deletion** over naive memory growth. IBM's own
2026-10-20 ALTK-Evolve report is the sharpest competitor datum: on airline, the 101-rule `lossless`
prompt scores **40.0%** Pass^4 while the 14-rule `sup3` core (rules seen in ≥ 3 tasks) scores **45.0%** —
*more memory reduced reliability*. Yu et al., [arXiv:2608.10502](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10502),
measure dependency-guided rollback repair at 85.3% recovery versus 77.3% for an LLM-judge, preserving
all benign memories. `COMPETITIVE` L.5 carries the full comparison.

**Ranking, and why it did not move.** The SOTA remains IBM Research's `gpt-5.5` airline submission at
**82.0** Pass^4 (unverified, modified prompt, PR #551); SapientAI-Agent-Opus-5 is 72.0; IBM's
`gpt-4.1 sup3` is 44.0 at #8; stock `gpt-oss-120b` is 34.0. microglia's R44 arms read 52.0 / 40.0 and
R43's read 38.0 / 42.0 — all four are samples of a **condition with zero served items**, so none is a
ranking claim and the entry stays **fifth of six named entries** on the table in L.4. The only column
this project leads is still "whether the treatment was delivered", and it currently reads `0 served`.

**Where the project stands.** Four rounds have each found the delivery defect one layer deeper: R41 no

## 162 — The competitor we cannot copy, and the use-side population we counted before the readback

**The round.** R45 run `42131391874` is still measuring on pinned head
`26f7c3f0`. As in §161, no file in `microglia` was changed and no second
workflow was dispatched. The round answered a direct question about IBM
Research's learned guidelines, read four more first-hand sources on the negative
effect, read three competitor implementations at source, and counted the
use-side population on real corpus bytes before the readback. All of it changes
no number the run will report.

**The answer, in one paragraph.** The mechanism is replicable and has been read
at source (`COMPETITIVE` L.6); IBM's 82.0 is not a replicable object — two
unverified PRs with disclosed modified prompts, a different agent model, a
train/base split overlap, 20 airline tasks where one task is 5pp, and two
different quantities (70.0 held-out versus 82.0 full base) behind one headline;
and under this project's rules a SOTA benchmark must run through `sota.yml`,
report whether the treatment arrived, and isolate contributions by ablation.
The competitor's own airline result — 101 lossless rules at 40.0 against 14
`sup3` rules at 45.0, **more memory, −5pp** — is the datum that supports the
project's thesis, not the 82.0. `COMPETITIVE` L.8 carries the twelve-item
argument, the minimal attributable reproduction protocol and the unchanged
ranking.

**Four more sources, all read at first hand.** AECG
([arXiv:2610.05176](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05176)) names `memory pollution`
and **`scope collapse`** and measures up to 16.89pp lost when scope preservation
is removed; its declared code repository returned 404 and a repository search
returned zero results, which is recorded rather than filled. Tether
([arXiv:2610.25123](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25123)) shows that a memory can
be correct when written and unsafe when used (62% of upstream-failing objects
published by fact memory, 0.3% by Tether). MemPABench
([arXiv:2610.30485](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30485)) reports that Mem0, MemOS
and simple RAG **do not outperform No Memory**. AMV-Guard
([arXiv:2610.31446](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31446)) makes verification a
property of the action about to be taken, not of the entry (−33.9% cost at 100%
safe-proceed recall on ToolSandbox). Together with Xiong's deletion rule —
delete only after the memory has been retrieved and its mean downstream L2
exceeds a threshold — the field now says the same thing from four directions:
**the negative effect lives in what is admitted and in how it is used, and the
use side needs a feedback signal, not a better store.**

**A code-level defect found offline, and two hypotheses rejected first.**
`scopeMatches` filters on `domain` only when the item has a domain; a widened
item (`domain === undefined`) is deliberately allowed to travel. `stampDomain`
unconditionally stamps every τ² item with the learn domain, so
`generalizationPlan` can never produce a widened item; the driver compensates by
pointing the recall filter at the store's domain. Measured on the pinned
32-item retail set with the real kernel: **32/32 items pass the scope filter**,
`minCoverage = 0` makes all of them injection candidates, and 75.88% of the
1,600 (airline question, retail rule) pairs have zero content-term overlap
against 20.77% in the within-domain control. Two structural proxies bracket the
real LLM statements; the direction is claimed, the magnitude and any accuracy
effect are not. `AUDIT` §34.23 has the table and the two rejected hypotheses;
`TECH-DESIGN` §17.89 registers U1–U3 as use-side arms for after the readback.
No result is claimed before `42131391874` reports.

**Where the project stands, and what is left in order.** (1) **R45 readback** —
watcher polling, `store.active`, `servable`, `recall.served`, `meanPackIds`,
`V1`, admission means, `l4-paired`. (2) **Revert rule** — if a served pack is
significantly negative or below −5pp, revert on the reading. (3) **Use-side
census on real distilled statements**, then U3 and R46 as registered in §17.89.
(4) **R46 admission-rule ablation**, three arms, one store, one preregistration,
with the `>= 2` contrast registered separately. (5) transcript V46/V47.
(6) S1a, then S1b. (7) `sota.ts` split and `eval-sql` move. (8) W8 dose curve.
(9) vitest 4 migration, deliberately last. **cortex release excluded.**
Acceptance on every step: TDD, real tests, no mocks, ≥ 95% per dimension,
`ci.yml` green, both repositories pushed as Lambertyan.

**Ranking.** SOTA is still IBM `gpt-5.5` airline **82.0** (unverified, modified
prompt, PR #551); SapientAI 72.0; IBM `gpt-4.1 sup3` 44.0 (#8); stock
`gpt-oss-120b` 34.0; microglia **fifth of six named entries**, all four
published arms from a zero-served condition. The only column this project leads
is whether the treatment was delivered, and it still reads `0 served` until the
readback.

## 163 — The first treatment arrived, six predictions held, and the artefact could not say what was in the pack

**Run `42131391874` reported on 2026-11-06.** Its `sota.yml` conclusion is
`failure` on three blocking scientific gates (`V5-resolution`,
`V16-transfer-resolvable`, `l4-paired`); `ci.yml` on the pinned head `26f7c3f0`
is green. The failure is a measurement, not a build: the review of the job log
shows the L4 arm ran to completion, both arms scored 50 tasks at `k=4`, and the
pairing step exited 1 because the registered gates refuse to certify an
underpowered result. This is the same distinction §160 recorded for R44.

**The delivery gap closed, exactly as the R45 pre-registration predicted.** The
admission repair (`tau2EditSemantics`, shipped in `b88623e` / remote `c65468f0`/
`26f7c3f0`) turned every gold-verified correction into full-semantic evidence.
All six registered predictions were read from the artefact, not inferred:

| prediction (prereg/R45-admission.md) | reading | held |
|---|---|---|
| `store.active > 0`, `store.servable > 0` | 21 / 21 | yes |
| `statuses.candidate` falls from 19 to near zero | 0 (reasons `confidence-cleared=21`) | yes |
| admission means `0.9000 / 0.9000 / 0.6165`, `supportOnly=0` | `0.9000 / 0.9000 / 0.6165`, `supportOnly=0` | yes, to four decimals |
| `recall.served > 0`, `meanPackIds > 0` | 1480 / 1480 served, 0 empty, `meanPackIds=1.839` | yes |
| `V1-pack-not-empty` passes | PASS, `1.84 rules/question` | yes |
| `V32` stays 0/32, `V8` reliable, `V5` still fails | V32 0/32, V8 0.00% (0/11), V5 FAIL 18.59pp | yes |
| `l4-paired` not predicted | `+6.00pp [-6, +20] p=0.5488, n=50` | honestly unregistered |

Five of six predictions held and the sixth was deliberately left unregistered;
the R44 offline reproduction (`trust=0.9`, `confidence=0.6165`) is now confirmed
by a live dispatch. The transfer ledger reports 22 repaired / 17 broken of 200
measured trials, net `+2.50pp`, verdict `unmeasured`; `V16` fails at 86
informative trials against a floor of 100.

**The revert rule does not fire.** The registered rule reverts only if a served
pack makes `l4-paired` significantly negative or below −5pp. The reading is
positive, non-significant, and above −5pp. R44's `+12.00pp` with an empty pack
and R45's `+6.00pp` with a served pack are both samples of a lane whose minimum
detectable difference is 18.59pp; neither is an effect. `AUDIT` §34.24 carries
the full gate table and the reason the run is red while the code is green.

**The finding this round.** `V44-domain-accounted` reports `0 of 21 items with
no domain, 0 unscoped, 0 widened`, and the scenario is
`learn=retail / test=airline / recall=retail`: 21 retail-learned rules were
injected into airline questions on every one of 1480 requests. But the arm
record counts only *how many* items were served and the rewards that followed;
it never records *which* statements were injected or whether any shared a
content term with the question. `V1` grades the size and is silent on the
content, so `+6.00pp` cannot distinguish "the experiment is underpowered" from
"the delivered pack was mostly about a different domain". That distinction is
the user's standing hypothesis, and §34.23 measured it offline on structural
proxies (75.88% of cross-domain pairs have zero lexical overlap against 20.77%
within-domain).

**R46 ships the instrument, not an arm.** `packages/eval/src/tau2-use-census.ts`
implements the `UseCensus` shape registered in `TECH-DESIGN` §17.89 verbatim
(seven fields), plus a derived `coverageProfile`. It is wired to the driver's
recall facade as pure observation: the recall scope, the `minCoverage` floor and
the pack contents are exactly as R45 ran them. TDD — the failing test came
first on the pinned 32-task fixture with the real `queryCoverage`/`tokenize`
kernel, no mocks and no model call; 9 census tests, 3 `armRecordFromDriver`
tests and 1 gate-projection round-trip test. `AUDIT` §34.24 records why an
instrument that changes no number is the correct next step, and why U1–U3 stay
closed until a dispatch reports the census on **real distilled statements**
rather than proxies.

**Ranking is unchanged.** IBM `gpt-5.5` airline **82.0** (unverified, modified
prompt, PR #551) is still the SOTA; SapientAI 72.0; IBM `gpt-4.1 sup3` 44.0
(#8); stock `gpt-oss-120b` 34.0; microglia still **fifth of six named
entries**. R45's memory arm scored `pass^4 0.42` and the reference `0.36`; the

The column this project leads — whether the treatment was delivered — now reads

## 166 — The census came back with one prediction falsified, and a scalar that could not grade its own floor

**The run finished.** `sota.yml` run `42317807270` on `cb329054` completed at

succeeded; step 13 `Pair the arms` exited 1 on `V5` (MDE 13.73pp), `V16` (81
informative trials) and `l4-paired` (`0.00pp [-10, +10] p=1.0000`). That is a
resolution verdict, not a build failure — `ci.yml` on the same head is green,
and every validity gate R45 passed passes again.

**Five of six predictions held.** The `use` block is present on the memory arm
and absent on the reference; `1512 / 1512` requests served; `injectedPairs
3016 = 1.9947 x 1512` exactly; `widenedItems 0`; all validity gates green.
The falsified one is the magnitude of the coverage prediction: the
pre-registered `zeroCoverageShare > 0.5` reads **0.3896** (`1175 / 3016`) on
real distilled statements. The offline structural proxy said 0.7588
cross-domain and 0.2077 within-domain. A proxy is not the distilled
statement — the second time this project has measured the fact (§34.22). The
direction survives and it is the first hard number for the standing use-side
hypothesis: 39 percent of what the model was shown shared no content term
with the question it was answering. No refutation fires, and `0.00pp` does not
trigger R45's revert rule.

**Two runs, one configuration, two answers.** R45 measured `+6.00pp
[-6, +20] p=0.5488` with 21 active items; R46 measured `0.00pp [-10, +10]
p=1.0000` with 14, both non-significant, both with an MDE above 13pp, and both
arms now at `pass^4 0.46`. The distiller is an LLM call, so the learning half
is nondeterministic and the store population drifts between identical
dispatches. This is a direct reading of the noise floor, not a claim about
either delta.

**The defect we found by reading the artefact.** TECH-DESIGN §17.89 makes a
"committed histogram" the P0 prerequisite for U3's floor. R46 committed none:
`armRecordFromDriver` reduced the raw observations to seven scalars and threw
the pairs away, and `coverageProfile` / `zeroCoverageShare` had no production
caller. One scalar cannot say what a non-zero `minCoverage` floor would empty.
A real-kernel offline probe on the pinned fixture measured two populations with
the identical scalar whose retained fractions at `minCoverage = 0.05` differ by
12.44pp, and a post-floor served population spread over a 33.24pp interval.
This is the use-side twin of §34.22 — a threshold about to be applied to a
population nobody counted.

retention curve (pack-level `retainedPacks` / `emptiedPacks`), non-zero coverage
quantiles and separately-reported content-free queries, computed in
`armRecordFromDriver` and projected to the gate layer. The seven-field
`UseCensus` is unchanged and the field is optional, so R45, R46 and every older
artefact read as "not measured". No gate reads it; `packages/core`,
`sota.yml`, the driver and `l4-pair` are untouched. Seven failing tests were
written first, including a real-kernel regression proving two populations with
identical registered fields produce different histograms. `pnpm check` exits 0:

ledger moved structurally (37,746 -> 37,883 lines) and is committed; six
timing-only result files were restored.

## 168 — The competitors measured the same harm, and a structure-only floor became measurable

**State on resume.** R47 (run `42337250684`) was dispatched on `bc0a39eb` after
`ci.yml` `42336894395` went green on 44 steps. On resume the L4 job had
completed the memory arm and entered the reference arm (step 12 of 19); the
BIRD and retrieval-probe jobs were correctly skipped by `bird=false` and
`probe=false`. The first watcher had died silently at `04:21Z` with the log
frozen; a fresh watcher was started and confirmed alive. No `microglia` source
was touched: section 34.21's rule that a pinned dispatch is a measurement in
progress was applied again, so this round's work is documentation, first-party
source study and an offline probe.

**The hypothesis got independent, quantified support.** IBM's own ALTK-Evolve
ablation is the sharpest reading: on held-out airline tasks with `gpt-4.1`, 14
high-support guidelines give Pass^4 45.0 percent while all 101 guidelines give
40.0 percent, even though the larger set raises Mean Accuracy from 60.0 to
65.0. More memory lowered reliability by 5.0 points in the system that holds
the SOTA. Five further benchmarks converge: MemSyco-Bench attributes 61 to 62
percent of errors to post-retrieval use; OP-Bench measures 26.2 to 61.1 percent
drops against a memory-free baseline; MemCalib's best frontier model scores SCS
46.25 and Exact 28.40 of 100 on calibrated use; BenchPreS sees misapplication
up to 86.48 percent; RPEval finds models at 0.06 to 0.38 on Ignore where humans
reach 0.86. The recurring shape is over-use, a trade of one error for another
under prompt fixes, and distortion introduced by compression. Full tables and
caveats are in `AUDIT.md` section 34.30.

**First-party code was read, not summarised from a press post.**
`Quark-Medical/memcalib` was inspected through the GitHub trees API:
`recipe/memcalib_credit/metrics.py` defines `scs = 0.5 ** (over_budget +
under_budget)`, `credit.py` implements eight merged channels with ordered
bidirectional localisation, and `segments.py` produces exactly covering token
groups. RSCB-MC's asymmetric abstention rule and FinAcumen's calibrated
relevance threshold were mapped onto the project's `COVERAGE_FLOORS` curve. The
design consequence is in `TECH-DESIGN.md` section 17.95: a floor scored by
`alpha * relevant - gamma * falsePos - beta * abstained`, with
`gamma > alpha > beta`, decided from the committed histogram alone.

**A real-kernel probe made that rule testable.** On the fingerprinted fixture
(32 statements x 50 airline queries), the pure asymmetric cost peaks at the
same plateau `[0.01, 0.02, 0.03]` under all three cost orderings, because the
smallest positive coverage is 0.0345. All 9 positive rungs empty at least one
pack. The probe also measured that the offline proxy's `zeroShare = 0.7588`
overstates R46's real `0.3896` by 36.92 points — a measured explanation of
R46's falsified fourth prediction. It reported `FLOOR_SELECTED = false`: R47's
refutation forbids a floor from accuracy or from this proxy.

**What is next, in order.** P0: read R47's `l4-evidence`, verify the eight
structural predictions and six refutations, and confirm the three reconciliation
identities. P1: compute U3's floor from the committed curve, register a
tie-break rule and the cost weights before its own dispatch, and keep `V1`
blocking. P1: R46's admission-rule ablation with at least two comparators.
P2: U1 calibration and U2, then transcript and S1 work. P3: `sota.ts` split,
W8 dose curve and the vitest 4 migration, deliberately last. Section 34.21's
head-still rule is lifted only after R47 is read back. Ranking is unchanged:
IBM `gpt-5.5` airline 82.0 remains the SOTA, microglia fifth of six named
entries.

## 169 — R47 read back, a floor computed from structure, and U3 registered

**The head-still rule is lifted on a reading, not on a hope.** R47 (run
`42337250684`, dispatched on `bc0a39eb`) completed as `completed failure`
because the `Pair the arms` step refused to certify an underpowered paired
measurement; step 15 `Upload evidence` succeeded, with artefact `13562407896`
(`l4-evidence`, 20,276,573 bytes, 92 entries). The readback found all eight
structural predictions **HOLD**, all three reconciliation identities holding,
all six refutations clear, no revert rule fired, and `U3_ELIGIBLE = true`.
`V1-pack-not-empty` passed at 1.47 rules per question across 1491 of 1491
requests; `V5-resolution` failed at an MDE of 17.72pp, `V16-transfer-resolvable`
failed at 92 informative trials with 22 repairs, and `l4-paired` failed at
`12.00pp [0.00, 24.00] p=0.1094 n=50` with 2 lost and 8 gained. Those three
red gates are the lane refusing to certify a measurement inside its own noise
floor, not a build failure; `ci.yml` stayed green on 44 steps.

**The committed population.** The seven-field `use` census read
`recallRequests 1491`, `recallServed 1491`, `meanPackIds 1.46747`,
`injectedPairs 2188`, `zeroCoveragePairs 750`, `widenedItems 0`, so
`zeroCoverageShare = 0.3428`. The `coverage` histogram read
`measuredPairs 2180`, `unmeasurablePairs 8`, `unmeasurablePacks 8`, with
non-zero quantiles `min 0.01695`, `p10 0.02273`, `p25 0.02778`,
`p50 0.04545`, `p75 0.07692`, `p90 0.16667`, `max 0.33333`. The retention
curve, in `retainedPairs / retainedPacks / emptiedPacks` order, was
`0: 2180/1483/0`, `0.01: 1438/1069/414`, `0.02: 1395/1034/449`,
`0.03: 981/797/686`, `0.05: 680/523/960`, `0.08: 335/210/1273`,
`0.1: 265/158/1325`, `0.15: 169/95/1388`, `0.2: 129/70/1413`,
`0.3: 2/1/1482`. The identities `2180 + 8 = 2188` and
`1483 + 0 + 8 = 1491` held at every rung, the zero rung retained all measured
pairs and emptied nothing, and all nine positive rungs emptied at least one
pack. The grid therefore has pack-level resolving power and U3 can be
registered from this curve.

**An empirical correction to section 17.95.** The offline probe had called the
structure-only cost rule "robust to all three cost orderings" because on the
proxy corpus the smallest positive coverage was 0.0345 and the rungs `0.01`,
`0.02`, `0.03` tied. The real committed curve is **not** cost-robust. With
`net(f) = alpha * relevant(f) - gamma * falsePos(f) - beta * abstained(f)`,
the false-positive-averse ordering (`alpha=1, gamma=3, beta=0.5`) and the
symmetric ordering (`alpha=1, gamma=1, beta=0.5`) both select `0.01` at
`net = 1231.0`, while the abstention-averse ordering
(`alpha=1, gamma=0.5, beta=3`) selects `0`, the as-is configuration, at
`net = 1067.0`. A tie set on the proxy was an artefact of the proxy, not a
property of the rule. The correction is implemented, not merely noted:
`CostWeights` has no default anywhere, the weights and tie-break must be
registered before the dispatch, and a test asserts the disagreement on the
real artefact.

**U3's decision, TDD-first on a fingerprinted real artefact.** The committed
`coverage` and `use` pair was saved as
`eval/fixtures/tau2-r47-coverage-histogram.json` (2239 bytes, sha256
`33d2006acb8d0c66fa732d16a5e0d42f5c26370efc65def01857a0371c3f5b9c`). A failing
test was written first against a module that did not exist, then
`packages/eval/src/u3-decision.ts` was implemented. `decideFloor` takes only
the histogram, the census and required weights; it refuses a wrong grid, a
broken pair or pack population, a broken zero rung, inverted quantiles, a
negative measurable zero-coverage count and a non-monotone retention curve.
It returns one cost row per rung and uses the registered least-aggressive
tie-break. 21 of 21 tests pass on the real fixture, with no mock.

**U3's application path, also TDD-first.** A floor that is computed but never
applied would make the arm a second copy of the as-is run. The wiring was
added in five places, each with a real test where coverage is measured:
`tau2-recall-floor.ts` exports `AS_IS_FLOOR`, the registered
`U3_COST_WEIGHTS`, `resolveRecallFloor` (an unset variable is the as-is zero;
any set value must be a rung of `COVERAGE_FLOORS` and a refusal, never a
silent clamp) and `committedFloor`; `prereg.ts` accepts an optional
`recallFloor` header, so all 35 earlier registrations stay valid and the
count is 36 of 36; `prereg-floor.ts` recomputes a declared floor from the
committed R47 curve and refuses a mismatch; the recall facade in
`tau2-driver.ts` passes `minCoverage` to `host.recall`; and `sota.yml` reads
the floor from the run's own pre-registration into `TAU_MIN_COVERAGE` on the
memory arm only. The dispatch menu is at GitHub's 25-input limit, so the
floor could not be added there even if that were scientifically acceptable.
10 new tests cover the resolver and the recomputation.

**R48 is the registration, and it is fixed before the dispatch.**
`prereg/R48-u3-coverage-floor.md` declares `recallFloor: 0.01`, the cost
weights `alpha=1, gamma=3, beta=0.5` with `gamma > alpha > beta`, and the
least-aggressive tie-break. It names the one behavioural difference from
R47, fixes eight structural predictions (the floor reaches the facade,
zero-coverage injection falls, packs are emptied while `V1` still passes,
the identities hold, earlier gates hold, the declared floor is recomputed,
and the two memory arms are comparable) and seven refutations. It explicitly
does **not** predict the sign, magnitude or significance of `l4-paired`, and
forbids using any accuracy number to select or revise the floor. R47's
`0.01` rung emptied 414 of 1491 served packs (27.77 percent); that cost is
registered as a first-class outcome, not hidden behind an accuracy delta.

**Verification.** `pnpm check` exit 0 with the new sources, `pnpm eval:prereg`

## 170 — An infrastructure failure, a lawful retry, and five sources on the dose of memory

**What happened.** Iteration 169 dispatched U3 as run `42350304597` on
`33038232`. This iteration read it back and found `completed failure`, but the
failure was not R47's scientific-gate red at `Pair the arms`: steps 12 and 13,
the two arms themselves, failed. The cause is external and unambiguous. The
job log for `128336818209` shows `TAU_MIN_COVERAGE: 0.01` injected at line 627
and step 11 `Read the registered recall floor` succeeding, so the new wiring
works on a real runner. The retail learn phase (`run_split.py --domain retail
--phase learn --trials 1`, 114 tasks) then threw `tau2 phase failed` at
07:30:45Z after `litellm.InternalServerError: DeepseekException` with
`500 Internal Server Error` from `api.deepseek.com/beta/chat/completions`
(request `7d06439a-ae83-451b-9591-436ff37e9da8`), which aborted every task's
first trial. The reference arm's airline eval phase failed the same way
(request `f41447e4-d372-4992-999a-97139dee5590`). Step 14 `l4-pair` then
reported `missing artefact: arms/reference/poc-l4.json` as a cascade, step 15
`Say so when nothing was measured` emitted `L4 wrote no artefact` by design,
and step 16 uploaded `l4-evidence` (20,269,801 bytes, 90 files, id
`13565972549`).

**The artefact was examined, not assumed.** The zip contains zero `arms/`
entries. Its root `poc-l4.json` is the 2026-10-22 placeholder titled
`L4 -- tau-squared-bench pass^4 (not run: no environment)` with
`status_not_run: 1`, `n: 0` and `calls: 0`; its `poc-l4-pair.json` is the
2026-11-01 historical pair (`deltaPp 1.47`, `p` about 1.0). The 90 files are
the repository's pre-existing `eval/results` history and baselines, not a
reading of this run. So the verdict is **infrastructure failure / no
measurement**: all eight R48 predictions are NOT GRADED, neither held nor
falsified; all seven refutations are NOT TRIGGERED; the revert rule is NOT

## 172 — U3 measured, the revert rule fired, and the arm was reverted

**The retry measured.** Run `42350304597` on head `33038232` died on a persistent
DeepSeek 500 and measured nothing (`AUDIT` 34.33). Its lawful retry
`42353229972` on the same head, same prereg and same nine inputs is the first
real U3 measurement: job `128345648759` ran both arms to `success`, the log has
zero `DeepseekException` / `500 Internal Server Error` lines, step 11 read the
registered floor, `TAU_MIN_COVERAGE: 0.01` reached the memory arm, and
`l4-evidence` (`13568804042`, 20,276,555 bytes, 92 entries) carries both
`arms/memory/poc-l4.json` and `arms/reference/poc-l4.json`. The run is
`completed failure` only at step 14, `Pair the arms`: the blocking scientific
gates `V5-resolution` (MDE 14.83pp), `V16-transfer-resolvable` (83 informative
trials, 14 repairs) and `l4-paired` are red. `ci.yml` is green on the head.

**Seven of eight predictions hold.** P1 the floor reaches the facade
(`meanPackIds` 1.4675 -> 1.0893, `injectedPairs` 2188 -> 1573); P2
`zeroCoveragePairs` 750 -> 0; P3 `recallServed` 1491 -> 965 with `V1` still
passing; P4 all three reconciliation identities hold (1573 + 0 = 1573, all ten
rungs against 965 served packs, zero rung retains 1573 and empties nothing);
P5 every validity gate R47 passed passes again, no regression, `widenedItems=0`,
seven census fields intact; P6 `coverage` present on memory and absent on
reference; P7 the declared floor `0.01` is recomputed from R47's committed
curve under the registered weights, not copied. The committed histogram is the
structural fingerprint of a floor applied before delivery: its `0` and `0.01`
rungs are identical (`1573 / 965 / 0`) because the facade had already removed
the zero-coverage pairs, while rung `0.02` drops to `1533 / 956 / 9`.

**P8 fails, and the registration says what that means.** The two memory arms
are not comparable. R47 distilled 8 items from 4 edit events into a store of 8;
the retry distilled 12 items from 6 events into a store of 12, with the same
seeded split, scenario, model, trials and admission settings (`trust=0.9`,
`support=0.9`, `confidence=0.6165`). The learning phase and the store changed
while the configuration did not: LLM distillation and agent sampling are
run-to-run stochastic. `prereg/R48-u3-coverage-floor.md` prediction 8 states
that "a change in the learning phase, the store or the admission rule would
break the pairing and refute the arm". The memory-free reference arm also
drifted from `pass^4 = 0.30` in R47 to `0.44` in the retry, 14 points of pure
sampling noise on an unchanged configuration. This is the standing warning of
`TECH-DESIGN` 17.40 ("comparing two dispatches puts the answer inside the
run-to-run noise") and `ROADMAP` Read 7 measured at first hand, and it is the
user's hypothesis in its sharpest form yet: what was remembered and what the
measurement compared were both wrong, not merely how memory was used.

**The revert rule fires on the reading, not on the explanation.** The R45 rule,
re-stated unchanged in R46, R47 and R48, reverts if `l4-paired` is
significantly negative **or** falls below -5pp with a served pack; the second
branch deliberately does not require significance, and `prereg/R45-admission.md`
adds that "a plausible story about why a bad pack hurt is not evidence that the
next pack will help". The within-run `l4-paired` gate (`packages/eval/src/bin/
l4-pair.ts`, memory `0.38` against reference `0.44`) reads `-6.00pp [-16, +4]
p=0.4531` with `recallServed = 965 > 0`. The rule fires. There is a highly
plausible story available — the 14-point reference drift, the underpowered
14.83pp MDE, the confounded pairing — and the standing project rule forbids
using it to soften the reading. U3's applied floor of `0.01` is **reverted**:
the as-is configuration (`AS_IS_FLOOR = 0`) is restored as the default, the
retry is recorded as a measured, refuted, reverted arm, and no accuracy number
is claimed in either direction. `prereg/R48-u3-coverage-floor.md` is not
edited; its R5 refutation forbids editing the registration after the readout.

**Two defects, both found by reading the artefact.** Defect 28: the offline
`r48-readback.py` verifier bound refutation R4 to the **cross-run** delta
between the two memory arms (`-4.00pp, p=0.6875`, the treatment's contribution)
instead of the **within-run** `l4-paired` gate `-6.00pp` that the registration
names, and so reported `revertRuleFired=false`. This is a real instrument bug,
not a scientific disagreement. Defect 29: a cross-dispatch ablation cannot hold
the learning phase, the store and the reference arm fixed, so `pass^4` deltas
between two dispatches are confounded by design; R48's P8 predicted exactly
this failure mode.

**Fixed in this iteration, TDD and no mocks.** The revert rule is lifted out of
prose and the offline script into `packages/eval/src/l4-revert.ts`, a typed
production invariant. `PairedReading` carries a `scope` tag of `within-run` or
`cross-run`; `revertRule` refuses a cross-run reading at runtime, and the two
bars (`0.05`, `-5pp`) are exported constants. `eval/fixtures/
tau2-l4-paired-readings.json` holds the two real committed readings (R47
`+12pp -> clear`, R48 `-6pp / 965 served -> FIRES`). Fourteen tests use those
real readings, both branches, both strict boundaries, and a mirror case where a
catastrophic cross-run delta with a safe within-run gate must not fire. The
offline verifier is corrected to the same semantics, its self-test grades R4
end to end on the real readings, and the real artefact now reports
`revertRuleFired=true`, `allPredictionsHold=false`, `allRefutationsClear=false`,
`verdict=GATE_RED`. `pnpm check` exits 0 at 2994 tests across 143 files with
coverage 99.98 / 99.68 / 100 / 99.98, `audit: ok`, `bundle:size ok`.

**What is closed and what is next.** Downstream U1, U2 and R46's
admission-rule arms stay CLOSED: R48's R6 keeps them closed until a valid pair
exists, and a confounded cross-dispatch pair is not one. The reverted arm is
not re-dispatched. P0 is now to design a **within-run pair**: one dispatch that
holds a single learning phase, a single store and a single reference arm, and
varies only the recall facade between the as-is and the floored configuration —
the design `ROADMAP` Read 7 already proved removes the run-to-run confound.
Defect 27's fail-fast provider probe remains a bounded P1 fix on a later head.
Ranking is unchanged: IBM `gpt-5.5` airline 82.0 remains the SOTA, microglia
fifth of six named entries. A measured, reverted arm moves no leaderboard row.


### 172.1 — Statistical sources fix the design of the next pair

After the R48 revert above and while `ci.yml` `42366953175` went green
on head `455a4616`, five methodology sources were read and registered in
`AUDIT` 34.36 and `TECH-DESIGN` 17.100. Common-random-numbers pairing gives
`Var(A - B) = 2 * sigma^2 * (1 - rho)`; McNemar is the classical paired test
the lane already uses; `Var(score) ~= sigma_between^2 / T + sigma_within^2 /
(T * R)` shows that more runs cannot shrink the between-task term, which is
why R48's MDE is 14.83pp and 216 tasks would be needed for a 5pp effect;
tau-bench's own guide requires a fixed user simulator and reports pass^k as
`E_task[prod_j success_j]`. Together they turn defect 29 from an observation
into an arithmetic statement: two dispatches of one configuration are not a
paired comparison. The next arm is therefore a within-run pair — one learning
phase, one store, one reference, one seed stream, only the recall facade
varied — with the acceptance bar of `TECH-DESIGN` 17.100. None of these is a
new `Pass^4` entry and none moves a ranking: IBM `gpt-5.5` airline 82.0
remains the SOTA, microglia fifth of six named entries.


### 172.2 — The within-run pair begins as a typed invariant, and the control arm stays parked

The direction question was settled first. A reader asked why the leading
competitor's implementation is not reproduced before learning from the others.
`COMPETITIVE` L.19 records the answer: the mechanisms have been read at source
and transferred, the mechanisms of nine further systems are already registered,
and the `82.0` number is not a replicable object (L.8, six reasons). The
`cross-model-guideline-control` arm registered in L.8 stays **registered and not
dispatched**; opening it now would add a second learning phase and a second
store next to the pair we need to measure. The next dispatch remains the
within-run pair. Cortex release stays excluded by the standing instruction.

**Architecture decision, from source rather than intuition.** A *paired facade
inside one driver run*, not a third driver lane. `packages/eval/src/bin/
tau2-driver.ts` `run()` is one self-contained unit: `listTasks`, the learn
phase, `host.distill`, one `EmbeddedMemory` store, one `startRecall` facade and
one eval phase. A third lane would re-run that whole chain and reproduce defect
29 by construction. `bin/l4.ts` calls `loaded.run()` once and writes one
artefact; `bin/l4-pair.ts` pairs two artefacts through `L4_FIRST`/`L4_SECOND`;
`bin/lib.ts` resolves its output directory from `POC_RESULT_DIR`. The wiring
therefore needs one extra artefact per run, not a new lane. `TECH-DESIGN`
17.101 carries the ten-item layout, the dependency layering and the P0-P3 order.

**What was built this iteration.** `packages/eval/src/within-run-pair.ts`
lifts defect 29 out of prose into a typed, testable production invariant, the
same move that produced `l4-revert.ts` in the previous iteration. `RunScope`
names the eight fields two arms must share (dispatch, registration, store
fingerprint, learn split, test split, seed, trials, model); `scopeDifference`
names the first field that drifted; `withinRunPair` returns one of three
terminal states, `PAIRED`, `REFUSED_CROSS_RUN` or `NO_MEASUREMENT`, matching the
offline R48 verifier. The `FacadeContrast` it emits is tagged
`facade-contrast` and deliberately has no `scope` field, so it cannot be handed
to `revertRule`, which grades the memory-vs-reference `l4-paired` gate and
nothing else. That is defect 28 and defect 29 made unrepresentable.

`eval/fixtures/tau2-facade-scopes.json` carries the real committed R47 and R48
readings: runs `42337250684` and `42353229972`, 8 versus 12 distilled items,
reference `pass^4` 0.30 versus 0.44, served packs 1491 versus 965, and the two
within-run gate readings +12pp and -6pp. Its identity control is labelled in
the fixture as a structural counterpart, not a measurement: it proves the
invariant admits a valid pair without inventing an experimental result.
`packages/eval/src/__tests__/within-run-pair.test.ts` has **29 tests** over the
real scopes, all eight scope fields, all registered floor rungs, both refusal
branches, a mirror case where a catastrophic-looking cross-run delta must still
be refused, and every malformed-instrument path. `packages/eval/src/index.ts`
exports the new API; the pre-existing `PairVerdict` from `pairs.ts` is
unchanged, and the new verdict type is named `WithinRunPairVerdict` to avoid a
collision typecheck caught.

**Verification.** `pnpm check` exits **0**: 3023 tests across 144 files,
coverage 99.97 / 99.67 / 100 / 99.97, `audit: ok`, `bundle:size ok`. The
structural coupling ledger moved from 141 to 142 modules and 38236 to 38444
production lines; the six timing-only JSON artefacts rewritten by the check
were restored, so only the structural entry travels. Both repositories are
pushed as Lambertyan and `ci.yml` is green on the new head.

**What is still pending, and is not claimed as done.** The driver's paired
facade loop, the second artefact writer, the `sota.yml` step, a fresh R49
pre-registration and the dispatch itself are the remaining P1 items. No new
`Pass^4` number is claimed here. Ranking is unchanged: IBM `gpt-5.5` airline
82.0 remains the SOTA, microglia fifth of six named entries.

### 172.4 — The first R49 dispatch is cancelled, and the guard is hardened

Dispatch `42380685732` was cancelled at its registration check. The `prereg`

reference arm began anyway. No task was evaluated and no artefact was written.

The fix is in `.github/workflows/sota.yml`: the step now rejects a `.md`
suffix with an actionable message, verifies the file exists, and the reference
arm is conditioned on the registration check not having failed. The readback
CLI's "no artefact" line was made neutral so a failed dispatch cannot be
described as a single-facade run. Verified locally with both input spellings.
