### 172.44 R62 built: one switch, one join, and three things that had to be right rather than added

R62 is implemented and pushed (`9aa538ee`). The arm is not dispatched yet: R57's `far` arm is in flight,
and the repository variables are global, so two graded runs at once would read one another's settings.

**The switch.** `TAU_DISTILL_SCOPE=edited|all`, resolved by `resolveDistillScope` in
`packages/eval/src/tau2-scope.ts`. Four cases, and the fourth is the one that matters: `correction` —
the *unit*'s word — is refused rather than guessed. A misspelt scope measures the control and reports the
control's numbers under a treatment's name, which is the exact failure `resolveDistillUnit` already
refuses and `resolveDistillForm` accepts on purpose.

**The record.** `Correction.provenance` is required (`edited` | `passed`), so a default cannot make every
record a repair by omission. `learnableCorrections` takes the scope as its fourth argument; `teachingOf`
now answers in three states and the order of its two tests is the design: an unscored task teaches
nothing under either scope (a missing measurement is not a pass), a pass with no stated criteria teaches
nothing (there is no rule to state), and only then does the scope decide.

**Three things that had to be right rather than merely added.**

- **`traceOf` refuses a payload carrying both `expected` and `rubricMet`.** A passing record has no
  reference to differ from — the attempt *is* the reference — and a payload that says "here is what
  should have happened instead" beside "nothing should have happened instead" asks the model to guess.
  A guess inside a prompt is an undeclared measurement, and this round's central reading is whether the
  distiller can say anything about a trajectory that succeeded.
- **The prompt grows two sentences only when the scope declares them**, and the test is a *diff*: adding
  the passing lines to the shared rules must change exactly those two lines and remove none, so a
  repair-only dispatch still reads R61's prompt byte for byte. A prompt change that silently moves a
  published arm's numbers is the kind of upgrade this repository refuses.
- **`provenanceCensus` joins a claim to its record through `EvidenceRef.runId`**, and returns four
  counts rather than a share. A percentage reads identically for a store of pure passes and for a store
  whose every claim was taught by a repair *and* a pass — and the second is the collision the round
  exists to find. An item citing a run the round never opened is counted separately, as
  `itemsUnattributed`, because it means the join does not hold and every reading above it is void.

| reading the artefact now carries | why it is a count and not a share |
| --- | --- |
| `provenance.edited` / `passed` | two populations, and a store that grew without changing character has to be distinguishable from one that changed character |
| `provenance.tasksEdited` / `tasksPassed` | support is counted on tasks, so the denominator differs from the claim count by construction |
| `provenance.itemsEditedOnly` / `itemsPassedOnly` / `itemsMixed` | the mixture is the finding; a share would round it away |
| `provenance.itemsUnattributed` / `evidenceUnattributed` | an instrument failure, not a category: a claim from nowhere invalidates the split for the rest too |

**`learning.edited` now means what its name says** — corrections from a repair. Under the published
scope that is the same number every existing readback already reads; under the widened scope the
population is read from `provenance` instead, which is the point of recording both.

**Instrumentation.** 22 new cases on the modules (4 on the resolver, 7 on the census, 5 on the payload
shape, 6 on the prompt), 1 end-to-end driver case that produces **one repair and two passes** from the
stub benchmark and checks that every stored claim is attributed and at least one came from a pass, and
**21 self-checks** in `eval/verifiers/r62_readback.py` — instrument first, then the four registered
predictions and the four refutations. Repository: **176 files, 3,604 tests, 99.96 / 99.68 / 100 /
99.96**; `tau2-scope.ts` and `tau2-provenance.ts` are **100 on all four dimensions**.

**One ordering decision, written down so it is not re-litigated.** The queue is R57 `far` (in flight) →
`near` → `adversarial` → R62. The R57 arms answer the question the project was founded on — does a
planted distractor reach the store, and does the pack then do harm — and they must run at the published
population, which is what an unset `TAU_DISTILL_SCOPE` gives. R62 is the population experiment and runs
last of the four.

### 172.45 A cap of twenty-five, and the gate that did not exist

Two commits after R62 went green, I tried to add two `workflow_dispatch` inputs so four independent arms
could share the wall clock. GitHub refused to parse the file —

> Invalid Argument - failed to parse workflow: you may only define up to 25 `inputs` for a
> `workflow_dispatch` event

— because `sota.yml` already had exactly twenty-five. **The consequence was total and CI was green**:
the push produced a run named after the file path and nothing else, no dispatch of any workflow in the
repository could start, and `ci.yml` succeeded on the same commit because it never looked at the other
workflow files. That is the failure mode this project spends its time on — a gate that reports success
because it is not looking.

| step | what it shows |
| --- | --- |
| the push | a run named `.github/workflows/sota.yml`, conclusion `failure`, no jobs |
| `ci.yml` on the same sha | **success** |
| the next dispatch attempt | `422`, "failed to parse workflow" |
| after the revert | workflow state `active`, dispatch accepted |

The revert shipped first (`1441fd4c`) because an unparseable workflow is every gate at once. Then the
gate: `scripts/check-workflows.py`, wired into `pnpm check`, asserts that every workflow parses, declares
at most twenty-five dispatch inputs, declares no input twice, and names a runner on every job. Its own
self-test found **two defects in it before it shipped** — the counter assumed eight-space indentation
while `sota.yml` writes six (so it counted zero inputs on the very file it exists for), and it counted
into a dictionary, which cannot hold the duplicate it was looking for. The indentation is derived from
the `inputs:` line now, the declarations are a list, and there is a case for each.

PyYAML is optional: the cap and the duplicate count are counts over literal text, so an image without
the library loses the validity check and nothing else, and says so on its own line rather than turning
the build red for a missing import.

**What this costs, stated plainly.** The four arms stay serial. `TAU_PLANTED_RULES` and
`TAU_DISTILL_SCOPE` are repository variables, a variable is global, and there is no dispatch input left
to carry an override. The correct fix is not another input — it is the rule `lane-scope` already
encodes: **the registration decides the experiment**, so the arm belongs in `prereg/*.md`'s frontmatter
and reaches the L4 job through a job output. That is the next change to the workflow, and it is written
down here rather than improvised at the end of a queue.

### 172.46 A planted arm was graded as the treatment, and the arm was the one that was right

Run `42534241219` on `1ecb6418` dispatched R57's `far` arm — one irrelevant rule planted in every pack,
at the published population. The reading came back exactly as the registration predicts, and the step
concluded `failure` anyway.

| reading | value | registered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| planted rules landing inside their band | 1920 of 1934 (99.3%) | the plant did what it was told |
| paired ledger | broke 9, repaired 9 of 57 episodes | net zero |
| excess | **+0.00pp** (half-width 14.59pp) | a distractor is not free and not harmful |
| `pass^4` | 0.5789 | published 0.575 |
| corpus digest | `0585fafcc817841a` | Mini-Dev, pinned |

The `L4 arm — memory` step failed on `l4-pass4`: `0.5789473684210527 (>= published + 0.05)`. That bar is
the treatment's. A distractor arm's own hypothesis is that it **does not clear** it — the arm's answer of
0.5789 against a 0.575 published number, with a ledger that broke and repaired the same nine episodes, is
the arm agreeing with its registration, and the gate read that agreement as a miss. This is the seventh
instance of one defect class (AUDIT 34.86): six `sota` runs whose memory arm was green and whose
memory-free control failed a bar no control can pass, and now a planted arm failing the bar it was
registered to miss.

**The fix is the control's fix, one arm over.** `SampleGateInput` gains `planted?: { arm }`;
`l4-pass4` is omitted when a plant is declared, and the two gates every arm owes — coverage and a fully
scored grid — stay exactly where they were, because planting a distractor does not license a small or
partial sample. The artefact says the bar does not apply rather than going quiet about it:
`published_bar_applies: 0`, and a new `planted_arm: far`. `delta` is omitted for a planted arm for the
same reason the gate is — a difference against the published number is the competitive reading, and this
arm is read by its paired ledger.

**The reading moves, it does not disappear.** `eval/verifiers/r57_readback.py` grades the plant census,
the trial count and the paired excess arm by arm, which is what it was built for; `sample-gates.ts` owes
a planted arm only the statement that the competitive bar is not its bar. Four new cases pin it: a
planted arm carries two gates, a small or partly-unscored planted arm still fails, an arm that planted
nothing keeps the bar (`undefined` and an absent key are the same statement), and the two remaining
criteria are named so a future edit that quietly re-adds the bar lands on a red test.

**The readback tool also learned to read what ran.** It refused a set of fewer than three arms with
`NO_MEASUREMENT`, which discarded a dispatch that had measured everything about itself — instrument,
plant share, trial count and ledger all present and all consistent. A partial set is now graded for what
it can answer: the state stays `GRADED`, a `partial:` line above the predictions states `1 of 3 arms
(far); missing near, adversarial, so the order is not graded`, and the order prediction becomes `n/a`
rather than a failure, because an arm that has not run is not an arm that failed. An empty set is still
`NO_MEASUREMENT`.

Queue unchanged and now unblocked: `near` → `adversarial` (each needs `TAU_PLANTED_RULES` set before
dispatch, since a repository variable is global) → R62 (`TAU_DISTILL_SCOPE=all`, `TAU_DISTILL_UNIT=trace`).
173 → 176 files, 3613 tests, coverage 99.96 / 99.69 / 100 / 99.96.

### 172.47 The same bar in a second place, found before it fired, and the run list stops printing source

`near` was dispatched at `71457278` (`42544865267`, `TAU_PLANTED_RULES=near`, `l4`, `bird` left empty so
`scope` skipped the BIRD lane again) and is in the memory arm. While it ran, the question from AUDIT
34.86 was asked of the rest of the lane: **where else does the treatment's bar live?**

Two places, and one of them is on the path `near` is about to walk.

| gate | home | whose hypothesis it states | what it would do to `near` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `l4-pass4 >= published + 5pp` | `l4.ts` → `sampleGates` | the treatment's | failed `far` at 0.5789 vs 0.575 — **fixed, `597788d`** |
| `l4-paired` | `l4-pair.ts` | the treatment's | fails the moment `near`'s registered harm is significant |
| `l4-effect-resolved` | `l4-pair.ts` | a claim the arm makes | grades a benefit sentence a distractor never claims |

`near` predicts it breaks more episodes than it repairs. A pair verdict of `HARM` is that prediction
**confirmed**, and the second row would have turned it into a red job — the same defect that had just
been repaired one file over, waiting one step later in the same job. Nothing had fired yet, which is the
only reason this is a fix rather than a second incident.

`l4-paired`, `l4-effect-resolved` and `l4-same-split` move out of `bin/l4-pair.ts` into
`packages/eval/src/pair-gates.ts`, where they are testable for the first time — a `bin/` file is
excluded from coverage, so three gates that decide whether the lane publishes a harm had never had a
test. For a planted arm the first two are omitted, the omission is recorded (`planted_arm` in
`poc-l4-pair.json`), and `l4-same-split` stays, because it is a property of the two files on disk rather
than a hypothesis about either of them. The plant is read from **the arm's own artefact**
(`tau2.plant.arm`), not from the dispatch's environment: an arm filed under `near` that carries no plant
census planted nothing, and its pair is a control pair whatever the variable said.

**The run list stopped printing source.** `42534241219` rendered the skipped BIRD job as

> `BIRD ${{ (((github.event.inputs.split == 'dev') && 'dev') || ((((github.event.inputs.split == 'train') && 'train (out-of-sample)') || 'Mini-Dev'))) }} (cross-fitted, memory on/off)`

because a job that is skipped never evaluates its `name:`. The nested ternary was written to put the
split in the title, and where the lane *is* skipped — the exact place a reader is trying to work out why
something is missing — it produced the longest line in the run list. It is now
`BIRD ${{ github.event.inputs.split || 'minidev' }} (cross-fitted, memory on/off)`, which renders as
`BIRD minidev (cross-fitted, memory on/off)` when the lane runs and as two short words when it does not.
`train` loses the `(out-of-sample)` suffix, which was a warning against quoting the number; that warning
is in the `split` input's description, shown beside the title on the run page, and in the artefact name.

176 → 177 files, 3623 tests, coverage 99.96 / 99.69 / 100 / 99.96, `pair-gates.ts` 100 on all four.
`scripts/check-workflows.py` still parses all five workflows at or under twenty-five inputs.

### 172.48 Two red pushes with every local gate green, and the two asymmetries that caused them

Four commits went out in this stretch. Two of them turned CI red while `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`,
`node scripts/audit.mjs` and `pnpm eval:verifiers` were all green locally, and the two causes are
different — which is why they are recorded separately.

**`71457278` and `25f90aff`: a `bin/` file, and a compiler run the local entry point did not make.**

```
packages/eval/src/bin/l4.ts(452,3): error TS2322: Type '{ …; planted_arm?: string; }' is not assignable
  to type 'Record<string, number>'. Property 'planted_arm' is incompatible with index signature.
```

`poc-l4.json`'s `metrics` is a `Record<string, number>`: `arm: 0|1`, `published_bar_applies: 0|1`,
`paired_p`, `k`. I wrote `planted_arm: 'far'` into it, which is a string, and nothing local disagreed
because `packages/*/tsconfig.json` lists `src/bin` under `exclude` — the lanes are processes, not library
surface, and they resolve with `nodenext` rather than through the path aliases, so the composite build
does not see them. `pnpm typecheck` was the composite build. CI's step 7 was `pnpm typecheck:lanes`, the
second compiler run that does see them, and the file had been carrying a type error for two commits.

The fix is two lines and one of them is not about the type. `planted_arm: 0|1`, because `metrics` holds
numbers and the arm's **name** already lives where it belongs — `tau2.plant.arm`, written by the driver
that planted the rules, one source of truth for a fact two files could otherwise disagree about. And
`pnpm typecheck` now chains `typecheck:lanes`, so the command a person types checks what CI checks.

**`25f90aff` and `9f63398`: the ledger the local gate rewrote and never compared.**

```
coupling ledger failed: the committed snapshot still describes the tree it was taken from
```

`pair-gates.ts` is a new module; the walk went from 166 to 167 and `poc-coupling.json`'s `scanned` field
stopped describing the tree. The comparison that notices this existed **only** as an inline `node -e`
inside `ci.yml`; `pnpm check` ran `eval:coupling`, which rewrites that same committed file in the working
tree, and then moved on. Worse, when the rewrite appeared as a dirty file during an earlier commit I read
it as regenerated churn and discarded it (`git checkout -- eval/results`), which is the exact inversion
this project keeps writing audits about: **the file is a ledger, and a ledger that is regenerated by the
step that grades it must be compared, not cleaned.**

`scripts/check-coupling-ledger.mjs` now holds the eleven claims that were inline, runs them against a
fresh walk in a temp directory, and gains `--self-test` with eight fixtures whose verdicts are known —
a tree that grew, a ledger with a failing gate, an unclassified module, an upward edge, a lost deferral,
a statement quoting a verdict, a disagreeing prose-only census. It is called from `ci.yml` (with the
directory the step already scanned) and from `pnpm check` (scanning for itself), so the two gates are the
same gate. The self-test is chained into `pnpm eval:verifiers` beside the twelve verifiers, taking that
list to thirteen.

| state | what it means |
| --- | --- |
| `51d7deb0` | CI **success** — the snapshot fix |
| `770292e9` | CI **success** — the ledger script and its eight fixtures |
| `32dc1a5` | CI in flight at the time of writing — `typecheck` covers the lanes |

`near` is unaffected throughout: it dispatched at `71457278` and its job pins that sha. It is in the
memory arm, ~2h.

### 172.49 Statements reach 100, and three fallbacks that no input could reach

Coverage before this stretch: **99.97 statements, 99.69 branches, 100 functions, 99.97 lines**. Four
files carried uncovered **statements**, which is the only category that means "behaviour nobody has ever
run":

| file | uncovered | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/node/src/mcp.ts` | 229-230 | the feedback tool's catch: a `MicrogliaError` and a rethrow |
| `packages/eval/src/facade-pair.ts` | 256-257, 459-460 | a task row with no id; a duplicated numeric guard |
| `packages/eval/src/within-run-pair.ts` | 194-195 | a pair with no common task set |

Two were **real gaps and became tests**. `mcp.ts` had no test that made `recordFeedback` fail, so the
one branch that decides whether a store failure is a tool error the model can read or a host defect
that escapes had never executed. The test injects a `TypeError` through the facade and asserts the
handler rethrows: the `MicrogliaError` branch tells the model what to do differently, and a `TypeError`
tells it nothing, so swallowing it would report a broken deployment as a refused request. The
`facade-pair` gap became a test with a nameless task row: the conversion refuses it before pairing, and
the verdict carries the refusal as `NO_MEASUREMENT` rather than crashing the step.

Three were **fallbacks no input could reach**, which is a different defect and is recorded separately
(`AUDIT 34.88`):

| site | the fallback | why it cannot fire |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sql/src/schema-link.ts:212` | `byColumn.get(k) ?? []` | the map is filled from the same blocks, two loops up |
| `eval/src/within-run-pair.ts:193` | `paired === 0 → unmeasured` | `validArm` refuses an empty or duplicate-id arm, and the id sets are compared on the line above |
| `eval/src/facade-pair.ts:454` | three `typeof !== 'number'` re-checks | the guard forty lines up tested the same three fields |
| `eval/src/ablations.ts:98` | `items[0]?.status ?? 'missing'` | `learn()` admitted one rule, and `status: 'all'` filters nothing |

Each is now asserted by construction with a paragraph saying what makes it total, so a future refactor
that breaks the invariant crashes there instead of silently doing less. `ablations.ts` went from the
repository's worst branch coverage (94.44) to 100.

**And one test that had been passing for the wrong reason.** `tau2-admission.test.ts`'s "refuses an
action that names no tool" passed an object-shaped `before`, so `isDriverCompletion(before)` failed
first and `tau2EditSemantics` returned `undefined` without ever reaching the validator the test is named
for. It had been certifying nothing since R58, and the coverage report was the only thing that noticed —
`return false` at line 53 was the file's last uncovered statement. The `before` side is now the shape
`complete()` writes, and two shapes that were never exercised (a name that is not a string; no
`arguments` object) have cases.

| reading | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| statements | 99.97 | **100** |
| branches | 99.69 | **99.76** |
| functions | 100 | **100** |
| lines | 99.97 | **100** |
| tests | 3623 | **3627** |

The remaining 0.24pp of branches is the same pattern at scale: ~40 files carry a `?.`/`??` fallback on a
lookup that cannot miss. Closing them is a campaign rather than a commit, and it is queued as such —
each one needs its invariant read before the fallback is removed, and in a measurement path an invariant
read wrongly is worse than a branch left uncovered.

### 172.50 The planted arm's wiring, end to end, and the variable state the next two dispatches need

`sampleGates` and `pairGates` were unit-tested and the **wiring between them and the environment was
not**. That gap is not hypothetical: the same wiring produced a `string` written into
`Record<string, number>` (`9f63398`, caught only by CI) and, a day earlier, a bar applied to an arm whose
registered hypothesis is that it misses the bar. Two modules agreeing in isolation says nothing about the
dispatch that drives both.

`packages/eval/src/__tests__/l4-planted-arm.test.ts` runs the two bins the workflow runs, with a driver
module standing in for the τ² environment, and reads what they published:

| case | asserted |
| --- | --- |
| `TAU_PLANTED_RULES=near`, every task passing | `arm: 1`, `published_bar_applies: 0`, `planted_arm: 1`, no `l4-pass4`, `l4-coverage` and `l4-fully-scored` intact, no `delta` |
| the same run with the variable cleared | `published_bar_applies: 1`, `planted_arm: 0`, no `tau2`, `l4-pass4` present **and passing** |
| a pair over a HARM reading, memory artefact carrying `plant.arm: near` | no `l4-paired`, no `l4-effect-resolved`, `l4-same-split` passing, `planted_arm: near`, the comparison and the `HARM` verdict still published |
| the same rows with no plant census | `l4-paired` **fails and blocks** — the exemption is keyed on the arm's own artefact, not on the environment the step ran in |

The last row is the one that makes the other three mean something: without it a bug that removed
`l4-paired` for *every* pair would pass all of them.

**The variable state the next two dispatches run under**, recorded because three of these decide what the
run measures and one of them is a landmine:

| variable | value | who consumes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TAU_PLANTED_RULES` | `near` | `tau2-driver` plants; `l4.ts` decides the bar; **must be cleared before R62** |
| `TAU_DISTILL_UNIT` | `trace` | the distiller's unit (R58) — shared by both R57 arms, so they stay comparable |
| `TAU_DISTILL_SCOPE` | *unset* (`edited`) | R62 sets it to `all`; the R57 arms must run at the published population |
| `TAU_TEST_DOMAIN` | `airline` | overridden per-dispatch by the registration (`retail`), which is the R54 fix doing its job |
| `TAU_MIN_TASKS` | `40` | the split floor |
| `TAU_ENV_READY` | `false` | so the L4 job needs `l4: true` on every dispatch |
| `TAU_TRACE_CLAIMS` | `6` | R60's ceiling |

The landmine is the first row: R62 is dispatched with `TAU_DISTILL_SCOPE=all` and **without** a plant, so
`TAU_PLANTED_RULES` has to be cleared in the same edit that sets the scope. A population experiment run
with a distractor in every pack would measure the distractor, and nothing in its artefact would say the
two variables were changed together.

### 172.51 R57 `near` read: it repaired more than it broke, and the band was graded on another population

Run `42544865267` on `71457278` — `TAU_PLANTED_RULES=near`, the published population, `bird` skipped by
`scope`. **The job concluded `success`**, the first planted arm to do so: the `sampleGates` repair shipped
at `597788d` is what turned the previous arm's `failure` into a reading.

| reading | `far` | `near` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one rule planted per served request | 1934 of 1934 | 1972 of 1972 |
| in band, of planted requests | 1920 (99.3%) | 699 (**35.4%**) |
| broke / repaired, of 57 pairs | 9 / 9 | **5 / 7** |
| excess | +0 | **−2 (−3.51pp)** |
| paired `pass^4` | +0.00pp (half-width 14.59) | +3.51pp (half-width 11.91) |
| verdict | `UNRESOLVED` | `UNRESOLVED` |
| gates in the arm artefact | `l4-pass4` present | **absent**, `published_bar_applies: 0` |

The readback returns **`ABANDONED`**: `near broke more episodes than it repaired` is **false** — it
repaired seven and broke five. That is the registered sign split, and it did not appear. It is not a
benefit: +3.51pp is exactly the drift a control arm has been measured to move on its own, and the
half-width is 11.91pp, so the honest sentence is *the predicted cost was not observed at this sample*,
which is the outcome the registration said would make the arm uninformative rather than wrong.

**The second failure was the registration's, not the arm's.** The band was graded at "60% of requests"
and measured 35.4%. Amendment 1 calibrated 60% on *task instructions*. The census counts *every recall
request*, and `eval/drivers/tau2/microglia_agent.py` sends the current message's content on each turn:

```python
def generate_next_message(self, message, state):
    text = getattr(message, "content", None)
    pack = recall(text if isinstance(text, str) else "")
```

8.6 requests per episode over 228 episodes is 1972 requests, of which the first carries the task's own
words and the rest are tool results and replies. A rule authored to share two of the *question's* terms
cannot be expected to share two of `{"order_id": "#W1234"}`. The arm was graded against a population it
never ran on — R51's defect one layer down (`AUDIT 34.89`).

**Amendment 2, written before `adversarial` was dispatched and not after it read.** The per-request
band share becomes a reported distribution; the graded prediction becomes the one the contrast exists
for — *the two polarities sit at the same level*, within 10pp of each other — because Amendment 1's
argument was that polarity must not move the dose, and a between-arm equality needs no absolute
threshold. `r57_readback.py` implements it, and its self-test grew two cases: one that the gap abandons
the account, one that a lone arm's share is *reported* (the old case named a near band failure and was
passing because the far line contains the words "band landed" — a test passing for the wrong reason, in
the tool whose job is to catch that).

**`adversarial` is in flight** (`42556573088` on `e55d1028`, `TAU_PLANTED_RULES=adversarial`), on the
commit that carries `pairGates` — the arm most likely to produce a significant `HARM` is the one for
which that gate most needed to stop blocking.

### 172.52 R57 read in full: the ladder has two rungs, and the first one is flat

Three arms, all on the published population, all on one 114-task retail split with 57 paired tasks.
`far` and `near` were read earlier (`42534241219`, `42544865267`); `adversarial` ran as
`42556573088` on `e55d1028`.

| arm | planted / served | in band | broke | repaired | excess | `pass^4` delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `far` (shares nothing) | 1934 / 1934 | 1920 (99.3%) | 9 | 9 | **+0.00pp** | +0.00 (half-width 14.59) |
| `near` (shares two terms) | 1972 / 1972 | 699 (35.4%) | 5 | 7 | **−3.51pp** | +3.51 (half-width 11.91) |
| `adversarial` (contradicts) | 1910 / 1910 | 712 (37.3%) | 11 | 7 | **+7.02pp** | −7.02 (half-width 14.59) |

**What the registration predicted, and what it got.**

| prediction | registered | measured | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| one rule in every served request | all three arms | 1934/1934, 1972/1972, 1910/1910 | pass |
| the two polarities sit at the same level | within 10pp | **1.8pp apart** | pass |
| `far` harmless beyond drift | not worse than 3.51pp | +0.00pp | pass |
| `near` worse than `far` | beyond 3.51pp | **−3.51pp, i.e. better** | **fail** |
| `adversarial` worse than `near` | beyond 3.51pp | **+10.53pp** | pass |
| refutation: `far` ≈ `near` | fires if within drift | **fired** | refutation |

**The finding, stated as the registration allows it to be stated.** Proximity of vocabulary does not
cost accuracy at this sample: `near` broke five episodes and repaired seven, and its excess sits
inside the drift a control arm moves on its own. Contradictory content does cost accuracy:
`adversarial` broke eleven and repaired seven, ten and a half points worse than `near`, well outside
the same drift. The dose ladder is therefore **two rungs, not three** — 0 and +7pp — and the variable
that separates them is not distance but **whether the injected statement is contradicted by the
correct behaviour**.

That is the answer to the question R57 was dispatched to ask, and it is the opposite of the design
the negative-effect literature is usually read as supporting. Retrieval-distance tuning cannot reach
it: the two polarities land in the band at the *same* rate (35.4% vs 37.3%), because the band share is
a property of the request texts rather than of the rule, and the arm that hurt is the one whose rules
*matched the right questions and said the wrong thing*. The defence is write-side (admission,
contradiction resolution, credit assignment), which is where R55–R56 put it.

**The readback said `ABANDONED`, and the reason is a defect in the readback.** Two graded lines
contradicted each other on one pair of numbers: `near is worse than far` passed at −3.51pp against
+0.00pp while the refutation fired on the same two values, "indistinguishable, inside a drift of
3.51pp". The prediction read `near_pp - far_pp > -drift`, which is "near is not much *better* than
far" — it passes when near is worse, equal, or better by up to the drift. A predicted order needs the
gap in the direction the order names, so it now reads `near_pp - far_pp > drift` (`4a638b3`). The
three-arm reading changes from "one prediction failed" to "one prediction failed and the ladder's
first rung does not exist", which is the sentence the data supports.

**`adversarial`'s job was red, and not for the arm's reason.** The pair measured HARM, which for a
distractor is the prediction being confirmed, and `l4-paired` no longer blocks on it (`4083945`). The
block was `V5-resolution`: the artefact had published `the memory costs accuracy: -7.02pp` — the
sentence `HARM` carries — at a sample whose minimum detectable difference is 20.86pp. The gate was
right and the artefact was wrong: on a planted arm the loss is the distractor's, and attributing it to
the memory is a false sentence in a machine-readable file. A planted pair now reports `claim: null`
and the state stays (`fc28a34`), so `V5` reads `claims no direction`, which is true. `adversarial` was
re-dispatched on that commit; the numbers above are from the run before it and the re-run is a
reproduction rather than a new measurement.

**And coverage reached 100 on all four dimensions, reproducibly.** The campaign is in 172.49; this
stretch closed the last twenty branches, nine by tests and nine by removing fallbacks no input could
reach (`present()` in the kernel states the invariant and throws), and two by writing a guarantee as a
property of the writer rather than as a branch (`curate`'s tie-break is the sort's stability over a
bucket that already arrives in id order; `journal` appends the newline per row rather than per file).
The last one, `sql-guard`'s send callback, read 100% on one full run and 99.98% on the next, on the
same suite — it is reached when `close()` races the write, and the existing case waited 150 ms first.
A case that closes with no delay at all makes it deterministic, and three consecutive runs report no
gap (`d5b6ee6`).

### 172.53 The arm became a line in the registration, and three 2026 sources price the ladder

**The dispatch menu ran out, and the workaround was the defect.** R57 has three distractor arms.
`TAU_PLANTED_RULES` is a repository variable, a variable is global, and `sota.yml` is at its
twenty-five-input ceiling — so "run the ladder" meant three six-hour runs that could not overlap, and
the *next* experiment was one forgotten `PATCH` away from measuring a distractor nobody had declared.
The scenario pair and the recall floor were already registration-header values; the arm was the only
per-experiment value still living outside the experiment.

| before | after |
| --- | --- |
| `TAU_PLANTED_RULES` repository variable, read by `l4` | `plantedArms: far,near,adversarial` in the prereg header |
| one arm per dispatch, three dispatches, no overlap | one `arms` job renders a matrix, `l4` fans out, `fail-fast: false` |
| artefact `l4-evidence` overwritten per run | `l4-evidence-<arm>`, one per leg |
| a round with no arm left the variable as the last round set it | a round with no `plantedArms` emits `[""]` and plants nothing |

`""` is the value the driver already reads as "plant nothing", so the control leg needs no branch
anywhere — the empty case is a matrix element, not an `if`. `plantedArmMatrix` is exported and tested
per shape (列表、无头、重复、非法名、空声明), and `pnpm eval:prereg-arms` is the renderer the workflow
calls, so the matrix the job fans out over is a value a test can inspect rather than a `yq` expression
in YAML.

**The validator a dispatch runs first was grading the last build.** `pnpm eval:prereg` refused R57 with
`unknown key: plantedArms` — about a key its own source had just declared. The cause: `bin/prereg.ts`
was the one bin in the repository importing `@agentix-e/microglia-eval`, which resolves to `dist/`, so
the first thing a dispatch checks was the previous compilation. Every other bin imports `../`; this one
does now too. The general lesson is worth a line: **a CLI that resolves its own package name is testing
the build, not the source**, and it will keep passing until the day it is supposed to fail.

**Three 2026 sources, and what each one prices.** Read after R57's three arms, so they were graded
against a measurement rather than absorbed as background (`COMPETITIVE`, 2026-11-09):

| source | the number | what it says about our defect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MemPoison (arXiv 2607.14651) | write-time consistency leaves L1 ≈5%, L2 ≈23%, L3 ≈28% | a check that compares a claim **to the store** removes one grade of three |
| GhostWriter / AM-Sentry (arXiv 2607.06595) | inject ~98%, activate ~60% | excess loss per *use* is not excess loss per *task*; we measure only the former |
| InMind | direct query ~100%, implicit association 14.4% | "the memory is not reached" is not our failure mode |

The first one is the important one, because it explains an asymmetry R57 measured and could not
explain: `near` — true, relevant rules — cost **nothing** (−3.51pp, i.e. it repaired more than it
broke), and `adversarial` — rules that agree with the store and contradict the episode — cost
**7.02pp**. A rule that agrees with the episode can be ignored by the reader; the expensive rule is the
one that agrees with everything the reader already holds. That is MemPoison's L2, and it is the grade
write-time consistency cannot see.

The third one is a correction to how our own relevance panel should be read. R26's `retrieval_relevance`
splits packs into on-topic (663 questions, 50.98% with memory vs 52.19% without) and off-topic (871,
60.28% vs 61.77%). The 9.3pp absolute gap between the rows is **difficulty, not harm** — a question that
needs a rule is a hard question — and the effect is the delta: −1.21pp vs −1.49pp, 0.28pp apart, both
inside a 1.96pp minimum detectable difference. **Relevance predicts difficulty, not harm**, which is why
a relevance-filtered retriever cannot fix this and why the next mechanism is a contradiction gate rather
than a better retriever.

### 172.54 The denominator was never measured, and it is 43%

Four BIRD dev artefacts, four configurations, one number in a 1.5pp window: **42.8% to 44.3% of
questions produce byte-identical SQL with and without memory.** The pack changed nothing observable on
those, so they cannot carry any of the effect, and every delta over tasks in this repository has been
dividing by 1534 where the mechanism acted on 854–877.

| artefact | identical | changed | won / lost | per task | per change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `poc-sota-bird-dev` | 680 (44.3%) | 854 | 47 / 68 | −1.37pp | −2.46pp |
| `R24-dev-split` | 662 (43.2%) | 872 | 64 / 73 | −0.59pp | −1.03pp |
| `R26-channels` | 657 (42.8%) | 877 | 67 / 62 | +0.33pp | +0.57pp |
| `R37-lexicon-grain` | 666 (43.4%) | 868 | 78 / 67 | +0.72pp | +1.27pp |

`eval/verifiers/use_rate.py` computes it from the two SQL strings the harness already writes, so the
measurement cost nothing and needed no dispatch. The 56–57% effective share is the same quantity
AM-Sentry reports as ~60% activation, from an independent instrument — theirs asks whether a memory was
used, ours asks whether the output moved.

**Two states exist so that the number cannot be quoted when it is not there.** A artefact where every
case produced the same SQL is `NO_MEASUREMENT`, not 0% — there is no change to take a rate over. And an
artefact where two identical SQL strings carry two different verdicts is `INCONSISTENT`, because then
`predictedSql` and `correct` describe different runs and no rate over them means anything. Both have
fixtures; the second one is a two-row artefact that contradicts itself, which is the only way to prove
the check can say no.

**The direction of the bound is written down rather than assumed.** Identical text proves the memory did
nothing; differing text does not prove it did something, because the decoder may have sampled
differently. So 43% is a lower bound on not-using and 57% an upper bound on using. A denominator, not an
attribution — and the reason the per-change column is the one a cross-system comparison should quote.

| BIRD memory effect, per change | not measured | **+1.27pp** |

### 172.55 The adversarial re-run died on a rate limit, and the limit was in the wrong unit

`42568927112` ran fifty minutes and failed both legs at 06:36, one minute apart:

```
RateLimitError: your current concurrency is 6, which exceeds your concurrency limit of 5
               based on your remaining balance
```

The lane was passing `TAU_CONCURRENCY=2`. Both numbers are honest and they count different things:
`max_concurrency` is tau2's **task** count, the provider's is a **request** count, and an episode holds
an agent, a user-simulator and an evaluator call at once — so two tasks are five or six requests. The
limit is also a function of the account balance, which is why a value that had been in place since the
lane was built was refused for the first time on the longest run it has ever attempted.

| item | state |
| --- | --- |
| the unit confusion, expressed at the value (`fc23de1`) | **fixed**, task-level 1 |
| `litellm`'s `num_retries=4` retrying at the same concurrency | **open** — four attempts at one refusal, then `run_tasks` dies with all 228 episodes |
| R57 `adversarial` clean artefact | **blocked** on the account, not on the code |
| the three-arm readback | unchanged — it still rests on the three separate dispatches |
| DeepSeek account | **needs topping up**; concurrency falls with balance and every l4 run is long |

**What this means for the plan rather than for the paper.** Nothing about R57's numbers changes — the
three reads stand and Amendment 3's reproduction is still the right next dispatch, it simply cannot be
dispatched against a balance that caps concurrency at 5. Two conclusions follow, and they are ordered:

1. **No further l4 dispatch until the account is topped up.** A 6-hour matrix that dies at minute 50
   costs three legs and returns nothing, and it does that by design rather than by accident: the
   retry does not lower what it is retrying at.
2. **The work that does not need the provider goes first.** `use_rate.py` (172.54) and the coverage and
   documentation work needed no calls at all; R63's contradiction gate is implementation plus tests
   before it is a dispatch, and it can be built while the account is sorted out.

| reading | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TAU_CONCURRENCY` default | 2 (task-level) | **1** |
| arms lost to a rate limit | 0 | **2** (`42568927112`) |
| open defects on the l4 lane | 0 | **1** — a retry that does not lower its concurrency |

### 172.56 The bill had four causes, none of them visible from inside the lane

A day of dispatches cost more than it should have, and the first finding is that **nothing in the
repository could say why**: `calls: 0` on every arm in `eval/results/history/`, no token count, no
cache-hit rate, no money. The four causes were found by reading the agent and the rate card (`AUDIT`
34.94), and three of the four share one shape — **a number about an experiment that the experiment did
not choose.**

| # | cause | the number it moved | state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the pack was recalled **per turn**, so the second system message changed on every call and the prefix cache broke after it | memory-arm input billed at the **miss** rate on the whole history, against the reference arm's **hit** rate | **fixed** (`a276f80`) |
| 2 | the same line made the treatment different every turn | every published facade arm measured a *sequence*, not a store | **fixed**, registered (`R57` Amendment 4) |
| 3 | `deepseek-chat` is retired and silently routes to a model whose **thinking mode is on by default** | reasoning tokens at the output rate, every turn of every episode, for a tool call | **fixed** (pinned name + `thinking: disabled`, both arms) |
| 4 | peak is exactly **double**, and every long leg started inside one | ×2 on everything | **measured**; scheduling is an operator action |
| — | a retry that does not lower its concurrency | a refused run is four refusals and a dead job | **open** |

The schedule detail is worth recording because it is not a code defect: peak is 01:00–04:00 and
06:00–10:00 UTC, which is 09:00–18:00 in UTC+8, and the four consecutive R57 legs started at `05:43`,
`03:28`, `01:18` and `00:28`. **The lane's schedule was set by the operator's time zone, at a factor
of two.**

**What the lane can now say about itself.** `usage_stats()` reports prompt, completion,
`prompt_cache_hit_tokens`, the derived uncached share, the cache-hit rate, and the bill in both bands
with the rate card and its date. Every phase prints it, and the driver writes one unconditional
`[tau2] usage:` line beside the score. Two self-checks run without tau2 or litellm installed — 10
cases for the agent's recall clock, 12 for the arithmetic and the calendar — because a test that needs
a 400MB benchmark to check a loop counter does not run in `pnpm check`.

**What it costs to copy the leaderboard, and what it costs to keep the bill down.** Read in the same

human metadata, +3.6pp fused — everything above 63 on MiniDev is *SQL-first schema linking* and

because the SQL is already generated and its columns and literals are free supervision. Multi-candidate
selection costs **×3–5** and is therefore last, submitted-only. **The ordering that saves money and the
ordering that raises the score happen to agree for the first two items and disagree only on the third.**

### 172.57 The instrument could not see the effects, and the artefacts contained the answer

Three readings this round, all from data that was already committed, none of which cost a dispatch.

**The `k` in `pass^k` was choosing the answer.** Every four-trial run also contains `pass^1`..`pass^3`,
so re-reading the same 228 episodes at each `k` is free arithmetic. For R57's three arms:

| arm | k=1 | k=2 | k=3 | k=4 | spread | sign stable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `far` | +0.00 | −8.77 | −1.75 | +0.00 | 8.77pp | yes |
| `near` | +3.51 | −3.51 | −7.02 | −3.51 | **10.53pp** | **no** |
| `adversarial` | +5.26 | +7.02 | +14.04 | +7.02 | 8.78pp | yes |

Not one cell reaches p<0.05 (best: `adversarial` at `pass^3`, p=0.096, and that is not the registered
`k`). At `n=57` the smallest detectable effect at 80% power is **17.0–20.9pp**; the observed 7.02pp
would need **504 tasks**. So the "contradictory rule costs 7pp" sentence, which went into three
internal documents and a competitive analysis, is withdrawn (`prereg/R57-toxicity.md` Amendment 5).

Trials were the expensive dimension and the one that bought nothing: `pass^4` compresses four draws into
one per task, so the discordant count *grows* with `k` (16 pairs at `k=1`, 18 at `k=4`) and the paired
interval with it — ±14.59pp at `k=4` against ±13.75pp at `k=1`. **Four trials produced a wider interval
than one would have, at four times the cost.** And the control arm, an identical condition, moved
14.04pp at `pass^2` and 5.26pp at `pass^4` across three dispatches, against a drift constant of 3.51pp
taken from a single pair.

**31% of the remaining errors are a table the model should not have read.** The per-case record splits
them: `table-extra` 94 (6.13pp), `table-missing` 47 (3.06pp), `table-both` 62 (4.04pp), same-tables
445. **Schema linking's ceiling on this artefact is 13.23pp** — repairing every table-selection error
takes 57.76% to 70.99%. `table-extra` at double `table-missing` says the model over-reaches, so the
lever is a sharper pruner; the share rises to 42–43% on `challenging` questions.

**And then the arm that had already run.** Reading every artefact's `arms` field — 63 readings across
30 artefacts, none of them ever read in aggregate — produced the largest effect in the repository and
its sign is wrong:

| arm | delta | broke | repaired | p | n |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `oracle` | +33.14pp | 0 | 116 | 2.4e-35 | 350 |
| **`linked`** | **−9.58pp** | **202** | **55** | **6.4e-21** | **1534** |
| `full-noevidence` | −16.30pp | 300 | 50 | 1.4e-44 | 1534 |
| `values` | +5.43pp | 11 | 30 | 4.3e-03 | 350 |
| `values` | +0.85pp | 74 | 87 | 3.4e-01 | 1534 |
| `gated` | +0.29pp | 0 | 1 | 1.0e+00 | 350 |

Schema linking, which MCS-SQL prices at +2.1 points, **costs 9.58pp here**, and the same artefact says
why: that arm's errors where a gold table is absent go 107 → 291 and 44 predictions lose their `FROM`.
The pruner removed tables the answer needed.

The oracle row is the other half of the message: **on the same 350 questions the benchmark's own hint is
worth +33.14pp and every product-side arm is worth under one point.** That is where the headroom is.

### 172.58 The additive linker exists, and it is the arm the regression asked for

`linked` is the largest effect in this repository and its sign is wrong: −9.58pp at p=6.4e-21, 202
questions broken against 55 repaired, with the mechanism visible in the same file — errors where a gold
table is absent go 107 → 291, and 44 predictions lose their `FROM`. The failure is structural rather
than a tuning error: a pruner decides before the SQL exists, so when it is wrong the model cannot ask
for what it cannot see, and no threshold changes that. The guard the function already carries (decline
when nothing matches, decline when the key closure covers two thirds of the database) fires on the easy
cases and leaves BIRD's thirteen-table dumps room to prune a bridge table two joins away.

`annotateSchema` is the variant that cannot reproduce that failure. It keeps every table, moves the
named ones to the front, and prefixes two lines: how many tables the question names, and that none was
removed. The only things it adds are recoverable by a reader that ignores them, which is what makes it
free beta on the literature's claim — a model is more reliable at writing SQL than at selecting tables,
so anything that draws attention without removing options is upside with no downside.

| item | state |
| --- | --- |
| `annotateSchema` in `packages/sql/src/schema-link.ts` | **done**, six cases |
| the `linked-additive` arm and its channel floor | **done** — a run where the header never appears is refused, not published as a null |
| `ChannelKind` as a named union, `CHANNEL_FLOORS` as a `Record` over it | **done** — "add a channel without a floor" is now a compile error, and four copies of `'values' \| 'linked'` that had to be edited together are gone |
| measured delta | **pending the next BIRD dispatch** |

**What the arm can and cannot conclude.** It cannot conclude anything about pruning — that question is
closed. It can say whether ordering and labelling are worth anything, and a null result is the useful
one: it would mean the lever is not attention but verification, and the next variant generates a
candidate SQL first and repairs an identifier that does not resolve instead of hiding the table it
lived in. That is AskData's mechanism, and this repository now has the measurement that says why it
matters — theirs never removes a table either.

### 172.59 The bill is now part of the instrument, and the ceiling was measured before it was bought

Round 62 fixes the measurement gap on the lane that runs on a schedule, and spends no model calls
doing it. The order was deliberate: the previous round's P0 was a dispatch of `linked-additive`, and
dispatching an arm whose ordering signal had never been measured would have been the mistake this
repository keeps finding in its own history.

**What the BIRD lane could not say, and now can.**

| question | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what did this run cost | nothing was recorded | `usd`, `peak_usd`, `usd_if_all_off_peak` in the artefact and on stdout |
| how much of the prompt was cached | discarded | `prompt_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `cache_hit_rate` |
| was thinking on, and what did it cost | never sent, never read | `SOTA_THINKING`, `reasoning_tokens` |
| which model answered | the retired id was recorded | `deepseek-flash` by default, `model` beside `configured_model` |
| what does the weekly run cost extra | 03:00 UTC Monday, double | 18:00 UTC Monday, single |

The rate card moved to `eval/manifests/model-rates.json` and has two readers: `packages/eval/src/cost.ts`
and `eval/drivers/tau2/run_split.py`. Both used to hold their own copy. A test asserts the TypeScript
constant equals the file; a Python self-check asserts the driver's bill and its peak windows equal it.
**A price that appears in two languages is a price that is eventually wrong in one of them.**

**The bug the instrument found on its first run.**

`schemaBlocks` returned zero blocks for a backticked `CREATE TABLE`. BIRD's dumps use three quoting
conventions and the identifier pattern knew two, so `toxicology`, `thrombosis_prediction` and
`student_club` parsed to nothing — and `annotateSchema` treats a zero-block schema as `single-table`
and returns the DDL unchanged. The arm that was about to be dispatched was **inert on three of eleven
databases**, and its null would have been published as a statement about ordering. Two more defects
came out of the same check: a foreign key's target table arriving as a column of this one, and
case-sensitive name matching that made 298 of 1,534 questions unscoreable (`postHistory` declared,
`posthistory` queried).

**The ceiling, measured for free.**

| signal | clean | mean depth | precision | recall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| anchors (shipped) | 42.89% | 49.63% | 49.98% | 87.38% |
| recalled, k=5 | 56.58% | 44.04% | 47.93% | 95.05% |
| both, recall first | **56.65%** | **43.00%** | 39.27% | **99.66%** |

**+13.75pp of clean orderings, [10.30, 16.88], p < 1e-4, n=1,534, zero model calls.** Anchors add
0.07pp over recall alone and cost 8.7 points of precision, so the ordering to ship is recall-first
with anchors as the fallback. The ceiling is 56.65% and not 100%: four questions in ten have gold
tables that no table-set signal determines, which is why an ordering arm cannot be expected to
deliver the 13.23pp that `error_budget` prices schema linking at.

| lanes | — | `pnpm eval:table-recall` (zero calls) |

**What this changes for the next round.** The recall-first ordering is a mechanism the lane does not

### 172.60 The arm the ceiling chose, and the stand-in that proved it before it was paid for

Round 63 lands `recall-order` — the arm the free measurement argued for — and it does it in the only
order that makes the number trustworthy: the mechanism was measured first (round 62, zero calls),
then built out of the same functions the measurement uses, then proved against a stand-in endpoint,
then registered, then dispatched.

**What the arm is.** The schema keeps every table; the ones the nearest five training questions in
the same database read come first, the lexical anchors after them, the rest in declaration order.
One decision separates it from `linked-additive`, which is what makes the comparison paired: the
ordering *inside* the moved group.

| | `linked-additive` (control) | `recall-order` (new) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what moves a table to the front | a word in the question | the gold table set of the five nearest training questions |
| the order inside the moved group | declaration order | the signal's own priority |
| measured clean orderings, dev | 42.89% | **56.65%** |
| tables moved per question | — | 4.88 |
| prompts changed | — | 1,534 of 1,534 |

**Why the shared implementation is the point.** `bin/table-recall.ts` no longer builds its own
neighbour pool; it calls `goldIndex` and `recalledFor`, the two functions `runFold` calls. Re-run
against the dev split it reproduces its predecessor exactly — 42.89 / 56.58 / 56.65 and +13.75pp
[+10.30, +16.88] — and that reproduction is the only evidence that the mechanism being paid for is
the mechanism that was measured.

One trap came out of the refactor and is now a comment where it happened: regrouping the loop by fold
permuted the paired vector, and the seeded bootstrap returned [10.63, 17.01] instead of [10.30, 16.88]
for identical data. A bootstrap interval is not bit-invariant to permutation, and an interval that
moves when nothing moved cannot be compared against itself. The array is filled at the row's own
position now.

**Proved before it was paid for, for the first time in this lane.** `DEEPSEEK_ENDPOINT` has existed
for rounds; this is the first arm to use it. A 40-line HTTP server answering `SELECT 1`, twenty
questions on the dev split:

```
[sota] arm linked-additive: 5.00%
[sota] arm recall-order: 5.00%
[sota] recall-order: clean=13/20 (65.00%) depth=35.44% precision=39.19% recall=96.67% retrieved=80.00% k=5
[sota] model=deepseek-flash thinking=provider-default [sota] usage: prompt=142,800 (cached=95,200, 66.7%)
       completion=4,760 bill=$0.0103 (peak 0.0%) reasoning=0
[sota] failed: MG_E_CONFIG: The benchmark ran but cannot support a claim (V5-resolution: not estimable …)
```

Both arms fired, the ordering block was computed from the prompts actually sent, the bill was
computed from the parsed usage, and the run then refused to publish a claim — which is the gate doing
its job on a stand-in that answers every question the same way.

**Two dispatch failures, both before any spend.**

| what happened | what caught it | what changed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prereg` input given as `prereg/R63-recall-order.md`, which the description read as a path | the `Which lane this dispatch buys` job, in eleven seconds and zero calls | the input is documented as a bare id and the step refuses a path, naming the fix in the message |
| the same string also names the artefact | — | the refusal now happens before the artefact name is used, so a typo cannot lose a twenty-minute run into a subdirectory nobody publishes |

`preregFileOf` normalises all three forms (`id`, `id.md`, `prereg/id.md`) for the CLI, which does
take a path; the dispatch refuses the path instead, because two places build the file name from it
and only one of them is in TypeScript.

**Registered before it ran.** `prereg/R63-recall-order.md`: the arm fires on ≥95% of questions, the
clean share lands within ±5pp of 56.65%, `retrieved_share` above 90%, accuracy within ±4pp of zero,
the memory arm still null, the bill computable, the lane reliable. And the resolution stated in the
file rather than in a footnote: **at n=350 the design resolves about 6pp**, so a 2pp effect can be
neither confirmed nor refuted, and a null from 350 questions is not evidence of absence.

### 172.61 The population was measured before it was paid for, and it was five times smaller

The round opened with two questions and closed both of them without a wasted dispatch.

**R63 published.** `recall-order` on minidev, n=350, 1,923 calls, $0.2165 off-peak: `full` +0.57pp
[−2.86, +4.00], `linked-additive` **+2.00pp** [−0.29, +4.29], `recall-order` **+0.86pp** [−1.43,
+3.14]. All blocking gates pass, parse 100.00%, `reasoning_tokens` 0. The free ceiling it was
dispatched against — +13.75pp of ordering quality — converts to under a point of accuracy, which is
the branch the registration named in advance: **the ordering line is closed for accuracy** and the
next P0 in that line is the retrieved-exemplar arm (the nearest training question's gold SQL as a
worked example), the lawful approximation of `oracle` at +33.14pp.

**R64's population, measured for free.** `pnpm eval:retry-population` re-executes the baseline
statements in an existing artefact against the split's databases and counts what a retry arm would
have acted on: `minidev 26/350 (7.43%)`, `dev 98/1534 (6.39%)`, `no-query=0`. The registration had
predicted ≥140 on minidev by reading base accuracy as failure count; a retry acts on what the
*pipeline* rejected, not on what was wrong. The floor cannot be reached on either split, and R64 is
amended to `dev` with a floor of 90 before dispatch rather than after.

**What the empty results are.** Same pass, no extra cost: of the 89 empty results on dev,
**54 (60.67%) read exactly the gold tables** and **32 (35.96%) are missing a gold value** — the
classic value-spelling miss. Only 35 are table-selection misses, the bucket R63 just measured as not
moving. The retry line's deficit is values, not schema text, and that is recorded in the amendment
before the arm is dispatched.

**And the mechanism is now one function.** `retryTriggerOf` holds the three conditions; the lane's
retry prompts and the audit both call it, so the population counted and the population acted on
cannot disagree. Every artefact from here records `retry_population` per run and `retryReason` per
question — the number that was prose for twenty rounds is now a field.

## 173 — The retry was worth one point, and the bar could not have been cleared

R64 published, the only two-digit arm in the register was implemented, and both findings are about
documents disagreeing with the things that read them.

### 173.1 One rejection in five is repaired, and the ceiling is the population

Run `42661260446`, `dev`, n=1,534, 5 folds, 5,241 calls, 0 call failures, **$0.44**, cache 73.79%,
band `off_peak`. Every amended prediction held: 98 retried questions, a repaired rate of **20.41%**
[13.27, 28.57] (p = 1.9e-06), a net delta of **+1.30pp** [+0.78, +1.89] with **20 gained and 0 lost**.
`full` was null for the fourth time: +0.07pp, 87 gained / 86 lost.

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| retried population | 98 / 1,534 = 6.39% (`empty` 88, `error` 10, `no-query` 0) |
| repaired | 20 / 98 = 20.41%, spread over all five folds (1, 3, 5, 6, 5) |
| by trigger | `empty` 19/88 = 21.6%, `error` 1/10 = 10.0% |
| by difficulty | simple 14/49, moderate 5/41, challenging 1/8 |
| ceiling if every rejection were repaired | **+6.39pp** — this arm took a fifth of it |

The zero-cost measurement made before the dispatch from R63's artefact predicted 98 and produced 98;
one question moved from `empty` to `error`. That is the smallest error a measurement that spends
nothing can have, and it is the reason the floor was amended from 140 to 90 *before* the run rather
than after it.

### 173.2 The promotion bar was above the band it was paired with

Promotion required the repaired rate's lower bound to exceed 25%; the bound is 13.27%. Closing required
the upper bound to fall below 10%; it is 28.57%. The result therefore sits in the only region the
document did not assign, and neither bar is wrong in isolation — both are wrong *together* with the
prediction they sit beside:

- at n = 98 a rate near 20% carries a standard error of about 4.1pp, so a lower bound above 25% needs a
  point estimate near **35%** — the top of the predicted band, not the middle the document said to
  expect;
- a promotion condition expressed as an interval bound is strictly more demanding than the same
  condition expressed as a point estimate, by a margin that is easy to write and hard to notice.

Recorded as **Rule 10** in the roadmap: a promotion bar is part of the prediction and must be reachable
by it. The mechanism is neither promoted nor closed, and that outcome is now written into the
registration rather than left to the next reader to interpret.

### 173.3 One stale default, found by reading the artefact against the document

`retry_population.meetsFloor` came back **false**. The registration had lowered the floor to 90 two
hours before the dispatch; the lane's constant still said 140. The value now lives beside the
summariser that reports it and a test asserts it equals the figure R64's amendment registers, so the
next amendment has to touch code rather than only prose. This is the third instance of the same class
in this record — a number that lives in a document and a number that lives in a lane — and the first
one fixed at the seam instead of at the instance.

### 173.4 The `examples` arm exists, and its void conditions are a gate

`oracle` at **+33.14pp** is the largest positive in the record and is undeployable: it injects the
memory item whose evidence is the question being asked. R65 was registered before the code existed, and
the code now exists:

- **Same database only** — a gold query names tables that exist in one schema; a neighbour from another
  database is not a weaker example, it is an unusable one;
- **the tree's own similarity** — `similarityOf`, the function table recall already ranks with, so the
  two arms move together if retrieval is ever replaced;
- **whole exemplars or none** — the 1,200-character cap drops the last exemplars instead of truncating
  one, because a truncated `WHERE` clause is a wrong query the model is invited to copy.

`V75-exemplars-delivered` turns R65's two void conditions (fires on ≥80% of questions, cap hit on ≤5%)
into a blocking gate, pushed whenever the arm is configured — including when it fired on nothing, which
is a wiring defect rather than a vacuous pass.

the commit that moved it was pushed unverified. A green check is a statement about a tree, not about a
session.

### 173.5 The exemplars were worth four points, and the replication is why we know

R65 was the register's last two-digit lever. Three valid dispatches of the same deterministic prompt —
`42729684852`, `42732114335`, `42732137586` — on minidev, n=350, each about 1,440 calls and $0.12–0.22:

| run | `none` | `full` | `examples` | `examples − full` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 51.14% | 50.86% (−0.29) | **56.57% (+5.43)** [1.43, 9.43] | +5.71 [1.71, 9.71] |
| 2 | 52.57% | 51.71% (−0.86) | **55.71% (+3.14)** [−0.86, 7.14] | +4.00 [0.00, 8.00] |
| 3 | 52.57% | 52.29% (−0.29) | **55.43% (+2.86)** [−0.86, 6.57] | +3.14 [−0.86, 7.14] |
| **pooled** | — | **null on all three** | **+3.81pp**, 95 / 55, n=1,050, p=0.0014 | **+4.28pp** |

The first dispatch of the arm was **void by its own gate**: at the registered 1,200-character budget the
third exemplar did not fit on 34 of 350 questions (9.71% against a 5% allowance), the lane refused the
run, and `V75` published the reason instead of a claim. Amendment 1 raised the budget to 1,600 and left
the hypothesis, the dose and the thresholds untouched; the re-run delivered three exemplars on 98.3% of
questions and passed all thirteen gates.

Three things follow, and the second is the one that changes how this project reports.

1. **The two-digit lever is closed.** Three correct worked examples from the same database are worth
   about **four points**, so `oracle`'s +33.14pp is a fact about the answer key rather than about the
   prompt. The registration said in advance that a delta inside ±4pp would mean exactly that, and the
   pooled estimate is inside it.
2. **The interval in an artefact is conditional on the dispatch.** The same arm read +5.43, +3.14 and
   +2.86 on three runs with identical prompt content, and the controls moved with it: `none` by up to
   1.43pp, `full` by 3.14pp on a store that differed by four distillations. At n=350 the dispatch spread
   is 3–4pp — the width of the bootstrap interval itself. **Rule 13** now requires a mechanism to be
   replicated before it is believed, and R65 is the first arm this project has priced that way.
3. **The branches of a refutation have to tile.** R65's valid run landed at +5.43pp: above the +4pp
   close and below the +6pp promote. R64 landed in a gap of the same kind. **Rule 12** now requires an
   ordered partition with a named outcome for every region, and R67 is written that way.

**R67 is registered and undispatched.** The prompt's content is spent — ordering +0.86pp, memory null
on four splits, exemplars +3.81pp, pruning −9.58pp — and the published pipelines that reach 66–78% on
BIRD do it by drawing several queries and selecting one. `sample-5-first`, `-random`, `-exec`, `-prior`
and an oracle pool ceiling, four branches that partition the space, and two dispatches from the start
because of Rule 13.

**And one process failure worth recording.** R67's first commit went out with a red `eval:protocol`
check: the Refutation section used a numbered list where the checker wants bullets, and the check had
been piped into `tail -2`, whose exit status is the pipeline's. The repository was fixed in the next
commit, the CI run on the broken commit is the evidence, and the rule is now "never pipe a gate into a
pager".

### 173.6 A 7B model beating us is a statement about its scaffold, and the confound is now removable

DPC's re-runs put Qwen2.5-Coder-7B at **48.6%** with DAIL-SQL+SC, **53.0%** as XiYanCoder-7B and
**66.2%** with CHESS+SC on BIRD dev; this lane reads **58.02%** single-pass. At a fixed model the
scaffold is worth **+17.6pp**; at a fixed scaffold class our single draw is **+9.4pp ahead** of
theirs. So the thing to copy is CHESS's three stages, not the 7B — and the record already has measured
opinions on two of them (value retrieval is load-bearing and our empty executions are 36% value
misses; XiYan's selection model is −2.74 EX when removed, GradeSQL's outcome reward +4.33, our own
model-comparison selector −1.14pp, which is why `exec-signature.ts` compares shapes).

What was missing was not reading: it was that the comparison could not be **run** here. The model id
and the endpoint were variables and the credential was not, so a backbone swap would have spent
DeepSeek's key on another provider's host, tripped the breaker and been reported as a dead endpoint.
That is fixed in `packages/eval/src/credential.ts` — `SOTA_API_KEY` where the lane points,
`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` only at `api.deepseek.com` and at a stand-in on this machine, refusal before the
first call otherwise, and `model_credential` in the artefact so two backbones stay tellable apart.
**R68** is registered on top of it: R67's three arms, one host, one variable moved, ceiling share
reported on both backbones, and Rule 14 — *absolute points are not comparable across baselines; the
share of the ceiling is* — is the axis both rows finally share.

### 173.7 The retry learns the spelling, and the backbone becomes a variable

Two registrations that had been sitting undispatched are now runnable, and one of them was not when
it was dispatched.

**R66 `retry-values` is implemented.** R64 repaired 20 of 98 rejects and 19 came from the empty
bucket; 32 of the 89 empty results read exactly the gold tables and filtered on a value the database
does not spell that way. The arm appends, per literal the failed attempt wrote, one line: what it
wrote and what the column actually holds. Built from the attempt's own text plus a read of the
database at **zero model calls**, so it costs exactly the 98 calls `retry-blank` costs — which is the
whole reason it is registered at dev rather than at minidev. `V76-values-delivered` implements the
file's own void condition (fires on < 30% of empty retries) as a blocking gate, on the `V75`
precedent. Dispatch `42747637476`, dev, n = 1,534, in flight at the time of writing.

**The 5-draw execution selector did not exist.** R67's first dispatch, `42747647806`, died in two
seconds: `Unknown arm 'sample-5-exec'`. The selector has been in `SAMPLING_SELECTORS` since they were
factored into one list, the parser accepts any `sample-N-SELECTOR`, `sample-3-exec` is a registered
arm — so the formula was constructible, plannable and absent from `OPTIONAL_ARMS`, which is the list
membership is checked against. This is the third instance in two iterations of **one fact with two
representations where only one was updated**: `RETRY_POPULATION_FLOOR` stayed 140 while the
amendment said 90; `retry-values` was registered while the arm did not exist (R66's own header says
so); now an arm whose parser form exists but whose name does not. R66 wrote the sentence about
itself; R67 assumed the machinery. The refusal cost two seconds and no calls, which is the right
price; the arm is in the union, pinned by the test that pins every other arm, and R67 records the
void dispatch as Outcome 0 rather than deleting it. Re-dispatched as `42749802682`.

**The backbone is a dispatch input, and it took two attempts to get right.** `SOTA_MODEL` was a
repository variable that the distillation cache key also read, so a backbone swap was a global
mutation two backbones could not share. The first design added three inputs — `model`, `endpoint`,
`credential` — and that was the original defect wearing a fix: it could move the host and leave this
provider's key behind. The repository's workflow linter then refused the file outright, for declaring
28 `workflow_dispatch` inputs against GitHub's cap of 25. The answer is **one** input, `backbone`,
with a closed vocabulary: empty leaves every published run where it was, `zhipu:MODEL` moves the
model, the host and the key together. `density_panel` became a repository variable at the same
default to pay for the slot — the precedent this file already set for `template` and
`sample_temperature`. `SOTA_ENDPOINT` joins `SOTA_API_KEY`; `DEEPSEEK_ENDPOINT` still works, because
every rehearsal here uses it.

Gate state: 3,857 tests over 187 files, four coverage dimensions at **100%**, `pnpm check` green,
coupling ledger 176 modules / 17 deferred / `core` 0.

### 173.8 The pool holds 8.85 points and the selectors cannot see any of them

Dispatch `42749802682`, minidev, n = 350, 5 folds, **2,930 calls, $0.4708** at 100% peak pricing
($0.2354 off-peak), cache 77.4%, 1,750 candidates signed and reconciled, all gates green.

| arm | accuracy | vs `none` | vs `sample-5-first` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | 52.29% | — | — |
| `full` | 51.43% | −0.86pp [−4.00, +2.00], p = 0.71 | — |
| `sample-5-first` | 50.86% | −1.43pp, p = 0.42 | — |
| `sample-5-random` | 52.00% | −0.29pp | **+1.14pp** |
| `sample-5-exec` | 52.00% | −0.29pp | **+1.14pp** |
| `sample-5-prior` | 53.14% | +0.86pp, p = 0.70 | **+2.28pp** |
| `sample-5-oracle` | **59.71%** | +7.43pp, p < 1e-4 | **+8.85pp** |

Four readings.

**Temperature costs 1.43pp; the pool repays 8.85.** Five draws at T = 0.7 contain the answer on
8.85pp more questions than the first draw — below R67's predicted +10…+25pp, which is the prediction
being wrong in the conservative direction and is recorded as such.

**Execution-shape selection is worth exactly a coin flip.** `sample-5-exec` and `sample-5-random` are
not approximately equal, they are the same number: 52.00%, +1.14pp over `first`, 12.9% of the
ceiling. And the reason is measured rather than argued: on the 120 disagreeing questions (296 pairs)
**every one of the seven signals has an AUC interval straddling 0.5** — draw-order 0.510 [0.421,
0.596], null-share 0.492, empty 0.535, duplicate-share 0.537, column-shape 0.541, value-type 0.542,
row-shape 0.546. A selector built from signals that cannot rank cannot rank.

**The prior selector is the only one above chance** (+2.28pp, 25.8% of the ceiling) and its own
report says not to trust it: `db-signature` reads +10.00pp on 80 questions, 36 with any support,
in sample — an upper bound for a verifier, not a result.

**The branch that fires is R67's own third one: narrow to the pool.** `exec − first` is under +8pp
(1.14) *and* the ceiling is under +15pp (8.85), so the registration's instruction is to widen or
diversify generation before any further selector work. **R69 is registered** on exactly that: k = 10
at the existing temperature, and k = 5 at T = 1.0, two dispatches, ceiling and ceiling-share as the
axis. Its arms (`sample-10-*`) are the same class of gap that cost R67 a dispatch, and the file says
so in its header rather than discovering it at runtime.

**R66 is still in flight** (`42750334097`, dev, n = 1,534, 15,000-call cap). Its first attempt,
`42747637476`, measured fold 1 and refused: the forecast said 13,479 calls against a 12,000 cap,
because the cap had been set from R64's *bill* rather than from a cold-cache forecast. The refusal
cost a fold and no result, which is the mechanism working.

### 173.9 The value block fires on three empty retries in four and moves three questions

Dispatch `42750334097`, `dev`, n = 1,534, 5 folds, **5,594 calls, $0.7078**, cache 73.5%, `V76`
passed, every other gate green, 0 call failures.

| arm | accuracy | vs `none` | gained / lost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | 56.71% | — | — |
| `full` | 56.58% | −0.13pp [−1.83, +1.56], p = 0.94 | 82 / 84 |
| `retry-blank` | 58.08% | +1.37pp [+0.85, +1.96], p = 9.5e-07 | 21 / 0 |
| `retry-values` | 58.28% | +1.56pp [+0.98, +2.22], p = 1.2e-07 | 24 / 0 |

**The mechanism works; the mechanism is nearly worthless; those are different claims.** The block
reached 69 of the 91 empty retries (**75.82%**, against a predicted floor of 60%), which is what
confirms the literal matcher is reading the right columns and writing short, specific lines (112
lines, 141 characters mean, none dropped). It then converted **six questions `retry-blank` did not**
— and broke **three that `retry-blank` had repaired**. Net **+2.97pp on the retried population**,
exact McNemar p = **0.51**, and **+0.20pp** on the benchmark.

The `0 lost` column is why this needs spelling out. Every arm reports gained and lost **against
`none`**, and against `none` a retry cannot un-answer anything: both retry arms are strictly additive
by construction. Against its own control the block is 6 up and 3 down, and 69 questions received
evidence that changed nothing.

**Registered branch: narrowed.** A positive under +8pp leaves the value explanation "one contributor
among several" and means the composition's 35.96% share "overstates what is recoverable" — three
questions out of 1,534 is the size of that overstatement. The tempting re-description, *the block
fired on 76% of retries so the mechanism is confirmed*, is exactly what the registration forbade in
writing: firing is not converting.

**Two predictions held, one failed, one was mis-priced.** Fired share 75.8% (held); non-value
failures undamaged (held trivially — `error` 0/10 in *both* arms, where R64 repaired one of ten);
delta +0.20pp at the floor of the predicted +0.2…+1.1 band (held); repaired rate **23.76%** against a
predicted 25–40% (failed, and the predicted "+4 to +16 more repairs out of 98" was actually +3 of
101). The bill was +6.7% in calls but **1.6× in money**, and the artefact says why: the dispatch ran
at **03:34 UTC**, inside the 01:00–04:00 window that bills at exactly double. $0.235 bought nothing.

### 173.10 The width ladder, and a quote that cost two dispatches

R69 is dispatched as one run rather than two. Its five-draw arms ride **beside** its ten-draw arms —
one pass of ten draws contains the five-draw pool as its first five, so the width effect becomes a
paired difference inside a run instead of a comparison across two days, two caches and two endpoint
states. R69's temperature half became **R70**, because a registration header carries one temperature
and R69 wanted 0.7 and 1.0: a header that lies to one of two dispatches is worse than two files.

Three instruments moved to close the same shape at three different layers:

- **`temperature:` is a header key**, read by `eval:prereg-temperature`, refused outside `(0, 2]`, and
  refused on a registration that draws nothing. `SOTA_SAMPLE_TEMPERATURE` is a repository variable,
  and a variable is global: an experiment that moves it moves it for every queued dispatch. This is
  the third knob to leave the variable space, after the template and the model.
- **`config.sample_temperature` is in the artefact.** It was in the environment and in one stdout
  line and nowhere in the record, so R69 and R70 would have been indistinguishable from their numbers
  — the same gap `model_credential` closed one iteration earlier.
- **`armsAgainstRegistration`** makes the lane refuse an arm list that disagrees with the
  registration it claims to execute. Containment rather than equality: every declared arm must be
  bought, and a dispatch may buy more, because R66's header names `retry-values` while its dispatch
  buys `retry-blank,retry-values` — a treatment without its control is not a measurement.

Then both dispatches died in **one second**, on `Resolve the sampling temperature`, on an apostrophe
inside a parameter expansion (`AUDIT.md` § 35.08). No calls, no folds, two dispatch objects. The
checker is the fix: `scripts/check-workflows.py` now runs `bash -n` over every `run:` block in every
workflow — parse, not execute — and two self-test cases pin it.

Gate state: 3,868 tests over 187 files, four coverage dimensions at **100%**, `pnpm check` green.

### 173.11 Width buys two points, and the run published five arms of six

Dispatch `42796339905`, minidev, n = 350, 5 folds, **4,829 calls, $0.3967, `off_peak`**, 3,500
candidates signed and reconciled, 14 gates, every one green.

| arm | accuracy | vs `none` (52.00%) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `full` | 50.57% | −1.43pp |
| `sample-5-first` / `sample-10-first` | 51.71% | −0.29pp |
| `sample-5-exec` | 50.86% | −1.14pp |
| `sample-10-exec` | 50.57% | −1.43pp |
| `sample-5-oracle` | 61.14% | +9.14pp |
| `sample-10-oracle` | **absent** | — |

**The published ceiling row is the ten-draw ceiling under a five-draw name, and the ten-draw arm was
never built.** The lane looked for *the* oracle arm, kept the first in union order, and read the pool
whole. Every gate passed anyway: a gate checks whether a measurement is valid, and the missing rung
was never measured. Recovered from the pool at zero cost — which is what the pool is for:

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| `first` (same draw at both widths) | 51.71% |
| `ceiling(k=5)`, best of the first five | 59.14% |
| `ceiling(k=10)`, best of all ten | 61.14% |
| **width effect, paired within the run** | **+2.00pp** |
| majority, k = 5 / k = 10 | 51.71% / 52.29% |

**Branch: width saturates** (delta within the registered 3pp band). Five draws already contain what
this model produces at this prompt; ten buy two points of ceiling and nothing at the selector —
